title: Bind retirement obligation checker to the canonical workspace pile format
description: The F10 retirement checker landed after the workspace-binding worktree branched and still decoded piles through the removed ambient-workspace API. Its fixtures also constructed ws-less ordinary facts. This made the two independently green branches fail when combined on main and, if merely shimmed, could classify rejection under the wrong workspace.
design: Pass the authenticated trace workspace into every immutable pile decode, construct hostile ordinary facts/piles with that workspace, and keep the static destructive-call inventory aligned with the running source.
acceptance_criteria: The retirement obligation, peer capability, workspace binding, and repository-layout suites pass together on main; typed rejection classification uses the same expected-workspace decoder as production.
notes: Fixed in 8cfe94a. Combined focused integration suite: 40 passed.
close_reason: Fixed in 8cfe94a; combined retirement/workspace suite passes.

title: Keep every restorable candidate durably reachable after pile retirement
description: A cold DB-free publisher cannot reproduce Catalog settlement from the committed root. RangeTree and FactTree contain only current proofs, while WorkspaceRuntime retires a valid closed pile after the root covers only the subset classified publishable; losing/inactive receipts then survive solely in one client's SQLite facts table. A later authority-rank or suppression change can restore such a receipt (the existing late device-rank tests prove this), but a cold worker has neither its canonical bytes nor an authenticated route to it. Evolving FactTree postings cannot recover bytes that are no longer rooted or retained as durable intent.
design: Choose one family-neutral durable retention law before claiming store-only settlement: either keep exact closed-pile intent live while any valid durable candidate may be restored, or publish a content-addressed candidate archive reachable from the root without duplicating raw fact bytes. If a currently rooted fact is deactivated, publication must preserve/recreate its exact restorable closure before the CAS that removes it. Do not make SQLite, object-store LIST of orphaned hashes, or provider event delivery authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: A cold process given only the bucket reconstructs the same candidate set and later restoration as Catalog across losing offers, rank rewires, suppression activation/clear, and restart after every object/root/retirement boundary. Retirement proof rejects deleting the last durable copy of any restorable candidate. No raw fact body is duplicated and no family-specific candidate registry is introduced.
notes: Evaluated smallest one-tree option: keep eligible FactRecord location as its reconciliation key (bounded RangeTree lookup), but when standing is lost emit encode(fact) once as a content-addressed object and put blob_oid on the dormant fid record; activation removes blob_oid. This avoids updating every fid when a leaf splits and exposes one root-reachable body copy. Completeness additionally requires generic postings for dormant candidates with rank/state plus declared-need routes, repair importing dormant rows from FactTree, sync reconciling dormant candidates outside RangeTree, and the F10 retirement witness accepting either eligible RangeTree residency or the exact dormant blob. It is coherent but deliberately remains this bead because it changes .17.8's current 'raw facts remain in manifest piles' design law.

title: Prevent broker-parent mutation from erasing acknowledged ingress
description: A dedicated ingress bucket protects canonical integrity, but today's broad R2 parent token can still DELETE an acknowledged staged object or pile. That destroys the only durable work item before publication and violates the ingress retirement obligation under broker-parent compromise.
design: Decide the explicit availability threat boundary. If broker-parent compromise is in scope, obtain a provider primitive or upload gateway whose broker parent can create but cannot delete acknowledged ingress, or move acknowledgement behind a separate verifier-controlled durable boundary. Bucket lifecycle may collect abandoned sessions but must not impersonate witnessed retirement.
acceptance_criteria: Generated policy and adversarial tests distinguish canonical isolation from ingress availability. Compromising the broker parent cannot delete an acknowledged pile/object before an authenticated publication/rejection witness, or DESIGN explicitly accepts and bounds this availability-loss boundary with user-visible acknowledgement semantics.
notes:
The direct-upload method now separates the two claims: a broad ingress parent passes canonical isolation but fails exercise_ingress_retirement_boundary because it can DELETE acknowledged stage object/pile keys; an abstract PUT-only parent passes. No claim is made that current R2 can issue the latter. Resolve this bead before treating broker-parent compromise as F10-safe.
Provider-doc check 2026-07-29: temporary child credentials can name actions=[PutObject], but the broker parent Object Read & Write token remains the broad authority under test. README/DESIGN now distinguish canonical integrity from acknowledged-ingress availability and keep the latter decision open.
The .17.10.1 running history found the exact-value retirement precondition: provider DELETE has no compare-by-value guard, so get/exact-DELETE/read-back is safe only while every accepted same-address write is create-only and body-bound. The model's broker-parent overwrite control is retained and refuses retirement; resolve this bead for both overwrite and DELETE authority, not DELETE alone.
Executable negative schedule: test_parent_replacement_between_exact_get_and_delete_is_rejected pauses retire_exact after its exact GET, uses the broad broker-parent PUT to replace the acknowledged value, then resumes unconditional DELETE. The helper necessarily removes the replacement because providers expose no delete-if-value; check_stage_cleanup rejects the first overwrite with a deterministic replay prefix. This is why .17.9.1 must remove/accept that parent authority rather than treating read-back as atomic conditional deletion.

title: Validate invite bootstrap before mutating local workspace state
description: Invite redemption decoded a second raw fact-list format, selected the last invitation by tag, and called add_workspace before proving that the outer link workspace, encrypted blob workspace, closed bootstrap workspace, genesis anchor, and every bootstrap fact agreed or that the complete bootstrap passed the kernel. A hostile or truncated invite could therefore mutate node-local keyring/workspace state before authoritative validation.
design: Carry the canonical base64 pile codec inside the encrypted invite. Require link W == blob W == pile W; run the database-free kernel over the complete bootstrap and require exactly one valid invitation before constructing the member or calling add_workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Foreign-inner-pile and incomplete-proof invite vectors both fail before node.workspaces or keyring bytes change; a valid invite still joins through the ordinary pile path.
notes: Implemented canonical encrypted invite piles and validated link W == blob W == pile W. core.kernel.drain must accept the complete bootstrap and yield exactly one valid user_invite before member construction or Node.add_workspace. Regression vectors cover foreign inner W and incomplete proof with byte-identical keyring/workspace state before and after. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Fixed and covered by invite-before-keyring adversarial tests.

title: Reject foreign receipts during catalog reopen and reindex
description: Catalog.stage is not the only receipt door. Existing canonical blobs are replayed by schema upgrade, explicit reindex, and Node reopen/rebuild. Without an expected anchor on those paths, a foreign receipt already on disk can regenerate generic routes and reach eligibility/publication under the wrong workspace.
design: Make upgrade_schema and _reindex require the workspace anchor and reject every blob not canonically bound to it. Node.idx supplies the path/keyring workspace; Catalog.reindex uses Catalog.anchor. Keep the kernel and catalog agreement exact.
acceptance_criteria: Direct staging, explicit reindex, legacy relational upgrade, and realistic Node reopen reject foreign or ws-less ordinary receipts without publishing them; bound legacy relational receipts still migrate.
notes: Implemented anchor-required Catalog.stage, explicit reindex, legacy-schema replay, Node.idx upgrade/reopen, and root rebuild paths. Foreign canonical blobs and ws-less ordinary legacy receipts fail closed; bound legacy relational receipts still migrate. Realistic reopen/reindex negatives and full suite pass (576 passed, 2 skipped).
close_reason: Fixed and covered by stage/reindex/legacy-upgrade/reopen anchor tests.

title: Choose uniform ingress staging versus provider-native canonical PUTs
description: AWS can bind SHA-256 and create-only semantics on a presigned canonical object PUT. R2 currently has both a payload-binding question and a broad parent-token boundary, making a separate untrusted ingress bucket attractive. We must choose whether physical provider differences remain behind one logical upload interface or whether both providers use the same session-scoped staging-and-promotion protocol.
design: Prefer uniform staging if it fits measured serverless budgets. The broker chooses exact session/member/workspace staging keys; clients upload all objects first and a closed pile intent last; publishers stream with hard bounds, verify SHA-256 and pile semantics, conditionally promote canonical obj values, CAS root, and retire staging under F10. This keeps untrusted bytes and abandoned sessions out of the canonical namespace and makes AWS/R2 failure behavior isomorphic. Compare against AWS direct canonical PUT with provider-checked SHA-256 and R2 staging. Do not choose from nominal provider limits: measure real Bao proof sizes, maximum legal piles, requests, memory, duration, storage operations, and failure recovery.
acceptance_criteria: A provider-neutral trace and focused benchmark run realistic messages plus small, median, and maximum supported attachments through both alternatives on local Lambda/Worker artifacts and opt-in live S3/R2. Results include bytes read/written, requests, peak memory, turn duration, cost-driving operations, abandoned-session cleanup, duplicate content, crash at validate/promote/root/delete, and poison-key behavior. The chosen protocol has one client state machine and one publisher obligation law; any provider-specific physical adapter is isolated under deploy/adapters. DESIGN records the measured reason and direct-to-object-store property.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model runs one logical staging/promotion/F10 state machine under both S3 and R2 labels, including poison plus crashes after validation, canonical promotion, and root publication. It intentionally does not choose uniform staging versus AWS-native canonical PUT; physical adapters and measured deployment limits remain this decision bead's work.
The provider-neutral abstract corpus now covers 12 cases: clean; crash after validate/promote/root/pile-delete/object-delete; poisoned staging bytes; foreign workspace/member; missing member authorization; missing object; and preexisting canonical collision. Exact bucket/key/declared-digest binding is checked for every state transition. Real competing root CAS and ambiguous delete results remain child .17.10.1.

title: Isolate the R2 upload broker from the canonical workspace bucket
description: Cloudflare now supports locally signed temporary R2 credentials restricted to exact object paths and explicit PutObject actions, which is suitable for clients. But the parent R2 API token held by the broker is scoped only at bucket permission granularity: Object Read and Write includes read, write, and list. If that parent token targets the canonical workspace bucket, a compromised broker can bypass its intended role and mutate or enumerate root/obj/pile despite returning narrow child credentials.
design: Keep the client direct-to-R2 path but enforce the broker boundary with provider resources, not code convention. Prefer a dedicated untrusted ingress bucket: the broker parent token is scoped only to that bucket and locally signs short-lived PutObject-only temporary credentials for exact staging objects; it has no binding or token for the canonical workspace bucket. The database-free publisher alone reads and retires ingress, verifies SHA-256/workspace/member/pile closure, promotes immutable objects into the canonical bucket, and CASes canonical root. Compare this with any newer R2 primitive that can make a parent credential write-only and path-scoped; require live evidence before using one bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Generated Cloudflare policy/config and adversarial tests prove that the broker parent credential itself, not merely a returned child credential, cannot read/list/delete or address any canonical workspace key. Exact child credentials cannot change action, bucket, path, body contract, or expiry. Publisher crash during staged-object verification/promotion/root CAS retains a recoverable obligation; abandoned staging expires only under a bounded ingress-bucket lifecycle and never deletes canonical data. One-command deploy/remove owns both bindings and preserves both buckets.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model now attacks the broker parent itself with canonical root GET/PUT, workspace LIST, object/pile PUT, and object DELETE. A dedicated ingress-bucket parent passes for both provider labels; the one-bucket broad parent is a seeded first-failure negative control. Staging poison and validate/promote/root crash histories preserve F10. This remains a design oracle, not generated Cloudflare policy or live evidence.
Promotion traces now serialize and parse a symbolic staged intent carrying workspace, member, declared object digests, and member authorization; exact candidates retain foreign/unauthorized/missing/poisoned work and the oracle rejects any promotion outside that closure. Production decode_pile and mint.stateless are explicit refinement seams. The newly discovered ingress DELETE availability gap is tracked by child bug .17.9.1.

title: Publish the generic candidate index needed for DB-free settlement
description: The running root cannot support bounded serverless settlement. AuthorityTree stores only the current winner, while FactTree is addressed by fid and the RangeTree is ordered by reconciliation key. When a new pile offers an existing authority address or suppression deactivates a winner, a database-free publisher must find every remaining eligible candidate and its proof/key without SQLite; today its only complete option is a corpus-wide manifest scan.
design: Do not add another ad hoc tree. Evolve FactTree into the authenticated counterpart of the client generic fact_index: one mechanical keyspace covers fid-to-record/key, reconciliation key, type, each explicit role/target reference, and every declared offer/candidate with deterministic proof rank and fid ordering. Raw fact bytes remain once in manifest piles; a fid row supplies the fact key needed to locate its home range. Keep SuppTree for explicit suppression state and AuthorityTree only if its winner cache still materially bounds ordinary reads; otherwise derive or merge it when that actually reduces code and fetches. Path-copy only rows affected by the eligibility delta, and bump the layout cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: A cold database-free publisher handles a new unique offer, a losing offer, a new canonical winner, winner suppression with fallback, reference/type query, and unrelated fact without enumerating FactTree or RangeTree and without SQLite. Fetch counts are bounded by tree depth plus returned candidates. Differential tests against the client catalog produce identical candidates, proofs, authority winners, suppression transitions, and roots over seeded histories. The change does not duplicate raw fact blobs, introduce a range directory, or add a family-specific registry/tree.

title: Prove collision-resistant body binding for direct R2 PUTs
description: A direct uploader is untrusted but obj and pile keys are SHA-256 addresses. Exact-key permission plus If-None-Match prevents overwrite yet does not prove that the uploaded body hashes to the granted key; a malicious member can win creation of a not-yet-present legitimate oid with different bytes and permanently wedge immutable publication. AWS presigned PutObject supports a provider-checked SHA-256 checksum. Cloudflare currently documents R2 PutObject conditionals and Content-MD5, while its presigned examples use unsigned payloads; MD5 is not an acceptable substitute for the content-address invariant.
design: First test whether an R2 S3 SigV4 presigned PUT can bind and enforce the exact SHA-256 payload digest, create-only header, and exact content length even though the compatibility table does not advertise flexible checksum fields. Inspect the actual signed-header/query set and run opt-in live positive and body/header substitution cases. If R2 enforces the collision-resistant binding, ratchet the exact presigner form and SDK versions. If not, do not issue raw R2 PUT URLs: use a narrowly isolated upload-only Worker or another provider primitive that streams with a byte ceiling, computes SHA-256, and conditionally stores only the matching key. It still receives no root/list/delete authority.
acceptance_criteria: A replayable fake and opt-in live R2 test show that changing one body byte, body length, digest/key, create-only condition, or any signed header cannot create or replace the target, while an exact request succeeds and an equal replay is safely classified. The test examines bytes at the target after every result including timeout. The chosen path has a documented hard request ceiling and cannot occupy an immutable key with nonmatching bytes. README and deployment policy distinguish raw direct PUT from the upload-verifier fallback.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model now ratchets the provider-independent oracle: an exact-key same-length wrong body must be rejected without occupying the oid; MD5 and unsigned profiles are explicit failing controls; an applied-but-lost exact write must retry as equal. The signed body-SHA condition is deliberately symbolic and is not live R2 evidence. This bead remains open for adapter refinement and opt-in live proof.
The final abstract oracle separates provider response from privileged state observation: raw create-only replay is a generic precondition failure, while only an upload verifier may classify equal replay. Same-length byte mutation, zero-length binding-algorithm mutation, wrong-byte incumbent preservation, and MD5/unsigned planted profiles are ratcheted. Live provider proof remains open.
Provider-doc check 2026-07-29: R2 Workers API R2PutOptions accepts one supplied sha256 checksum plus onlyIf conditional, so a streaming upload-only Worker is a concrete collision-resistant verifier fallback. The S3 compatibility table still advertises PutObject conditionals and Content-MD5 but not flexible SHA-256 checksums; this is not evidence for raw presigned canonical PUT.

title: Method: mutate direct-upload capabilities and notification histories
description: Reusable problem-finding method for direct bucket ingress. Generate one valid exact upload request and systematically mutate each authority-bearing dimension: provider, endpoint, operation, bucket, workspace, member, object class, key, digest, size, content type, signed headers, expiry, condition, and body. Separately generate histories that lose, duplicate, reorder, and replay notifications, responses, and retries while tracking the durable pile obligation.
design: The oracle is capability attenuation plus the publication invariant, not provider success text. A mutation must either be rejected without changing protected keys or produce the one exact authorized immutable value. Every acknowledged pile creates an F10 obligation; a notification never does. Run the same corpus against the in-memory verifier, S3 SDK/presigner, R2 S3 presigner, local wiring environments, and opt-in live providers, recording semantic gaps as concrete defect beads.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded corpus with shrinking finds intentionally planted weak policies such as unsigned conditional headers, prefix rather than exact-key grants, body/checksum substitution, workspace/member swapping, URL replay after expiry, overwrite on replay, event-as-work, and notification loss without scan recovery. CI is credential-free and deterministic; live runs are opt-in and prefix-safe. Every novel provider or implementation gap emits a replay fixture and a linked defect bead.
notes:
Credential-free design corpus implemented in tests/direct_upload_method.py with focused tests. It reuses ConformanceRun only for deterministic seeds/history and Obligation for F10 vocabulary; diagnostics explicitly call this a contract model, not provider evidence. The body-SHA condition is symbolic pending live adapter refinement. Cases cover exact capability dimensions, create/collision/outcome-unknown retry, notification faults and fair scans, broker-parent compromise, provider-neutral staging/promotion crash boundaries, budgets, first-failure prefixes, and concrete integration seams.
Adversarial re-review found and fixed additional oracle escapes: cold retries previously retained process-local root state; abstract events were mislabeled as F10 evidence; extra signed constraints were rejected; raw PUT replay assumed privileged readback; typed staged authority/closure and canonical collision/delete crashes were absent; and promotion/root/delete events were not exact-bucket/key bound. Planted negatives now catch cache-only roots, foreign workspace/member/unauthorized intents, poisoned bytes, canonical overwrite, wrong-bucket state transitions, undeclared cross-workspace promotion, and unknown operations. Broader mint-vs-wire, shrinking, and real CAS ambiguity are tracked in .17.6.3, .17.6.4, and .17.10.1.
close_reason: Credential-free seeded direct-upload method implemented and adversarially reviewed: exact attenuation, abstract retirement ordering, notification recovery, broker-parent boundaries, typed staging/promotion, crash erasure, budgets, replay traces, integration seams, and planted weak controls. Remaining runtime/provider refinements are explicit linked beads.

title: Deploy separate upload brokers and publishers on AWS and Cloudflare
description: Extend the segregated deploy/aws_lambda and deploy/cloudflare_worker packages with provider-native upload brokers, pile consumers, schedules, queues, policies, CORS, alarms, and safe removal. Keep gateway, broker, and publisher roles independently deployable and least-privileged; do not put provider boilerplate or branches in core.
design: Implement the provider-neutral protocol selected by poc-16-x1p.17.10 behind segregated packages. AWS uses a narrow authorization endpoint, S3 pile-created notifications to Lambda, and EventBridge scheduled fallback; IAM makes presigner/broker, reader, and publisher separate principals. Cloudflare uses a narrow Worker broker, exact R2 child capabilities, R2 event notifications through Queues, and Cron fallback. If R2 parent credentials remain bucket-broad, broker and client capabilities target a dedicated ingress bucket and only the publisher can verify/promote into the canonical workspace bucket. Publisher identities alone may read/drain ingress, conditionally create canonical immutable pages, CAS root, and perform F10-governed retirement. Generated deployment identity, workspace, canonical bucket/prefix, ingress bucket/prefix, and queue/schedule ownership are pinned for update/remove.
acceptance_criteria: One-command test/package/deploy/update/smoke/remove flows exist for both providers. Generated IAM/R2 policies prove clients cannot list, delete, overwrite canonical immutable values, cross workspace/member/session scopes, or touch root; the broker parent credential itself cannot address the canonical bucket; reader cannot upload; publisher cannot alter provider policy. Live smoke uploads a realistic attachment directly, observes verified publication after event and after deliberately dropped event via schedule, reads it through the gateway, and removes compute/queues without deleting canonical or ingress bucket data. Staged test objects are cleaned only under an exact generated test session.

title: Wake publishers without making notification delivery authoritative
description: Connect S3 object-created notifications and R2 event notifications to the database-free publisher, add an authenticated low-latency poke, and retain a bounded scheduled pile scan as the progress path. Events and pokes are hints; only the durable pile object establishes work.
design: Filter notifications to the pile prefix and deduplicate only as an optimization. A handler may receive duplicates, stale events, reordered events, or no event. It validates the named key against the same listing/drain path, performs bounded fair work, and schedules continuation when the turn budget ends. Scheduled scans use provider pagination correctly and eventually revisit every durable pile despite insertions. No notification handler may delete or claim a pile by ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded tests drop, duplicate, delay, and reorder notifications; deliver object events before pile events; lose poke responses; insert keys between list pages; throttle turns; and run concurrent scheduled and event consumers. Every valid durable pile eventually publishes under fair provider recovery, poison piles cannot wedge later work, no hint creates work absent a pile, and F10 rejects every unsupported deletion. Opt-in live AWS and R2 tests prove notification wiring under generated prefixes.

title: Teach clients objects-first, pile-last direct upload
description: Replace the daemon-proxy upload coordinator with a provider-neutral client flow. The client asks the broker for exact capabilities, conditionally uploads every required immutable object, verifies every response or reconciles an unknown outcome, and only then uploads the canonical closed pile as the durable publication intent. The client never receives a prefix credential or root authority.
design: Keep provider signing and HTTP details behind one narrow upload-capability interface. Reuse the same canonical object identifiers and closed-pile codec as local and peer publication. Missing-object negotiation and bounded batching may optimize the object phase but cannot allow the pile to overtake a required object. Treat exact equal replays as success, hash collisions as fatal, and an unknown object PUT outcome as a read/retry problem rather than permission to overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: A real client command uploads messages plus a multi-chunk attachment through fake S3 and fake R2 without a writable daemon. Tests cover zero objects, thousands of objects, partial success, timeout after apply, timeout before apply, equal replay, collision, resume after restart, and pile capability minted only for the authenticated workspace/member. Request and memory bounds are explicit and the existing peer path remains compatible.

title: Build the database-free pile publisher
description: Implement the store-only publication engine used by Lambda and Cloudflare consumers. From a pinned root and one or more durable pile intents, validate canonical workspace/uploader/closure, verify referenced immutable objects, derive the authenticated-tree and RangeTree changes without SQLite, write immutable pages conditionally, and CAS the composite root.
design: Use the same family kernel and authenticated-tree codecs as clients. Treat the object store as source of truth and keep bounded in-memory state per turn. Batch a serial union of eligible intents, reconcile opaque-token CAS loss, reload/reapply after STALE, respect the R2 root hot-key cadence, and use the F10 obligation checker before any pile delete.
acceptance_criteria: Differential tests compare store-only and client publishers over every family and suppression transition. Two or more cold workers with delayed views, disjoint/overlapping piles, 429, missing objects, malformed facts, crash at every object/root/delete boundary, and lost responses converge to the from-scratch canonical root with no SQLite import, lost intent, split tree, or unsafe deletion.

title: Issue exact conditional S3/R2 upload capabilities
description: Add a database-free upload broker that validates a workspace upload proof and returns short-lived presigned PUT capabilities for exact immutable object keys and one exact pile key. The broker, not the client, chooses workspace prefix and authenticated member segment.
design: Sign operation, provider endpoint, bucket, exact key, collision-resistant body digest, exact length or hard provider byte ceiling, expiry, content type, and If-None-Match star. Prefer exact per-key bearer requests over broad temporary credentials. Raw direct PUT is conforming only when the provider verifies that the body SHA-256 equals the content-addressed key; Content-MD5 is insufficient. Where R2 cannot prove that property, issue a capability for a narrow upload-only verifier that streams under a hard ceiling, computes SHA-256, and conditionally creates the matching key. Separate roles: broker may attenuate upload authority but cannot root-CAS; uploader can use only returned requests; publisher can read intents/objects and CAS root but cannot alter policy.
acceptance_criteria: Fake and opt-in live S3/R2 tests upload N and N+1 bytes, substitute one body byte, wrong collision-resistant digest, missing/surplus signed headers, expired/replayed URLs, existing equal/colliding keys, wrong workspace/member/key, and attempted LIST/DELETE/root access. The provider or upload verifier must never occupy an immutable key with nonmatching bytes. Equal replays are idempotent; every other mutation fails without clobbering data. Browser CORS, exact request ceilings, multipart limits, and the R2 raw-PUT versus verifier decision are explicit.
notes: Broker implementation requirement refined by x1p.17.6.3: before deriving any object-store key, independently validate the pinned workspace as valid_fid and the authenticated member segment as exactly 16 lowercase hex. Equality between proof claims and descriptor is not path-shape validation; reject slash, uppercase, short/long, Unicode, and other noncanonical segments before signing.

title: Direct-to-bucket uploads with DB-free serverless publication
description: Replace the writable-daemon requirement for cloud workspaces with a two-stage design. Authorized clients receive exact, short-lived S3/R2 upload capabilities for immutable objects and one content-addressed pile intent. Clients never receive root permission. A database-free Lambda/Worker publisher consumes durable pile intents, validates the workspace/uploader/closure and referenced objects, updates authenticated trees, and conditionally advances root. Object-created events or an authenticated poke reduce latency; strong LIST plus scheduled draining preserves eventual progress.
design: Uploads are objects-first and pile-last. Exact-key signed PUTs require checksum, size ceiling, expiry, and If-None-Match star; the broker chooses the workspace/member prefix. The pile is a durable at-least-once work item, not a lock. Missing referenced objects and provider failures retain it. Multiple publishers share one bucket and use opaque-token root CAS; F10 retirement proof governs deletion. Separate presigner, uploader, publisher, and reader capabilities so no client can list, delete, or write root.
acceptance_criteria: From a credential-free client, upload a realistic attachment and facts directly to both fake S3 and fake R2 using granted exact-key capabilities, then wake two cold database-free publishers. Exactly one root CAS linearizes at a time, both workers converge, the file is readable, and the pile retires only with a valid witness. Lost poke/event, pile-before-object, duplicate/replayed URL, expired URL, checksum mismatch, wrong member/workspace, 429, crash, and restart are safe. Opt-in live S3/R2 tests and one-command deploy/remove flows cover the complete path.

title: Method: re-close valid facts under a second workspace authority graph
description: Reusable cross-tenant confusion probe: create two workspaces sharing one user/device signing key, author a valid ordinary fact in W1, then replace only its surrounding closure with W2's valid membership/authority facts. Also build a pile that declares W2 but contains one W1 fact and a request whose uploader token is for W1 while the URL/path names W2. This distinguishes cryptographic fact binding from ambient-context validation.
acceptance_criteria: The probe covers every fact family, detached author evidence, suppression actions, file descriptors/chunks, invite redemption, mint request piles, sync, and direct ingress. It fails if any byte-identical ordinary fact is accepted in both workspaces or if request, uploader, pile, and fact workspace can disagree. Every exposed family gets a concrete defect bead and regression vector.
notes:
Reusable construction ratchet added: parse every facts/**/*.py Fact(...) call and fail if it omits the fifth workspace argument, passes literal None outside the unique workspace genesis family, or if the compiled registry has anything other than exactly one GENESIS family. This turns the audit method into a permanent family-addition tripwire rather than a one-time grep.
Completed vectors: same signing key and same fact form across W1/W2 produce distinct fact/signature ids; foreign outer pile, mixed/re-closed facts, W1 grant at W2 route, uploader/path mismatch, CF Worker/Gateway/Lambda mint, invite bootstrap, catalog stage/reindex/reopen, sync push, suppression evidence, files/chunks, and no-dual-decoder format cutover. Hostile mixed bytes are rejected before any family dispatch or Catalog.stage call. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Reusable cross-workspace re-close probe and construction ratchet implemented across all families and runtimes.

title: F10 follow-up: run obligation checker through F2 seeds and provider adapters
description: The F10 branch supplies the small replayable obligation checker and deterministic real-Node schedules over ScriptedBucket/AdversarialBucket. Complete the remaining reuse promise by wiring that same checker (not a parallel oracle) into F2's bounded seeded 2-6 writer histories and the S3/R2 conformance adapter traces. Normalize provider events to the existing acknowledged create/root CAS/exact read/delete vocabulary, preserving opaque tokens and paginated LIST.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed F2 CI seeds and at least one deterministic S3 and R2 adapter-conformance schedule emit checker-compatible histories. Every pile DELETE is checked against current authenticated publication or semantically reclassified exact rejection evidence; failures report the first unsupported DELETE and seed/provider trace. Long soak remains optional.

title: Bind every fact and closed pile to one workspace
description: Fact envelopes currently contain type, timestamp, atoms, and body hash but no workspace anchor. The daemon authenticates an uploader for ambient ws and drain(stream, ws) rejects a foreign genesis root, yet an ordinary fact authored by a key that belongs to two workspaces can be re-closed under the second workspace's member/authority chain because its fid and author signature are identical. The engine therefore cannot prove the invariant that every fact in an uploaded closed pile belongs to the request workspace.
design: Make workspace identity canonical before family dispatch. The workspace genesis fact is the sole exception: it has no ws field and its fid defines W. Every other fact carries ws=W in bytes covered by its fid and signatures. The closed-pile envelope also names W. The ingress door checks request workspace equals authenticated uploader workspace equals pile workspace and checks every ordinary fact workspace before staging. Bump the format cleanly rather than retain an ambiguous dual decoder.
acceptance_criteria: Create two workspaces sharing one signing key. Equivalent ordinary facts have different fids, a W1 fact re-closed with W2 authority is rejected, a W1 pile uploaded under W2 is rejected before staging, and a mixed-workspace pile is rejected even if every individual signature is valid. The sole workspace-genesis exception has no ws field and is accepted only when genesis.fid equals the expected anchor. The authenticated uploader/path member must be eligible in the same W. Invite redemption, sync, files, suppression actions, database-free mint, rebuild, and versioning hydration use the same rule; realistic full tests and cross-runtime vectors pass.
notes: Implemented clean workspace-bound fact/pile format. Genesis is the registry's unique ws-less fact and genesis.fid defines W; every ordinary fact and signature includes ws=W in hashed bytes; every pile carries W. Expected W is mandatory at decode across ingress, leaves, sync, mint, invite, suppression evidence, and rebuild. Layout v6 and catalog v26 force clean rebuild; prior ambient facts/piles/catalogs have no dual decoder. Added deploy vectors, hostile before-dispatch/stage tests, construction source ratchet, docs, and benchmarks. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped in 140.14s.
close_reason: Workspace-bound fact/pile format, all trust paths, clean format stamps, docs, and full regression suite complete.

title: F10 defect: aliased delete reference evades production-site inventory
description: The initial production deletion inventory visited only Call(Attribute(..., attr='delete')). Refactoring to deleter = st.delete; deleter(source) leaves the destructive capability in production but silently disappears from the claimed exhaustive ratchet. Inventory every delete attribute reference, distinguish direct calls from aliases, flag dynamic getattr(..., 'delete'), and require the sole reference to remain the reviewed direct retirement call.
acceptance_criteria: An alias mutation fixture is reported as a delete capability reference even though the later call target is a Name. Production has exactly one direct delete reference in Node._retire_ingress_exact; dynamic delete getattr references are also surfaced.
notes: Fixed before handoff: production_call_sites inventories every matching Attribute reference and literal getattr, classifies direct vs alias, and its mutation fixture catches both store.delete aliasing and getattr(store, 'delete').
close_reason: Delete capability references, aliases, and literal getattr are inventoried; production remains one reviewed direct site.

title: F10 defect: forged rejection type name satisfies destructive witness
description: The first obligation checker authenticated failed/meta bytes and schema but trusted the error string's PermanentIngressRejection subclass prefix as the classification proof. A writer can forge exact/hash-bound InvalidPile metadata for a valid pile, or KernelRejected metadata for bytes whose family handler raises a program exception. Durable syntax is not a demonstrably input-local verdict. Reclassify the exact bytes deterministically through decode_pile + drain and require the recorded type to agree; program failures and valid piles must fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Forged InvalidPile metadata over a valid pile and forged KernelRejected metadata during a family/program exception both fail at the DELETE. Real exact InvalidPile and KernelRejected production paths pass. itm.8 remains open for bounded/authenticated status presentation.
notes: Fixed before handoff: exact rejection bytes are deterministically re-run through decode_pile + drain and metadata type must agree. Valid-pile/InvalidPile and family-program-failure/KernelRejected forgeries are negative controls; real InvalidPile and KernelRejected pass. poc-16-itm.8 remains open for status presentation budgets/authentication.
close_reason: Rejection witness now requires deterministic exact-byte classification agreement; both forged semantic substitutions reject.

title: F10: bind publication proof to the root current at classification
description: The first ghost-obligation checker draft searched every historical committed root for publishable fact ids. That is unsound: an obsolete good snapshot could mask the current authoritative root being malformed or no longer representing those facts. A publication retirement witness must validate the latest applied root at or before the runtime's post-settlement classification event; historical roots are diagnostic history, not current authority.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation schedule publishes a formerly valid then malformed/excluding current root and proves the checker rejects a DELETE even though an older root contains the claimed fids. Positive winner, CAS-loser identical-root reconciliation, and lost-response reconciliation still pass.
notes: Fixed before handoff: publication proof now selects the latest applied root at each post-settlement observation, never an arbitrary historical root. A malformed-current-root mutation with an older good root is rejected.
close_reason: Current-root binding implemented with obsolete-root mutation control.

title: Method: test revocation across DAG and provider control planes
description: Reusable problem-finding method: every infrastructure removal test must exercise both planes. First prove the operations DAG no longer authorizes the service; then use the service's previously valid raw provider credential, endpoint token, and grant material directly against the bucket/runtime. If any old path still reads, mints, mutates policy, or serves the removed workspace, the removal is incomplete even when all in-band queries deny it.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable matrix runs voluntary leave, authorized removal, provider outage during reconciliation, lost teardown response, credential-cache delay, KMS/policy administrator interference, and rejoin under fresh identity. It reports which plane remains live and creates a concrete defect bead for every surviving stale path. The method is used by fake AWS/R2 tests and opt-in live conformance.

title: Reconcile infrastructure DAG state into provider capabilities
description: Build an idempotent controller that reads active infrastructure bindings from the operations workspace and realizes them as isolated AWS Lambda/S3 or Cloudflare Worker/R2 deployments. It must also revoke provider credentials, rotate grant material where required, and remove the exact deployment binding after leave or removal.
design: The DAG is desired state; provider APIs are an effectful reconciliation layer with an explicit observed-state record. Use stable deployment identities and exact ownership checks already present in the provider managers. Never treat a successful fact commit as proof that IAM revocation or teardown happened; publish/observe a provider result separately and retry ambiguous outcomes safely.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded fake-provider tests cover create/update/no-op, crash at every provider boundary, ambiguous response reconciliation, concurrent reconcilers, voluntary leave, forced removal, credential and grant-secret rotation, and exact teardown without bucket-data deletion. Opt-in live tests prove a removed service's old credential cannot directly read the workspace and the remaining service continues.

title: Define infrastructure offer, acceptance, binding, leave, and removal facts
description: Implement the in-band half of infrastructure membership as a two-workspace fact-family handshake. The operations community admits and removes infrastructure principals. A target workspace invites one currently admitted principal with an exact service scope; the infrastructure principal accepts; the resulting binding is active only while both communities' supporting facts remain live. Voluntary leave and authorized removal on either side deactivate it under ordinary suppression/authority rules.
design: Start from existing member/device invite and shared-device-link patterns, but do not overload content membership. Facts must bind both workspace anchors, infrastructure principal, provider class, deployment identity, logical prefix, endpoint identity, and bounded capability set. Cross-workspace proof transport must remain explicit and replayable; core sees only generic dependencies, offers, suppression keys, and policy results.
acceptance_criteria: Simple fact handlers validate infrastructure-community admission, workspace invitation, node acceptance, wrong-community/workspace/provider/deployment rejection, duplicate/idempotent acceptance, voluntary leave, workspace admin removal, infrastructure-community removal, suppression propagation, and rejoin with a fresh binding. Database-backed and database-free contexts agree, and no accepted infrastructure fact confers content author/member authority.
notes: Core kernel contexts are intentionally single-workspace. Do not model the link as an ordinary hard dependency that resolves a foreign workspace fid. Each side records a locally authorized, anchor-bound half (or a signed portable offer/acceptance receipt); the infrastructure reconciler joins the two pinned DAG projections and requires both halves live.

title: Model infrastructure nodes as in-band service members
description: Infrastructure authority is in-band DAG state, not an implicit permanent provider role. One operations community governs infrastructure principals; a target workspace invites an exact active infrastructure principal, and that node accepts a workspace-scoped service link. Either side can end the link: the workspace removes it or the node leaves support. The protocol must bridge the resulting two-DAG desired state to the external AWS/R2 control plane: IAM credentials, bucket/prefix access, grant secrets, deployment lifecycle, and revocation are reconciled from those authenticated facts.
design: Separate three authorities: the infrastructure community decides which service nodes are live; each target workspace decides which live node it invites and what exact service scope it grants; the provider-account controller realizes or revokes the external capability. An active binding requires compatible, live facts from both DAGs plus the node's acceptance, like shared device linking across communities. The infrastructure role is distinct from human/content membership. Voluntary leave stops service; workspace removal or infrastructure-community removal also requires external credential revocation/rotation before the old operator is no longer trusted.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent implementations derive the same active service bindings from both pinned DAGs. An operations community can add an infrastructure node; a workspace can invite that exact node; it can accept one exact workspace scope, serve only the declared capability, leave voluntarily, or be removed from either side. Every removal drives tested IAM/secret/deployment revocation; stale credentials cannot read or mint afterward. Content membership is neither required nor accidentally granted, and another workspace/prefix remains inaccessible.

title: Make shared rejection reason records retry-idempotent
description: The content-addressed rejection record included now_ms(), so its key changed for every worker and every retry. A permanently invalid pile whose exact DELETE repeatedly fails could create an unbounded failed/meta/* object stream even though payload, source, and typed reason never changed; the two-worker race only asserted that at least one record existed.
acceptance_criteria: The shared record identity is a deterministic function of exact payload id, exact source key, and typed permanent reason, with no wall clock or worker identity. Concurrent workers and repeated pre-apply delete failures produce exactly one immutable metadata object for the same rejection obligation; optional observation time stays node-local.
notes: Removed wall-clock time from durable reason identity. The two-worker barrier race now requires exactly one shared record, and repeated delete-before-apply failures remain at one record.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Do not promote arbitrary codec ValueError to permanent rejection
description: decode_pile wrapped every ValueError raised anywhere inside decoding as InvalidPile. A programming ValueError from from_json or a helper would therefore become a typed permanent verdict and justify exact pile retirement, contradicting the rule that generic exception classes are not proof of bad input. Give immutable JSON/fact shape and integrity failures their own InvalidEncoding subtype and translate only that known input-local vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed JSON, pile shape, fact shape/integrity, blob shape/integrity, recursion, encoding, and size failures remain total ValueError-compatible codec failures and typed permanent pile rejections. An injected arbitrary ValueError from a fact-decoder program path escapes unchanged and runtime retains its exact pile with no rejection evidence.
notes: Implemented InvalidEncoding at the bounded JSON and fact shape/integrity doors; decode_pile translates only explicit input-local exception types. Added a direct negative-control regression.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Bound CPU from legally fragmented S3 response bodies
description: Contiguous accumulation fixes retained-object memory, but a legal or hostile stream can still return one byte per read. At the 64 MiB host ceiling that drives roughly 64 million Python calls before completion, creating a CPU denial of service.
acceptance_criteria: S3Config imposes a validated finite read-call budget with a conservative production default and hard maximum. Bounded reads fail closed and close the body when the budget is exhausted; exact/short/N+1 behavior below the budget remains correct; a one-byte-fragment probe proves calls never exceed the configured budget.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: contiguous reads now have a default 4,096-call budget and validated 65,536 hard maximum across S3 and R2-host configs; a 64 KiB one-byte stream fails closed after exactly 4,096 calls and closes. 128 focused tests pass.

title: Preserve family programming failures through ingress judgment
description: The generic resolve_edges() and accepts() helpers caught every family exception and returned ordinary invalidity. That erased the distinction between an immutable input-local rejection and a validator/needs programming failure, allowing runtime ingress to quarantine and retire exact input for a code bug. Add a strict streaming-judgment path that preserves unexpected exceptions for retry/status while existing projection/read callers remain fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic family needs/validator exception retains the exact pile, produces no failed/ quarantine evidence, does not publish its candidate, and does not wedge a healthy independent pile; ordinary invalid facts remain typed permanent rejections.
notes: Implemented strict exception preservation only for the streaming ingress judgment. Generic projection/read helpers retain their existing fail-closed behavior.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Preserve bounded R2 reads through the Worker read-only wrapper
description: Cloudflare ReadOnlyStore exposed get/has but hid R2BindingStore.get_bounded. Gateway therefore fell back to generic get, allowing route ceilings below the core adapter ceiling to allocate an oversized ArrayBuffer before rejection.
acceptance_criteria: ReadOnlyStore exposes only read capabilities including get_bounded, every gateway route passes its route-specific ceiling to R2, mutation methods remain unavailable, and request-level allocation-failing sentinels prove no oversized body allocation.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Avoid per-fragment object retention in bounded S3 reads
description: The bounded S3 reader retains every legal short fragment in a Python list until join. A provider/body returning one byte per read can therefore allocate millions of Python objects even though the byte ceiling is enforced.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded reads accumulate into contiguous bounded storage rather than retaining one object per fragment; ContentLength, N+1, early-EOF, exact-limit, and close semantics remain intact; a realistic one-byte-fragment body completes within the byte ceiling.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 1f9e645 is 408f72e on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 1f9e645: contiguous bounded accumulation plus a 64 KiB one-byte-fragment probe; 106 focused tests and the 496-test integrated suite pass.

title: Classify definitive ObjectStore rejection as permanent StoreError
description: F1 review found that the new adversarial harness mapped Fault.REJECTED to RetryableStoreError alongside throttling and explicitly retryable service rejection. A permission, policy, invalid-request, or configuration rejection known to occur before mutation is definitive but not necessarily retryable; collapsing it into the retry class can teach consumers to spin on permanent failure and makes the failure-taxonomy oracle unsound.
acceptance_criteria: Fault.REJECTED raises exact StoreError before any history event or mutation; THROTTLED and RETRYABLE_SERVICE raise exact RetryableStoreError; TRANSPORT on a mutation remains OutcomeUnknown; realistic tests assert exact types and unchanged data/history so subclasses cannot silently collapse categories.
close_reason: Corrected F1 fault taxonomy: permanent pre-mutation rejection is exact StoreError; throttle/service are exact RetryableStoreError; transport mutation remains OutcomeUnknown. Focused realistic gate: 76 passed.

title: Make rejection evidence immutable under shared-worker races
description: Host store_factory gives every worker the same workspace prefix, but Node describes failed/ as node-local and writes mutable failed/meta/<payload-hash> records containing timestamps. Two workers rejecting the same pile can overwrite one another's metadata while racing deletion. The exact payload is already content-addressed, so the proof surface should be deliberately shared and immutable; node-local retry/program presentation must remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: Exact rejected bytes use one shared immutable payload key; each typed-reason/source record uses a content-addressed immutable metadata key and is read back before retirement. Two independent Nodes over one shared store may reject the same pile concurrently/in either order without clobbering evidence, losing the ghost obligation, or retaining a false local-only claim. Status reads all immutable records deterministically while retryable/program attempt errors remain node-local.
notes:
Reusable probe: instantiate two Nodes with the same store_factory, barrier both after evidence persistence and before delete, and verify one idempotent retirement plus immutable records from both workers. Never infer node locality from a key prefix when the store factory itself is shared.
Implemented shared immutable evidence keys, exact readback, idempotent same-pile retirement, and concurrent real-Node coverage. Retry/program presentation remains node-local.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Protect authoritative S3 object ACL and tag metadata
description: The storage-law bucket guard denies deletion and unsafe PutObject but still permits PutObjectAcl, PutObjectTagging, and DeleteObjectTagging on authoritative root/object keys. These mutations can change access or governance metadata without changing bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The bucket guard denies authoritative ACL/tag mutation under both threat profiles, tests assert exact actions/resources/principal scope, and operator documentation requires auditing pre-existing ACLs/tags and recommends BucketOwnerEnforced ownership controls.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Reject fabricated R2 version tokens from malformed FFI results
description: R2BindingStore._token str()-coerces arbitrary etag values, so None aside an integer or object becomes a fabricated CAS token. Provider results must supply an actual strong string token; malformed result types must fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: R2 read_versioned and successful CAS accept real non-empty strong string ETags, reject None, integer, object, weak, and empty values without coercion, and size remains mandatory/type checked before arrayBuffer. Workerd FFI shape validation remains tracked separately.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Exercise native R2 result shapes through real workerd FFI
description: Host Python fakes model R2Object.size as int and etag as str, while the deployed Python Worker receives JavaScript binding values through Pyodide FFI. The current workerd smoke calls only /healthz and never proves a local R2 get exposes size, etag, arrayBuffer, head, conditional put, or list page/cursor in the Python shapes the adapter validates.
acceptance_criteria: A local workerd test seeds the actual R2 binding, then drives root/object reads plus conditional create/CAS/list through R2BindingStore and the request boundary. It records and validates Python-side types for size, etag, ArrayBuffer conversion, conditional-null results, objects, truncated, and cursor. Oversized metadata rejects before arrayBuffer. Any compatibility normalization is explicit and malformed host fakes remain rejected.
notes:
Reusable discovery method: cross the actual language/runtime FFI boundary for every provider field before ratcheting its Python type. Pure Python lookalikes and import-only health checks do not establish binding semantics.
Host fakes now reject malformed size and non-string ETag metadata, and every Worker route has a zero-arrayBuffer oversized sentinel. Actual workerd R2 FFI result types remain unobserved, so this method bead intentionally stays open.

title: Exclude failed staged candidates from later pile settlement
description: A pile merge commits durable candidate/staged rows before root CAS. On a publication failure, _restore_authoritative_state rebuilds proofs from the root but deliberately retains staged receipts. A later independent pile can trigger a full canonical rebuild; without an explicit allowed-staged boundary, the failed pile's candidates join that settlement and can change offer winners or become published even though their own unit is still pending.
acceptance_criteria: Each pile settlement admits non-staged receipts plus only that pile's staged fact IDs; disallowed staged receipts force the filtered rebuild path and cannot supply offers, dependencies, actions, or winners. A realistic conflicting-offer test fails the first pile after merge, processes a healthy pile behind it, proves the failed candidate remains staged but ineligible, then retries it without loss. Restart and post-CAS failure paths remain correct.
notes:
Reusable probe: make two independently closed units offer the same canonical address, fail the lower-fid unit after its SQLite merge but before publication, then force a rebuild with the higher-fid unit. Assert the pending lower-fid receipt cannot leak into the later root.
Implemented allowed-staged settlement filtering and restart coverage: a failed pile remains durably staged but cannot become eligible through a later independent pile's rebuild.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Prove exact rejection evidence before ingress retirement
description: Node._quarantine_ingress writes failed/pile and metadata, then unconditionally deletes the live pile without reading either record back or reconciling an ambiguous DELETE. A fake/provider can acknowledge a wrong or missing evidence write, or apply deletion and lose the response, leaving no locally checked ghost-obligation proof. Quarantine also accepts raw=None and can manufacture metadata for bytes it never read.
acceptance_criteria: Only a typed input-local permanent rejection enters quarantine; raw bytes are required; the content-addressed rejection payload and metadata are read back byte-exact before retirement; retirement checks the exact source bytes and reconciles an ambiguous applied delete; any evidence/read/delete failure leaves either the live source or a verified exact rejection payload and never blocks a later independent pile. Real-Node and injected store-boundary tests cover wrong/missing evidence, metadata failure, delete-before/after-apply failure, and restart visibility.
notes:
This is the concrete runtime slice of poc-16-ilr and poc-16-kgp.10's ghost obligation: a destructive event must cite exact committed-root representation or exact durable typed-rejection bytes.
Implemented exact immutable payload and content-addressed typed-record readback before exact-source retirement, including ambiguous delete reconciliation and two-worker races.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Declare serialization boundary for Lambda stack creation
description: A describe-absent preflight followed by sam deploy is not one atomic CloudFormation operation. Another actor can create the same friendly name between those steps, and SAM does not expose a caller-selected create-only changeset mode through this wrapper.
design: Treat this as a trusted deployment-administrator boundary, not as a proved atomic create. Exact StackId removes the analogous update/delete target race.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation states create mode requires external serialization for a chosen name and recommends high-entropy names for automation. Tests prove known collisions fail before SAM; a future implementation evaluates direct CREATE change sets if hostile same-name concurrency must be eliminated.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bind Lambda management to one stable deployment identity
description: The component marker is identical across every POC-16 Lambda stack, so selecting another legitimate stack by typo passes type checks. Updates and removals need a caller-supplied stable non-secret deployment identity distinct from component type.
design: Keep one component-type marker and add a separate poc16:deployment-id value. Do not infer ownership from the friendly stack name.
acceptance_criteria: Create requires a validated deployment ID stored in a stack tag plus template parameter/output. Update and remove require the exact caller ID to match both tag and output before using StackId. A negative control with two otherwise-valid POC-16 stacks proves the wrong deployment ID invokes no mutation.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: F10: check destructive operations with ghost obligations
description: Turn every destructive shared-bucket operation into a history-checkable proof obligation. Assign each immutable ingress key a ghost obligation at acknowledged creation; a DELETE may discharge it only by citing either (a) a committed root whose authenticated closure represents every publishable fact in the exact ingress bytes, or (b) a durable typed permanent-rejection record containing those exact bytes. Record object creation, root CAS, rejection persistence, LIST pages, crashes, retries, and deletes as a replayable trace. Apply the same checker to deterministic schedules, randomized F2 histories, and provider adapter tests so a new deletion path cannot silently bypass the retirement law.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable trace checker rejects delete-before-publication, delete-after-lost/unknown CAS response without reconciliation, retry-count quarantine, rejection without exact bytes, and cleanup of a newly reused key; it accepts winning publication, CAS-loser reconciliation against the committed root, and exact durable permanent rejection. At least one realistic real-Node concurrency test emits and validates the trace, failures shrink to the first unsupported DELETE, and every production ingress deletion site is covered.
notes:
Reusable problem-finding method extracted from the shared-ingress review: follow durable obligations, not worker ownership or retry counts. This makes destructive safety locally auditable even when workers have delayed catalogs and LIST spans pages.
Concrete itm coverage now exercises the rejection-side obligation across wrong evidence acknowledgments, delete before/after apply, repeated retries, and a two-worker barrier race. F10 remains open to emit/check one uniform trace for both valid committed-root representation and typed rejection across all adapters and deletion sites.
2026-07-29 deterministic core landed in codex/kgp-f10: a reusable checker plus real Node winner, identical-root CAS loser, applied-but-response-lost, unapplied unknown negative, exact InvalidPile/KernelRejected, two-page insertion/fairness, stale-catalog restart, reused-key, current-root, and production deletion-capability inventory schedules. Remaining acceptance scope is deliberately not claimed complete: randomized F2 and live/provider-adapter normalization are tracked by poc-16-kgp.29, depending on kgp.2 and x1p.3. Keep kgp.10 open until that integration lands.

title: Handle legal short reads in bounded S3 response bodies
description: One bounded StreamingBody.read(n) call may legally return fewer bytes before EOF on a generic stream. Treating the first short read as ContentLength truncation can reject valid bodies, while retrying without a total bound risks over-allocation.
design: Track remaining budget and declared ContentLength separately; require one EOF observation when length is absent and never exceed the allocation ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded loop reads at most limit plus one bytes, accepts deterministic one-byte chunks through exact EOF, rejects true early EOF and one-byte-over bodies, closes every stream, and never calls read without an amount.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Preserve mint provider faults across verifier exceptions
description: The mint path can record a provider fetch failure and then return 403 from an exception branch before inspecting that record, making a provider outage look like invalid authorization and bypassing 5xx telemetry.
design: Keep authorization details opaque while separating infrastructure failure class from a deterministic denial.
acceptance_criteria: Every return and exception path after provider fetch checks the recorded provider error first. A raising verifier/consumer probe plus ordinary invalid-proof control show provider faults return 503 and invalid proofs remain 403.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Make Lambda live-smoke naming and cleanup outcome-safe
description: The generated live-smoke stack name carries only 48 random bits, is not proven absent before deploy, and cleanup warnings discard the cleanup failure when a primary failure also occurred.
design: Use the same ownership markers as production, never delete an existing collision, and preserve both error objects rather than logging one away.
acceptance_criteria: Generated names contain at least 128 random bits, create mode performs an exact absence preflight, cleanup probes for a possibly-applied stack, absence is harmless, and simultaneous primary plus cleanup failures are returned as an ExceptionGroup. Deterministic collision and dual-failure tests cover both branches.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bind Lambda removal to the exact CloudFormation stack identity
description: Removal validates one stack by name and then asks SAM to delete that name, leaving a time-of-check/time-of-use window in which a replacement stack could become the target.
design: CloudFormation APIs accept the unique stack ID wherever StackName is accepted. Keep account/region/marker checks before using it.
acceptance_criteria: After ownership validation, removal passes the exact returned StackId ARN to SAM. A replacement under the same friendly name cannot change the command target in tests. Missing and malformed StackId values fail before deletion.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Refuse Lambda deploy takeover of unrelated stacks
description: sam deploy accepts an arbitrary stack name and may update or tag an existing unrelated stack. Deployment must distinguish a caller-declared create from an update and bind updates to an already-owned stack identity.
design: Expose mutually exclusive explicit create/update CLI modes. Treat only the documented CloudFormation not-found ValidationError as absence; permission, transport, and parsing errors fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Create mode proves the exact name absent and refuses any existing stack; update mode requires the account, region, deployment tag, and output marker and passes the exact StackId to SAM. Missing, unrelated, and mode-mismatch negative controls invoke no deploy subprocess.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Clean up a unique smoke Worker after partial deploy failure
description: The live smoke marks deployed only after pywrangler returns successfully. If Cloudflare applies the upload but the CLI loses its response or exits late, the unique Worker is leaked. Once absence of the generated name is established, treat invocation as potentially applied and attempt bounded unconditional deletion in finally, while preserving the original error and reporting cleanup failure.
acceptance_criteria: Failure injection applies a fake deployment then raises before returning; smoke still invokes deletion for the exact generated name. A failure before ownership/absence preflight performs no deletion. Cleanup errors remain observable without hiding the primary error, and R2 is never mutated.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: smoke establishes absence of a 128-bit random Worker name, marks upload possibly applied before Wrangler, and deletes only the exact generated config with a 60-second bound. Apply-then-error and dual-failure tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in source commit c331d25; focused Cloudflare/gateway/R2/async/layout suite passes 71 tests.

title: Reject oversized R2 objects before arrayBuffer allocation
description: The Worker config advertises a 4 MiB object ceiling, but R2BindingStore currently calls R2ObjectBody.arrayBuffer() before Gateway checks length. A valid 64 MiB core object or corrupt provider response can allocate beyond the deployment budget. Use the documented R2Object.size metadata to fail before body consumption, retain a post-read length/size check, and let the Worker translate the explicit over-limit result consistently.
acceptance_criteria: R2 store configuration has a validated read ceiling no larger than the core maximum; the Worker selects 4 MiB. A fake object above the limit has an arrayBuffer method that raises if invoked and the request is rejected without invoking it. N and N+1, missing/malformed size, short body, root, invite, single object, and batch paths are covered.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Refuse Cloudflare deploy/remove against an unowned Worker
description: manage.py accepts an arbitrary CF_WORKER_NAME and can overwrite or delete a pre-existing unrelated Worker. Give each deployment a stable non-secret ownership marker, inspect current Worker settings through the direct Cloudflare API before mutation, refuse absent/mismatched ownership except for explicit first creation, and verify ownership after deploy. Keep credentials out of generated config and logs.
acceptance_criteria: Negative controls prove deploy and remove refuse an existing Worker with missing or different ownership, malformed API responses, and ambiguous API failures. First creation is explicit, updates/removal require exact ownership, generated configs carry the non-secret marker, and a post-deploy check verifies the target. Live smoke uses a unique name and never weakens ordinary removal.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: stable POC16_DEPLOYMENT_OWNER binding, bounded direct settings API preflight, exact-owner postflight, explicit first creation, and owned-only removal. This prevents accidental targeting under the documented single trusted/external-serialization boundary; the unsolved concurrent-admin TOCTOU is poc-16-x1p.5.10.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in source commit c331d25; focused Cloudflare/gateway/R2/async/layout suite passes 71 tests.

title: Make direct S3 endpoint selection immune to ambient SDK overrides
description: S3Store._sdk_clients leaves Botocore's configured-endpoint lookup enabled. Even when the host JSON rejects endpoint_url, Boto3 officially honors AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, and endpoint_url entries in the selected shared profile before falling back to the AWS service endpoint. A production host can therefore route authoritative GET/CAS/LIST through an emulator, cache, proxy, or other non-S3 endpoint by ambient process/profile configuration. R2 passes its direct account endpoint explicitly and is not displaced by these lower-precedence settings.
acceptance_criteria: Set Botocore's supported ignore_configured_endpoint_urls option explicitly for SDK-created S3 clients while retaining explicit S3Config.endpoint_url as the deliberate test/emulator escape hatch and R2's explicit account endpoint. Unit tests capture both read/mutation Botocore Config values under hostile endpoint environment/profile settings; an integration-level resolved-endpoint check rejects or proves no ambient override. Existing injected-client and explicit-endpoint tests remain green.
notes:
Found while adversarially reviewing poc-16-x1p.6. AWS's current official service-specific-endpoint documentation says Boto3 supports global/service endpoint environment variables and shared-profile endpoint_url, and that ignore_configured_endpoint_urls=true suppresses them while explicit constructor endpoint_url still wins. Reusable probe: run host selection with hostile AWS_ENDPOINT_URL/AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 plus a shared profile and inspect both clients' resolved meta.endpoint_url before any operation.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Define and enforce the S3 bucket-policy publisher threat profile
description: The generated deny policy applies only to one publisher principal. A second permitted writer or lifecycle administrator can bypass authoritative-key immutability, so the renderer must not claim a bucket-wide invariant without defining who may write.
design: Prefer bucket-wide explicit denies scoped to the configured object prefix when AWS condition keys allow it. If shared administration cannot be safely constrained, enforce and name a single-publisher profile and validate the complete allowed-writer set.
acceptance_criteria: The renderer explicitly selects either a bucket-wide guard or a single-publisher deployment profile.
