Policy tests include a second-principal negative control and lifecycle mutation. Documentation states residual trusted administrators and never overclaims what AWS policy conditions enforce.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Smoke the built Lambda artifact with reproducible dependencies
description: The package smoke uses the invoking host Python and a fresh target directory instead of importing the SAM-built Lambda artifact under the declared Python 3.13 Lambda runtime. Direct pins alone do not lock transitive wheels or hashes.
design: Keep lock, build, and smoke boilerplate under deploy/aws_lambda. Permit a clearly reported local structural fallback only when the container runtime is unavailable; it cannot count as target-runtime evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A clean build produces one target artifact, the smoke executes that artifact in the Lambda Python 3.13 image or equivalent SAM local runtime, and SDK conditional-write plus PyNaCl imports are checked there. Dependency resolution is committed with hashes and fails closed on drift.
notes:
Source commit 542b945 replaces host-only smoke with SAM artifact execution in the Lambda Python 3.13 x86_64 image and commits a hash-locked full dependency closure. The closure installed successfully and the assembled artifact passed SDK/PyNaCl/endpoint tests on host Python 3.13 x86_64, but SAM is absent and this environment cannot access the Docker daemon, so target-image evidence remains outstanding and this bead stays open.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf. The exact hash-locked artifact again passed provider-free SDK capability execution on host Python 3.13 x86_64 with boto3 1.43.51/botocore 1.43.51; cfn-lint and the 551-pass integrated suite are green. SAM remains absent and Docker daemon access denied, so target-image execution is still the sole blocker.

title: Refuse removal of unowned CloudFormation stacks
description: The remove command accepts any stack name and invokes sam delete without verifying account, region, template identity, or ownership, so an operator typo can delete an unrelated stack.
design: Put an explicit deployment marker and component version in the template outputs/tags and require the marker in a read-only preflight. Provide no implicit broad-delete fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Removal first describes the exact stack and checks immutable POC-16 ownership outputs or tags plus expected account and region. Missing, ambiguous, or unrelated stacks are refused in negative-control tests and no delete subprocess is invoked. Live-smoke teardown still removes its generated owned stack.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Validate Lambda template inputs and gate deploy on health
description: CloudFormation accepts bucket and prefix values that S3Config rejects during cold initialization, and the normal deploy command can report success without checking the Function URL.
design: Share validation constraints mechanically where possible, cap physical key length for the longest gateway namespace, and separate liveness from provider readiness if both are exposed.
acceptance_criteria: Every CloudFormation-accepted bucket/prefix value is accepted by S3Config and known invalid or overlong examples are rejected before deployment. A normal deploy resolves the owned stack URL and runs a bounded health/readiness check; failure makes deploy fail.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Observe handled Function URL failures
description: The handler converts gateway and provider failures into HTTP 5xx responses, but the template alarms only on Lambda Errors, which does not count handled responses, and application failures have no structured log.
design: Retain an invocation budget alarm, replace the ineffective application-error alarm with Url5xxCount, and accept optional alarm action ARNs as deployment parameters.
acceptance_criteria: IaC alarms on Function URL Url5xxCount, handler failures emit bounded structured logs without secrets or request bodies, alarms expose notification configuration, and an injected provider failure proves a 503 is both returned and observable.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Fit AWS SDK deadlines inside Lambda timeout
description: S3 and Secrets Manager socket/retry defaults can outlive the 15 second Lambda timeout, causing hard termination before fail-closed response and telemetry paths run.
design: Configure separate read-only clients for a finite connect/read budget and no hidden long retry envelope. Validate the budget against the template constant in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Template timeout and every configured SDK connect/read/retry budget have a tested cleanup margin. S3 reads and Secrets Manager use explicit low bounded attempts and timeouts; injected timeout failures return or log deterministically before the Lambda deadline.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Make Lambda missing-object semantics least-privilege correct
description: The Lambda role lacks ListBucket, so S3 returns AccessDenied for absent keys and the gateway converts ordinary misses into 503 responses. Preserve the rule that arbitrary 403 is never absence while granting only the exact listing visibility needed to distinguish missing gateway keys.
design: Use bucket-level s3:ListBucket constrained by s3:prefix to the exact root, obj, and invite namespaces. Do not weaken adapter 403 classification.
acceptance_criteria: A semantic IAM/template test and an execution-role-equivalent provider probe show absent root, object, and invite keys produce the intended missing result, while a denied existing key still fails closed. The role cannot enumerate outside the configured deployment prefix.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Enforce S3 read ceilings before body allocation
description: The S3 adapter currently calls StreamingBody.read without an amount and gateway size checks run only after the provider body is fully downloaded. Oversized or corrupt objects can consume memory and time before central limits reject them.
design: Add a provider-neutral bounded reader surface or an S3-specific bounded read method used by Gateway. Keep provider SDK imports outside core and preserve the generic ObjectReader behavior at its declared absolute cap.
acceptance_criteria: ContentLength is checked before reading when present; streaming reads consume at most limit plus one byte; exact-limit bodies pass, one-byte-over bodies fail, truncated/inconsistent bodies fail, and the body is closed. Negative-control bodies fail the test if read is called unboundedly.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Adaptive batching stalls the 3 MiB black-box attachment transfer
description: After the byte-bound/adaptive-batch change on main, tests/test_blackbox.py::test_alice_bob_carol repeatedly times out waiting for Alice's 3,000,000-byte file to reach Bob and Carol. The full suite failed once after 45 seconds (391 passed, 2 skipped) and an immediate isolated rerun failed identically in 46.81 seconds, so this is reproducible rather than a one-off timeout. Text convergence succeeds before the file phase; the scenario also sends a concurrent 100,000-byte file from Bob. Investigate the separated facts-pile/blob-fetch path, batch 413 splitting, sync-cache blob state, and daemon byte ceilings.
acceptance_criteria: The isolated black-box scenario passes repeatedly with exact hashes for both 3,000,000-byte and 100,000-byte files, the transfer remains separated from the facts pile and within every request/response ceiling, an instrumented regression fails at the actual stalled seam rather than only timing out, and the full ordinary suite is green.
notes: Root cause reproduced from daemon logs and retained stores: the fact-only push changed Bob->Alice's root, but no blob moved; Alice has no outbound peer, while Carol only dials Alice. Carol's _fetch_blobs repeatedly hit HTTP 404 on a Bob-owned proof and aborted before completing Alice's proofs. Repair: every locally available referenced immutable object is hash-verified and PUT idempotently before its fact-only pile; failed object transport prevents the fact delivery, while replicas missing an object may still relay the fact for another source to satisfy. Real HTTP tests reject wrong-addressed objects and pull-only grants; the 3 MiB/100 KiB star black box passed twice. Reusable finding method split into the F9 bead: enumerate directed rather than merely connected replica graphs and schedule object availability independently from fact/root convergence.
close_reason: Objects-first, fact-only push ordering is implemented with hash-verified immutable PUTs; wrong-address/read-only/failure-before-fact tests pass, the directed star black box passed repeatedly, and the full suite is 399 passed with 2 live-provider skips.

title: Keep the Cloudflare package inside edge imports and centralized response ceilings
description: Integrating the host R2 S3 adapter made adapters.r2.__init__ eagerly import adapters.s3 whenever the direct Worker binding module was imported, pulling a host-only graph into workerd. The initial Cloudflare config also allowed an 8 MiB single object while the shared gateway's deployment response envelope is 4 MiB. Make host R2 exports lazy and derive every Worker budget from the core ceilings, with the single-object and batch responses both capped at 4 MiB.
acceptance_criteria: Importing deploy.cloudflare_worker.runtime does not import adapters.s3 or adapters.r2.s3; public from-adapters.r2 R2 S3 exports still work; staged workerd imports the direct binding; all configurable Worker budgets are no greater than core.limits and MAX_OBJECT_BYTES/MAX_BATCH_BYTES are at most 4 MiB; package, dry-run, workerd, and repository tests pass.
notes: Fixed on codex/x1p-cf-package: adapters.r2 keeps R2BindingStore eager but resolves R2S3Config/R2S3Store lazily, preserving public imports without loading host adapters in the Worker graph. Runtime ceilings are derived from core.limits; checked-in Wrangler vars are tested byte-for-byte against runtime, with both object and batch bodies capped at 4 MiB. Import, staging, dry-run, and request-level workerd tests pass.
close_reason: Edge import isolation and centralized 4 MiB response ceilings are implemented and covered by focused repository/package/build/workerd tests; the sole unrelated full-suite attachment regression is separately owned as P0 poc-16-x1p.13.

title: Choose the root CAS threat model for provider strong ETags
description: The ordinary S3/R2 deployment profile can use the providers' direct conditional-write APIs and explicitly assume their RFC 9110 strong ETags obey the provider register contract: one comparison token must not identify two different observable root byte strings. This is a provider axiom, not a mathematical injectivity proof. Decide whether POC-16 also promises correctness against a maliciously engineered ETag collision. If it does, use an independent linearizable generation register (AWS DynamoDB and a Cloudflare Durable Object are the leading constructions) because R2's unique version is not currently accepted by conditional puts. Keep content hashes, provider comparison tokens, and any generation capability separate.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md names the supported threat profile. Both adapters reject missing, empty, and weak ETags and conformance tests include a deterministic token-alias negative control. If malicious validator collisions are in scope, implement and test independent generation registers for both providers; otherwise document provider strong-validator semantics as an explicit deployment axiom and keep the stronger construction as a future profile.
notes:
Found while implementing poc-16-x1p.3's token ledger and A->B->A conformance schedule. The ledger permits token reuse for byte-identical A but rejects the same token for distinct bytes and prints its seed/history. Do not conflate this with value ABA, which is safe under today's immutable closure model.
2026-07-29 provider-contract review: RFC 9110 defines a strong validator as changing whenever representation data changes; AWS documents object ETags as unique and content-change-reflecting and If-Match as comparing the current ETag; R2 exposes strongly consistent ETag conditional operations. Those statements justify an ordinary direct-provider profile, but do not prove cryptographic injectivity against an adversary. Added hostile provider responses for W/ weak validators: reads fail closed and mutation successes become OutcomeUnknown. Reusable finding method: exercise each adapter with missing, empty, weak, and deliberately aliased validator tokens; keep a token-to-bytes ledger across an A->B->A schedule so safe value ABA is allowed but token aliasing across distinct bytes is rejected.
Decision: POC-16's production profile assumes direct S3/R2 APIs honor documented RFC 9110 strong-validator semantics, rejects missing/empty/W/ ETags, and does not claim correctness against deliberately engineered validator collisions. DESIGN.md now states the axiom and the stronger DynamoDB/Durable Object generation-register profile. The deterministic alias negative control remains the executable boundary.
close_reason: The threat model is chosen and documented: ordinary direct-provider strong-ETag refinement, explicit weak-validator rejection and alias negative control; deliberate validator-collision resistance is outside this profile and has a named generation-register construction.

title: Rootless publication stamps an unverified absent base during bootstrap races
description: Publisher.publish has a no-anchor branch that calls stamp(None, received) whenever settlement.base_root is None, without rereading or conditionally verifying that root is still absent. Another publisher can create root after base() and before this stamp. The loser then records an exact-root stamp for absence it did not win; later _sync_index may repair it, but the Publisher.stamp contract and one-snapshot reasoning are already false. Represent absence as an explicit conditional version and run the same no-op/base verification before stamping a rootless settlement.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic two-publisher bootstrap schedule pauses the rootless writer after reading absence, lets another writer create a valid root, and proves the first raises RootChanged/retains intent rather than stamping None. The ordinary single-writer rootless case still stamps absence without a CAS, and restart repair remains correct.
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (awaiting vpf/sgg dependency closure): rootless publication rechecks absence and a concurrent-bootstrap regression test fails the old behavior.
close_reason: Running Publisher rechecks absent root before rootless stamp and the deterministic two-publisher bootstrap regression passes; former vpf blocker is closed.

title: Bound R2 root hot-key publication rate and handle 429 without semantic loss
description: Cloudflare documents at most one write per second to the same R2 object key; the design serializes every publication through mutable root and local authoring can exceed that rate. Treat this as a provider liveness/throughput constraint, not a CAS correctness failure. Measure real publication demand, coalesce local durable intents behind a cadence, add jittered backoff for 429/retryable failures, preserve every staged intent across throttling and restart, and ensure 429 is never normalized to stale. If the required product rate cannot fit one root key, step back and choose an explicit register-sharding/serialization design rather than weakening CAS.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic clock tests burst concurrent publications above 1 Hz, inject 429s, crash/restart during backoff, and converge to the serial union with no busy loop or dropped intent. A live staging R2 test records the observed same-key limit. DESIGN.md states the sustainable commit-rate bound and whether batching is sufficient.

title: Byte-bound batched object reads and adapt peer page splitting
description: The /page batch route limits only object count (256), not encoded bytes. A legal batch of large blobs can exceed AWS Lambda Function URL/API Gateway or Cloudflare Worker response limits and can allocate unbounded JSON/base64 memory. Define an aggregate raw and encoded response budget, reject or truncate only at object boundaries with an explicit continuation, and make Peer.objs adaptively split requests without changing order or miss positions. Tree pages remain individually capped; blob fetches should prefer direct single/ranged reads where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Tests construct 256 individually valid large objects, prove handlers never exceed the configured response/body budget, and prove Peer reconstructs the exact ordered result through adaptive batches including misses and one object near the limit. Oversized single objects fail explicitly rather than loop; Lambda and Cloudflare limits are represented by deployment-specific configuration.
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending commit): daemon and shared serverless Gateway enforce exact compact-JSON/base64 aggregate response budgets as well as count, request, object, and root ceilings. Peer.objs recursively halves only on HTTP 413, preserves order/misses, and turns singleton 413 into an explicit ValueError. Exact-at-limit and one-byte-over tests cover the base64 envelope; a 256-valid-object test proves the responder stops fetching before exceeding its configured budget. The first draft exposed a separate valid-file failure: _push embedded every referenced Bao proof, making one facts pile proportional to file size and incompatible with a finite pile cap. Fixed by sending only the closed facts pile and using the existing hash-verified _fetch_blobs object path; a realistic attachment test proves separation and completion. Reusable probe: shrink only the configured byte ceiling while retaining 256 content-address-valid objects, which tests boundary logic without allocating production-sized buffers.
close_reason: Byte-bounded batch serving, exact envelope accounting, adaptive client splitting, singleton failure, and separated attachment transfer are implemented and tested.

title: Negotiate read-only peer capability for serverless authorization gateways
description: The Lambda and Cloudflare deployments are database-free authorization/read services, but core.sync assumes every authenticated peer accepts pile PUTs and can publish. When local state is ahead it pushes, so a read-only edge endpoint otherwise fails or misleadingly acknowledges work it cannot settle. Add an authenticated capability/version signal to mint or the root protocol and make sync choose pull-only behavior for a read-only peer. Unknown old peers retain today's full-peer behavior. The edge must reject unsupported mutation routes explicitly and never return a delivery receipt for unserviceable ingress.
acceptance_criteria: Black-box tests run existing Peer/sync against a read-only fake edge: behind clients pull, ahead clients do not PUT or lose intent, equal clients idle, capability tampering fails closed, and full peers retain bidirectional convergence. Lambda and Cloudflare handlers advertise the same capability bytes.
notes:
Assigned to poc16_audit on branch codex/x1p-readonly-cap from contract commit 7681d04.
Integration review found that the original daemon checked only whether a capability string was known, so a valid READ_ONLY grant could still authorize direct pile PUT if a client ignored negotiation. Fixed on main during merge: pure grant verification has require_push, daemon PUT enforces it, serverless gateway mints the canonical READ_ONLY profile, and a real HTTP regression sends a valid read-only token directly to the push door and gets 401.
close_reason: Landed a shared canonical full/read-only mint profile, HMAC-bound and sealed with the grant; Peer caches it fail-closed, sync retains pending local fact/action intent without PUTs to read-only edges, remint upgrades resume delivery, and real-HTTP coverage proves full, legacy, read-only, tampered, cold-cache, and remint behavior.

title: Add an async memoized WorkerView for awaited object stores
description: Cloudflare R2 binding calls are awaited, while core.worker.WorkerView and btreap.Reader synchronously fetch one data-dependent page at a time. Add a provider-neutral asynchronous authorization driver that reuses the one facts registry, kernel judgment, canonical codecs, and family authorize hooks rather than mirroring policy. It must perform hash/order/depth validation identical to btreap.Reader, memoize immutable objects per request, batch independent keys when possible, and enforce both aggregate byte and unique-subrequest budgets. The root is fetched and pinned once; a concurrent root update cannot alter the decision.
acceptance_criteria: Generated real-root/request fixtures yield identical decisions in synchronous and async views across valid, suppressed, removed, expired, malformed, missing/corrupt-page, and concurrent-root schedules. Tests count unique fetches and bytes, enforce configured budgets below the chosen Workers plan limits, and prove repeated tree paths hit the request cache. No async policy registry or family mirror is added.
notes:
Implemented core.mint.async_stateless as a provider-neutral awaited driver around the existing stateless/WorkerView/btreap path. A private BaseException cache-miss sentinel crosses existing Exception fail-closed boundaries; the driver memoizes bytes and missing objects per request, enforces explicit unique-fetch and aggregate-byte budgets, and never reads or repins root. Real Node snapshot tests cover differential allow/suppressed-history/removed/expired/malformed decisions, missing/corrupt pages, repeated-path memoization, budget boundaries, and a root change during an awaited fetch. Full suite: 269 passed.
Merged to main as f21e610. The shared async gateway now consumes async_stateless for both Cloudflare and Lambda, so awaited authorization has one policy path.
close_reason: Provider-neutral async_stateless uses the canonical WorkerView/policy path with per-request memoization and byte/fetch budgets; both deployments consume it and the full suite passes 399 tests.

title: Prove Cloudflare Python Worker packaging and remove POSIX imports from the read path
description: The preferred Cloudflare implementation reuses the authoritative Python facts/kernel rather than creating a second TypeScript security core, but it is not deployable until proven. core.mint -> core.worker -> core.manifest currently imports core.store, whose top-level fcntl import is unavailable in Python Workers. Split pure object-integrity/contract helpers from FsStore so the read-only graph imports no fcntl, sqlite3, or nonfunctional concurrency module. Build the actual repository modules with pywrangler, prove the selected Pyodide version supplies compatible PyNaCl, and complete an Ed25519 verification plus sealed-grant round trip in workerd. If this fails, stop and record the concrete incompatibility before choosing TypeScript/WASM.
acceptance_criteria: A pywrangler dry-run packages the actual core/ and facts/ modules without copies, imports the complete mint path in workerd, exercises PyNaCl signing verification and sealed-box round trip, and has an import-graph test forbidding POSIX/SQLite modules on the edge path. The resulting language decision and compatibility date are recorded in DESIGN.md.
notes:
Problem-finding method: a pywrangler dry-run is necessary but not sufficient. Inspect the emitted artifact for the canonical core/facts modules and forbidden host modules, then start local workerd and make a request that executes cryptography. This exposed accidental virtualenv bundling and a PyNaCl/libsodium EM_ASM load failure that dry-run alone missed. Stable Python 3.13/PyNaCl 1.5.0 and experimental Python 3.14/PyNaCl 1.6.2 were both tested; the exact-layout compatibility patch and request-context entropy path are covered by build and workerd tests. Upstream removal is tracked in poc-16-x1p.5.3.
Final evidence on branch codex/x1p-cf-package: 14 host-fake/package tests pass; Wrangler 4.115.0 clean dry-run emits 155 modules/1445.16 KiB including canonical core/mint.py, core/worker.py, core/limits.py, core/peer_capability.py, full facts, direct R2 binding, shared gateway, and patched PyNaCl while excluding POSIX/SQLite and host S3 graphs; local workerd accepts a request that completes Ed25519 sign/verify and sealed-box interoperability. Language/config decision is recorded in DESIGN.md at compatibility date 2026-07-29.
close_reason: Actual canonical Python Worker import path, PyNaCl compatibility, Ed25519/sealed-box request self-test, forbidden import ratchet, and dated design decision all pass in pywrangler/workerd.

title: Differential-test Python, Lambda, and Cloudflare authorization runtimes
description: Generate canonical provider-independent fixtures from real Python Node publications and request closures, then run them through core.mint, the Lambda handler, and the Cloudflare Worker. Cover clear/active suppression, principal liveness, delegated authority, valid/expired/malformed requests, corrupt or missing tree pages, root pinning during a concurrent update, opaque provider tokens, object-fetch budgets, and sealed grant contents. Include structure-aware randomized cases with deterministic seeds so a cross-runtime mismatch shrinks to a fixture and request trace.
acceptance_criteria: All three runtimes return identical status, authorization principal/verb, snapshot digest, and fail-closed behavior for the checked corpus; randomized seeds are replayable; fixtures are generated by code rather than hand-maintained parallel JSON; a mismatch fails CI and identifies the first divergent authenticated read.

title: Inject remote stores without provider dependencies in core
description: Node currently hardcodes FsStore in Node.store(), so an adapter can exist yet be impossible to select. Add a provider-neutral store factory/composition seam and configuration loader outside core provider logic. Preserve FsStore as the zero-config local default. Support one bucket plus a collision-safe workspace prefix mapping, validate keys/prefixes, keep secrets out of keyring/logs, and make daemon/CLI startup select S3 or R2 without importing provider SDKs unless requested. The edge deployments construct their own read-only stores directly and do not instantiate Node or SQLite.
acceptance_criteria: Tests run two independent Nodes over one injected scripted/provider store, default local startup is unchanged, invalid provider/prefix config fails before mutation, absent optional SDKs affect only the selected provider, and CLI/daemon help exposes reproducible S3/R2 configuration. No facts/family/core policy code branches on provider names.

Tests run independent Nodes over one fake bucket, rebuild/query across processes, prove exact disjoint workspace key sets, exercise the real CLI->daemon->Node path, and cover malformed/duplicate/oversize/secret/non-finite/missing-SDK cases. Audit findings recorded separately: ambient Boto endpoint redirection is P0 poc-16-x1p.1.2; random manifest geometry makes a warm-sync cost test flaky in poc-16-npz. Full suite: 399 passed, 2 skipped, with only the already-filed 3 MiB transfer stall poc-16-x1p.13 and newly filed poc-16-npz failing; focused provider/host/layout gate: 100 passed.

title: Deploy the database-free authorization service on Cloudflare Workers
description: Add an isolated deploy/cloudflare_worker package that uses a direct R2 binding and exposes the same database-free authorization/read boundary as the Lambda package: POST /mint plus the minimal authenticated root/object reads. It is not a publisher and must not acquire SQLite.
