title: Build deterministic and live S3/R2 conformance environments
description: Provide two deliberately different test layers. CI uses the seeded adversarial in-memory contract harness plus provider fake clients to force rare and ambiguous outcomes. Opt-in live tests use dedicated S3 and R2 buckets/prefixes to verify the provider claims we actually depend on: atomic body/token reads, If-None-Match creation, one-winner If-Match replacement under concurrent independent clients, immediate direct visibility, paginated LIST, opaque token handling, and safe recovery after a deliberately dropped client response where feasible. LocalStack, moto, MinIO, Wrangler local R2, or Miniflare may test SDK/package wiring but must never be cited as evidence of AWS/Cloudflare semantics. Live cleanup is restricted to a generated test prefix and validates the prefix before deletion.
acceptance_criteria: One ordinary-CI command runs deterministic tests without credentials; separate documented commands run S3 and R2 live tests with explicit opt-in environment variables and safe generated prefixes. Provider tests skip cleanly when credentials are absent, print a replay seed/history on failure, and never mutate production root/obj prefixes. Results distinguish contract proof, emulator wiring, and live-provider evidence.
notes:
Required live/fake cases discovered by provider audits: A->B->A token reuse; apply then discard the conditional PUT response; insertion between LIST pages; missing S3 object under a role without ListBucket (403 vs 404); quoted/non-content ETags; SDK conditional mutation with retries accidentally enabled; 412 vs 409 vs 429/5xx classification; R2 same-key throttling; two cold Lambda sandboxes sharing one secret; response batches immediately below/above front-door limits; and root changing while a mint decision holds its pinned bytes. Wrangler/local R2, moto, LocalStack, and MinIO prove wiring only, never provider semantics.
Provider evidence must also cover atomic same-response body/token pairing, conditional mutation SDK retry configuration, absent S3 GET under no-ListBucket IAM, stable signing secrets across cold instances, and front-door batch sizes immediately below/above limits.
S3 adapter audit contributed reusable deterministic probes: barrier-backed conditional bucket for one-winner races, broken streaming bodies, SDK retry-config capture, subprocess provider-import guard, apply-then-discard response, pagination insertion, and 403-without-ListBucket. Preserve these in the shared harness; live runs remain required for provider claims.
Implemented on codex/x1p-conformance: tests/provider_conformance.py is a seeded reusable sync/async schedule shared by FsStore, the S3 adapter, the R2 S3-host adapter, and the native R2 binding. It checks atomic version/token pairs, conditionals, immediate visibility, independent-handle one-winner replacement, bounded pagination, immutable collisions, and permitted A->B->A token reuse while a token ledger rejects aliasing across different bytes. Provider fakes preserve the reusable probes: atomic body/token mutation hook, applied-response discard, insertion between LIST pages, no-ListBucket 403, broken streaming body, quoted non-content tokens, and 409/429/5xx outcome classification. pytest markers separate ordinary/live/soak runs. Opt-in live S3/R2 tests reject endpoint overrides, require explicit flags and credentials, use only validated generated poc16-conformance/run-<128-bit> prefixes, cap cleanup, and remove current objects plus S3 versions/delete markers. Live execution was not possible in this worktree because no explicit provider opt-in/credentials were supplied; the tests skip cleanly, so the issue remains open pending live evidence. Reusable discovery method added: record every observed token->bytes association across a schedule and fail if one token aliases different bytes; this exposed poc-16-x1p.12. A second audit probe (unique cursors forever) exposed the native R2 LIST page-cap gap now recorded on poc-16-x1p.2. Commands: python3 -m pytest -q -m 'not live' tests/test_provider_conformance.py tests/test_provider_live.py; provider commands are in tests/test_provider_live.py's executable module docstring and should be copied into root README during integration.
Independent safety review added two reusable credibility probes before commit: validate the SDK's resolved live endpoint as an actual S3 service host rather than merely any *.amazonaws.com URL (an execute-api endpoint is the negative control), and require an awaited barrier with observed arrivals before describing asyncio.gather calls as a concurrent native-binding CAS race. The review also ratcheted propagation of a genuine live CAS OutcomeUnknown and prints generated prefixes for manual recovery if teardown itself fails. No destructive cleanup escape was found.
Post-implementation review accepted after the endpoint check was anchored to supported general-purpose S3 service endpoint shapes and regressions rejected both API Gateway and user-controlled ELB emulator hosts. The barrier-backed native R2 race was repeated successfully. Final local validation: 356 passed, 2 expected live skips; focused provider/store gate 75 passed, 2 live deselected; direct live marker command 2 skipped without opt-in; git diff --check clean.
Direct-upload refinement requirement from x1p.17.6.3: opt-in live presigner tests must inspect the actual wire surface (endpoint, bucket, exact key, signed header names and values, expiry/query claims, create-only condition, and body binding). They must not pass workspace/member/class/digest as an out-of-band provider oracle; those semantics are accepted only when derived into the key or signed values. Reuse WirePut/WirePutCapability as the credential-free contract oracle and keep live-provider evidence separate.

title: Implement the actual Cloudflare R2 ObjectStore adapters
description: Add provider-isolated R2 implementations for both supported access paths: a Python S3-compatible adapter for client/server nodes and a native R2-binding adapter for the Cloudflare Worker package. Share the abstract contract and golden conformance cases, not provider SDK code. The Python path uses the account endpoint and conditional headers without assuming boto's modeled S3 feature set. The Worker path returns object body plus R2Object.etag from one get(), uses onlyIf/conditional headers for root replacement and immutable creation, handles null conditional results distinctly from thrown/unknown outcomes, paginates list(), and bypasses custom-domain caching. Configuration covers account/bucket binding/prefix, timeouts, and local-vs-live environments.
acceptance_criteria: Both access paths pass the same opaque-token, conditional-create/replace, pagination, collision, and outcome-normalization vectors; native Worker tests use an R2-compatible local binding; an opt-in live R2 conformance run verifies global direct-API visibility and one-winner CAS; no authoritative operation uses a custom-domain/cache URL.
notes:
Native R2 Worker-binding adapter implemented on main: direct async get/body+raw-etag pairing, conditional create/replace, collision verification, paginated LIST, authoritative-key guards, and explicit retryable/unknown outcomes. Fake binding tests cover opaque tokens, short pages/cursors, collisions, 429/503 mapping, and guards. Host S3-compatible path and live conformance remain open.
Integration review found a real S3-compatibility trap: the AWS adapter's flexible ChecksumSHA256 headers are not listed as supported R2 PutObject features. The host R2 adapter therefore reuses the S3 conditional/CAS implementation but deliberately replaces AWS flexible checksum headers with R2-supported Content-MD5. Tests ratchet exact headers, direct account endpoint construction, conditionals, and credential isolation.
Conformance review found the native R2BindingStore LIST loop has no hard page count: it rejects a repeated cursor but will follow an unbounded sequence of distinct cursors. This violates the provider contract's bounded-drain requirement and gives a faulty binding/provider response an infinite request path. Add a configurable hard page cap and a fake binding that emits unique cursors forever; the S3-host path already has max_list_pages. Also add a malformed-result probe that rejects missing/empty native R2 etags instead of converting None to the literal token 'None'.
MAIN follow-up fixed both conformance-review gaps: native R2 LIST now has a configurable hard page cap and fails after exactly that many distinct cursors; root reads and CAS success reject missing/empty result ETags instead of manufacturing the token 'None'. Tests use a binding that returns a fresh cursor forever and malformed root/CAS result objects. The fresh-cursor-forever fake and null/empty-token response are reusable provider-result probes. Host/native implementation is complete; the bead stays open for direct live R2 evidence and the separate token-soundness decision.

title: Implement the actual Amazon S3 ObjectStore adapter
description: Add a production S3 adapter under adapters/s3/ or an equivalently isolated provider package; do not import boto3/botocore from core/. It must atomically return body plus opaque ETag from one GET response, use If-None-Match:* for absent root and immutable object creation, use If-Match with the exact captured ETag for root replacement, normalize 412/404/409 and SDK errors into definitive stale/retryable/unknown outcomes, paginate LIST, verify content-addressed collisions, and never issue unconditional writes or deletes for root or obj/. Configuration covers bucket, prefix, region, endpoint override, checksums/encryption, timeouts, and retry policy without assuming any ETag algorithm. Include a bucket/IAM policy that denies authoritative deletion and enforces conditional writes where AWS supports it.
acceptance_criteria: Fake-client tests exercise exact request headers and every result/error mapping, independent-handle races admit one winner, opaque ETags work, pagination is complete and bounded, and an opt-in live S3 conformance run verifies conditional create/replace, immediate visibility, collision handling, and ambiguous-retry recovery. Provider imports remain outside core/.
notes:
AWS implementation constraints: restrict the first adapter to general-purpose regional buckets; preserve returned ETags exactly including quotes; send ChecksumSHA256 independently of CAS; obtain body+ETag from one GetObject; configure the conditional-mutation client with total_max_attempts=1 so a hidden retry cannot turn apply+lost-response+412 into a false Stale; classify 412/404 as stale only in the documented conditional context, 409 as definitely-not-applied/retryable, and transport/429/5xx as unknown/retryable per the contract. A missing GetObject may be 403 when the role lacks ListBucket, so never map arbitrary 403 to absence. Fake-client tests must cover all of these. Reframe poc-16-eqd: Exists/False is safe only when the adapter has verified identical bytes; unknown/soft failure raises and prevents root CAS.
Assigned to aws_deploy on branch codex/x1p-s3 from contract commit 7681d04.
Adapter implementation complete on codex/x1p-s3: provider-isolated lazy boto3 construction, one-attempt mutation client, exact opaque ETag GET/CAS, conditional create/CAS, SHA-256 request checksums, scoped pagination, authoritative mutation guards, and conservative AWS error mapping. Fake-client/race/import-isolation coverage passes (48 focused tests with core store tests); full repository suite passed 291 tests before the final retry-validation additions. Issue intentionally remains open: IAM/bucket policy was excluded from this worktree assignment, and opt-in live-provider evidence belongs to poc-16-x1p.3.
Final validation after mutation-client retry metadata enforcement: python3 -m pytest -q completed with 302 passed; git diff --check clean.
Committed adapter and deterministic tests as 08b0d25 on codex/x1p-s3.
MAIN integration added deploy/aws_lambda/s3_bucket_policy.py: a deny-only, merge-safe guard renderer for the configured publisher principal. It denies root/obj DeleteObject and DeleteObjectVersion, denies publisher lifecycle mutation, requires If-None-Match for obj creation, and requires either If-Match or If-None-Match for root writes. Exact generated statements are tested. Live policy/provider evidence remains with poc-16-x1p.3, and provider-token soundness remains explicitly open as poc-16-x1p.12.

title: Production object-store adapters and serverless authorization deployments
description: Ship actual provider implementations and isolated deployment artifacts for the database-free authorization path. Core owns only the provider-neutral ObjectStore and WorkerView semantics. Provider SDK code lives under adapters/, AWS Lambda packaging under deploy/aws_lambda/, and Cloudflare Worker packaging under deploy/cloudflare_worker/. The program includes S3 and R2 adapters, opt-in live conformance environments, least-privilege policies, one-command build/deploy flows, cross-runtime golden vectors where runtimes differ, and rollback/observability checks. No deployment may route authoritative reads through a stale cache or asynchronous replica.
acceptance_criteria: Both providers pass deterministic contract tests and opt-in live conformance tests; Lambda and Cloudflare Worker packages build from clean checkouts, expose the database-free mint/read boundary, use least-privilege direct bucket bindings, and have tested local invocation plus documented one-command deploy/remove flows in the repository's three existing Markdown authorities or executable help.

title: Define the provider-neutral ObjectStore correctness contract
description:
The shared-bucket design needs a precise provider-neutral contract before its
S3/R2 adapters or adversarial harness can make meaningful claims.

Required operations and outcomes:

  read_versioned(key) -> (bytes, opaque token) | absent | transport error
  create(key, bytes)   -> created | exists | outcome unknown
  cas(key, token, bytes) -> applied(new token) | stale | outcome unknown

The bytes and token returned by read_versioned must describe one atomic object
version. For an absent root, CAS is conditional create. A successful return is
durable and immediately visible through the same authoritative direct API.
Tokens are comparison capabilities supplied by the implementation; callers
must never derive them from bytes or assume an ETag algorithm. Content hashes
remain a separate application identity.

The authoritative map has two roles:
  - obj/<sha256> is a grow-only content-addressed map, created conditionally and
    verified on collision;
  - root is one linearizable conditional register. Objects are made visible
    before one root CAS, which is the sole publication linearization point.

The contract does not require multi-key transactions, rename, append, or one
snapshot spanning multiple LIST pages. LIST is optional outside ingress and,
where supplied, must paginate internally or expose a bounded page/cursor API.
Direct S3 and R2 reads are strongly consistent. Stale successful reads and
post-acknowledgement invisibility are contract violations, not ordinary faults.
Cached custom-domain reads and asynchronous cross-region replicas are forbidden
for authoritative root/object access.

Failure results must distinguish a definitive stale precondition from an
ambiguous transport outcome: a request can commit and lose its response. Safety
comes from rereading/reconciling after unknown outcomes; liveness additionally
assumes fair retries and an available provider.

Deliverables:
  1. Write this contract into DESIGN.md and core/store.py.
  2. Introduce explicit version/result/error vocabulary used by runtime code.
  3. State which FsStore mechanisms refine the contract locally and where it
     is weaker (notably no fsync until fixed).
  4. Supply a reusable conformance suite for every implementation.
  5. Keep provider SDKs and deployment boilerplate outside core/.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md and the executable conformance suite agree on atomic versioned root reads, conditional create, linearizable conditional replace, acknowledged durability/visibility, opaque tokens, explicit unknown outcomes, immutable object verification, bounded paginated listing, and forbidden authoritative cache paths. FsStore and ScriptedBucket conform without claiming their POSIX mechanisms are deployable adapters.
notes:
Current-provider correction: AWS S3 has strong read-after-write and LIST consistency and PutObject supports If-Match/If-None-Match for general-purpose buckets; Cloudflare R2 direct Worker/S3 APIs are globally strongly consistent and support conditional put. The contract should exploit those properties. It must still model transport ambiguity, pagination, availability failures, and opaque tokens. A custom-domain cache or asynchronous replica is outside the authoritative adapter contract. FsStore is stronger in failure observability and unpaginated enumeration but weaker in power-loss durability because it currently omits fsync.
TOKEN/ABA LAW: provider tokens need not be generation-unique, but must be sound comparison capabilities for root content: the same token may recur only for byte-identical root values. Byte-identical X after X->Y->X is safe for today's value-CAS protocol because root bytes are the complete authoritative snapshot and referenced objects are immutable; work derived from X is valid whenever current bytes are exactly X. Model this value-ABA and remove global token-uniqueness claims. Reusing one token for different root bytes is nonconforming and must fail the conformance suite. Do not add a generation nonce unless semantics become history-dependent; it would damage byte-identical convergence and exceed ordinary S3/R2 ETag guarantees.
close_reason: The executable ObjectStore contract, explicit result/error vocabulary, provider-isolated adapters, DESIGN contract, and reusable deterministic conformance suite are implemented; provider-specific live evidence remains tracked separately.

title: Define and prove shared ingress-workset retirement
description: Workspace ingress is a shared, content-addressed workset: pile/<member>/<hash> authenticates and partitions the producer namespace, but interchangeable publishers may process any member's pile. Cross-member processing is therefore not itself a bug. The required safety law is retirement: a worker may delete a pile only after one committed root is proven to represent every publishable fact in it, or after the exact bytes and a demonstrably input-local permanent rejection are durably preserved. CAS losers and workers with delayed local catalogs may observe the result later by rebuilding from the committed root. Specify and test this under concurrent drainers, pagination, lost responses, no-op/already-present candidates, invalid input, and worker crash.
acceptance_criteria: A state-machine test treats ingress as a grow-only set plus idempotent retirement and proves that every deleted valid pile is represented in some committed, fully closed root. Two or more real Nodes may list/process/delete the same pile in any order without lost publishable facts, object/tree damage, or a private ownership claim. Invalid piles retain exact evidence before deletion. New piles inserted between bounded LIST pages remain for a fair later turn. Delayed catalogs rebuild from root. The producer member segment remains enforced at the HTTP write door.
notes:
CONSISTENCY CORRECTION (2026-07-29): current direct S3 and R2 LIST operations are strongly consistent. The bucket mismatch is not 2015-era eventual consistency; it is that LIST is paginated, a multi-page drain is not a multi-key transaction, and LIST-then-DELETE does not claim one consumer. Preserve the per-writer-vs-shared-queue decision and concurrent retirement tests, but do not inject stale direct LIST results as conforming provider behavior.
2026-07-29 model correction: the existing concurrent shared-bucket test already demonstrates a safe cross-member case—one worker wins publication and retires all three shared piles while the CAS loser rebuilds from that root. The earlier per-writer recommendation would strand work when the producer disappears and is not the intended interchangeable-worker model. The remaining risks are retirement before proven publication, currently ineligible receipts whose only durable holder disappears, paginated fairness, and permanent-vs-transient failure classification. Reusable finding method: track each pile hash as a ghost obligation and require every delete event to cite either a committed root whose authenticated closure contains its publishable facts or a durable rejection record containing the exact bytes.
poc-16-itm implements the malformed-input half of this law: exact payload plus deterministic content-addressed typed reason is read back before exact-source retirement; ambiguous deletes reconcile; two real Nodes coalesce evidence and retire idempotently. ilr remains open for the full valid-publication history proof, pagination/fairness, and every production deletion site.
2026-07-29 valid-publication half completed on codex/kgp-f10. The replayable obligation checker validates the current authoritative root (resident closure plus every authenticated Fact/Supp/Authority tree) before each valid retirement, and deterministically reclassifies exact bytes before accepting rejection metadata. Real schedules cover winner, already-represented/no-CAS, identical-root CAS loser retirement after reconciliation, applied-but-response-lost, unapplied unknown retention, two-page insertion behind an opaque cursor with a fair later turn, stale-catalog process restart, exact InvalidPile and KernelRejected, and same-key new lifetime. A real HTTP test ratchets producer-segment binding. First unsupported DELETE includes its replay prefix. Randomized/provider reuse is follow-up poc-16-kgp.29, not part of closing this workset-law decision.
close_reason: Shared ingress is now specified and tested as an interchangeable-worker durable workset: every real production retirement is trace-supported by current authenticated publication or exact semantically reclassified rejection; concurrency, ambiguity, pagination/fairness, restart, and producer-door conditions pass.

title: A lost CAS deletes the loser's staged receipts; recovery depends on an ingress pile a co-tenant will delete
description:
DESIGN.md, shared-bucket concurrency contract: "A loser retains its intent,
rereads the winning root, derives the union, and retries."

The catalog does not retain it. RootChanged -> _restore_authoritative_state
(node.py:259-262) -> _sync_index -> rebuild, and rebuild's first act inside its
transaction is discard_stage() (node.py:490). discard_stage does not merely
clear a marker -- it DELETEs the rows from both fact_index and facts
(catalog.py:276-286). The loser's durable receipts are gone from its catalog.

In practice the loser recovers because runtime.turn only deletes the ingress
pile on success (runtime.py:62), so the pile is still in pile/ and the next
turn re-drains it. The intent is retained by the STORE, not by the catalog.

That premise fails on a shared bucket, because of the companion defect
(filed separately): runtime.py:33 lists pile/ with no member filter, so any
co-tenant drains and DELETES every other writer's ingress. Verified during
review: two nodes sharing one store directory, A queues its own pile, B runs an
ordinary turn -- B consumes and deletes A's pile, and A's catalog does not have
the fact until it resyncs from B's published root.

In that run A recovered, because B's root happened to include the fact. The
unsafe case is a winner whose settlement admits a strict SUBSET of what the
loser staged -- which the design explicitly permits, since DESIGN.md has each
catalog re-resolve every named edge against its own candidate set. Then the
fact is absent from the loser's catalog, absent from the bucket, and absent
from the winner's root.

NOT YET CONSTRUCTED: I did not build a concrete family/settlement combination
that produces that strict subset, so treat the loss itself as unproven and the
missing-retention as proven. Building that case is the first task here, and it
is a natural target for the F2 fuzzer.

Fix direction: either make the loser genuinely retain intent (keep staged rows
across a rebuild rather than discarding them), or make the pile the declared
system of record and stop any node from deleting a pile it did not author.
notes:
REPRO (verified). Two Nodes with SEPARATE SQLite pointed at ONE shared FsStore
directory. B merges (staging fact_b durably into its own catalog), A wins the
CAS, B loses -- and after _restore_authoritative_state, B's candidate_of(fact_b)
is None and its facts count is back to the pre-merge value.

    seed = Node(tmp/"seed"); ws = cmds.create(seed, "alice", ts=1)
    raw_a, fact_a = closed_signed(seed, ws, message(pk, "general", "alice", 10))
    raw_b, fact_b = closed_signed(seed, ws, message(pk, "general", "bob",   11))
    for idx in seed._idx.values(): idx.close()

    bucket = tmp/"bucket"; shutil.copytree(seed.dir/"ws"/ws, bucket)
    A, B = (Node(copytree(seed.dir, tmp/a)) for a in ("A", "B"))
    for n in (A, B):
        shutil.rmtree(n.dir/"ws"/ws)
        n._stores[ws] = FsStore(bucket)      # one bucket, two indexes
        n._sync_index(ws)

    plan_b = B.merge(ws, candidates(raw_b))  # B stages, does not publish
    A.commit(ws, A.merge(ws, candidates(raw_a)))          # A wins
    try: B.commit(ws, plan_b)
    except RootChanged: pass                              # B loses
    B._restore_authoritative_state(ws)
    assert B.candidate_of(ws, fact_b.fid) is None         # <-- intent gone

In production B survives only because its ingress pile is still in pile/. That
premise is what poc-16-ilr removes on a shared bucket.
close_reason: Staged receipts now survive rebuild/root-CAS loss, remain hidden behind the published root, and retry on a later explicit turn even without an ingress pile; crash and shared-writer tests cover the boundary.

title: Separate root content identity from provider CAS tokens
description:
Port the publisher from its current content-hash pseudo-ETag interface to the
provider-neutral contract in poc-16-sgg.

Today Publisher.root_base() computes h(raw), FsStore.etag() returns h(bytes),
_sync_index compares that value with meta['root'], and publish() requires the
CAS return value to equal h(candidate). This works locally but conflates two
independent identities:

  content digest: h(root bytes), used to stamp the derived SQLite snapshot
  CAS token: opaque value supplied with the exact root version read

Implement one atomic versioned root read. Publication plans carry both the
base root bytes and its opaque CAS token. CAS consumes only that token and
returns a typed applied/stale result; timeouts and 5xx-like unknown outcomes
must not be reported as stale. SQLite continues to store h(root bytes), so
_sync_index compares its stamp with the digest of bytes actually read rather
than a provider ETag.

The initial absent-root transition uses conditional create. The no-op path
verifies that the exact base token is still current. Recovery after an unknown
outcome rereads authoritative root state and either acknowledges already
represented intent or rebases without blindly repeating a stale mutation.

FsStore remains the local implementation: flock is a valid local refinement,
not a mechanism exported to S3/R2. Add file and directory fsync or explicitly
scope its durability guarantee in the contract and tests.

The change must preserve realistic concurrent Publisher, rebuild, post-CAS
crash, and stale-index tests. It must also make it impossible for a naive
adapter to substitute an ETag for a content hash at either boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Core obtains root bytes and an opaque token atomically, stores only the content digest as the SQLite snapshot stamp, passes only the opaque token to conditional replacement, and distinguishes stale from unknown outcomes. Existing FsStore behavior and post-CAS crash recovery remain covered. No caller compares a provider token to h(bytes).
notes:
The existing no-flock reproduction remains a valid proof that FsStore's implementation mechanism cannot be copied to separate hosts: two check-then-write calls both report success and one update is lost. It does not show that S3/R2 lack CAS; current providers offer conditional writes. The port must use provider If-Match/onlyIf. Two safe API designs exist: separate the opaque provider token from h(bytes), or translate value-CAS by atomically reading (body, provider token) and conditionally writing with that token. Prefer separation because the current root read already receives both and it avoids a second GET. Preserve h(root) only as logical snapshot identity and HTTP peer cache tag.
Unknown-outcome recovery is not safe until poc-16-ed1 preserves durable staged intent across rebuild/rebase. Remove store.digest entirely; hash bytes from one exact read. Also cover the rootless absent-stamp race poc-16-289.
IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending contract/conformance parent closure): typed opaque VersionToken/ABSENT/Applied/Stale, exact paired reads, no store.digest/etag, unknown CAS reconciliation, content-hash SQLite stamps, and realistic Publisher tests.
close_reason: Opaque provider tokens and root content digests are separated in running Publisher/FsStore/provider code with paired versioned reads, typed CAS outcomes, no-op token checks, unknown-outcome reconciliation, and concurrent/post-CAS tests.

title: A publication-time failure wedges the whole ingress queue and quarantines nothing
description:
CONFIRMED by reproduction during review.

core/runtime.py WorkspaceRuntime.turn quarantines exactly two failure classes:
decode_pile raising (runtime.py:41-43) and drain rejecting (runtime.py:45-49).
Everything after that -- _sync_index, merge, blob writes, commit -- is wrapped
in a bare `except Exception: node._restore_authoritative_state(ws); raise`
(runtime.py:59-61). The pile is only deleted on success (runtime.py:62).

So any input that makes settlement or publication raise DETERMINISTICALLY is
retried forever, and because turn() iterates piles in one loop and propagates,
it also blocks every other queued pile behind it.

Reproduced: with a permanent publication failure armed, two queued piles (one
poisoned, one perfectly healthy) both stay queued across repeated turns, zero
are quarantined, and every turn raises. Since daemon do_PUT, do_GET /root and
/poke all call turn(), the workspace stops serving.

A transient failure DOES recover correctly (verified separately: the pile is
retained, and once the fault clears it drains). The bug is specifically that
there is no distinction between "retry me" and "I will never succeed".

This is the amplifier that turns poc-16-xjk into a permanent remote DoS, and
it is reachable from a plain `PUT /pile` by any member (core/daemon.py:149-155).

Directions:
  - separate transient failures (RootChanged, store I/O) from permanent ones
    (any deterministic ValueError from settlement/publication) and quarantine
    the latter with the same failed/{pile,meta} machinery already in
    core/node.py:165-187.
  - make turn() continue to the next pile instead of aborting the loop, so one
    bad unit cannot block unrelated ones. Piles are described as independent
    closed units; the loop should treat them that way.
  - add a retry counter to the pile record so a pile that has failed N times is
    quarantined even if its failure looks transient.
notes: 2026-07-29 safety refinement: do not quarantine or delete a pile merely after N failures. Arbitrarily long throttling, outage, CAS contention, or an outcome-unknown response is not proof of bad input. Publication/store failures retain the pile. A permanent retirement must be backed by a typed, input-local invariant violation established independently of provider state; generic ValueError is insufficient because tree/resource errors and programming bugs may depend on the current root. The loop should restore per-pile state and continue with other independent work, but must ensure a failed pile's staged candidates cannot poison the next pile's settlement. Reusable probe: inject the same exception at every boundary before/after object create, root CAS, catalog stamp, rejection evidence write, and pile delete, then assert the ghost retirement obligation.
close_reason: Typed permanent rejection, exact durable evidence, staged-intent isolation, healthy queue continuation, retry retention, and shared-worker diagnostic lifecycle implemented and accepted. Broader performance/audit/fuzzing follow-ups remain explicitly open.

title: Attacker-ground fact ids force the treap past MAX_PAGE_DEPTH and stop publication
description:
CONFIRMED by measurement during review.

core/btreap.py priority is H(FORMAT, layout_seed, key) and the tree is a
Cartesian tree on (priority, key). layout_seed is public -- it is
h(canon(["composite-layout-seed-v1", anchor])) (core/indexes.py:56-58) and the
anchor is in every root. FactTree keys are "fact:"+fid, and a fid is the hash
of an envelope whose timestamp and body the author picks. So an author can
grind fids offline against a known seed.

Grinding fids to be co-monotone in (key order, priority order) degenerates the
Cartesian tree into a chain. Measured on a real workspace seed:

    D=30   ground depth 30    honest depth 10    27,382 hashes
    D=60   ground depth 60    honest depth 10   235,920 hashes
    D=120  ground depth 120   honest depth 12  1,699,876 hashes

Depth is exactly D. MAX_PAGE_DEPTH is 128, so roughly 130 ground facts and a
few seconds of hashing push the tree over the cap, at which point both
btreap.build (btreap.py:105-106) and btreap.update (btreap.py:282-283) raise
"btreap depth budget". Publication then fails deterministically for that fact
set, on every node that admits it, forever.

Chained with poc-16-kgp.9 this is a permanent remote denial of service: the
poisoned pile is never quarantined and blocks all other ingress.

The same grind applies to RangeTree, where the key is "<ts>:<fid>" and BOTH
halves are author-chosen, making it strictly cheaper.

Candidate directions (needs a decision, not a patch):
  - derive priority from a value the author cannot predict when choosing the
    fid -- e.g. seed the priority with something committed after the fid is
    fixed. Note this trades away history independence unless chosen carefully.
  - use a balanced structure whose depth does not depend on key entropy.
  - keep the treap but make over-depth a per-fact admission rejection rather
    than a publication-time abort, so one poisoned fact is refused at the door
    instead of wedging the snapshot. This is the smallest change and composes
    with poc-16-kgp.9.
Whatever is chosen, DESIGN.md's "bounded by the published depth and the hard
depth cap" needs to say who pays when the cap is reached.

title: F5: adversary-chosen-address resource fuzzer (grinding)
description:
Every address in this system is a hash of bytes the author chose, so every
structural property derived from those hashes is attacker-controlled at the
cost of a hash grind. Nothing currently tests that.

The grindable surfaces:
  - FactTree/SuppTree keys: "fact:"+fid, "action:"+sid (core/indexes.py:61-68)
  - RangeTree keys: "<ts:015d>:<fid>" -- BOTH halves author-chosen
    (core/shape.py:62-69)
  - treap priority: H(layout_seed, key), and layout_seed is public, derived
    from the workspace anchor (core/indexes.py:56-58)
  - leaf boundaries: int(fid[:8],16) % 64 == 0 (core/shape.py:77-80)

Fuzzer: an adversary that grinds fids to maximize each cost metric, plus
assertions that the metric stays bounded or fails gracefully.
  1. Tree depth. Grinding fids co-monotone in (key order, priority order)
     yields depth == number of ground keys, exactly. Measured during review:
     D=30 -> depth 30, D=60 -> depth 60, D=120 -> depth 120, versus depth
     10-12 for the same counts of honest keys. See poc-16-xjk.
  2. Leaf pile size. Grinding every fid to be a non-boundary (~1.02 tries per
     fid) puts unboundedly many facts in one home leaf. manifest._range
     re-encodes the whole pile on every insertion into it, so ingest becomes
     quadratic and one object grows without limit. There is no cap on pile
     size anywhere.
  3. Leaf count. Grinding every fid to BE a boundary (~64 tries per fid)
     makes every fact its own leaf pile plus closure sibling: maximal object
     count, maximal RangeTree size, maximal sync page count.
  4. Worker fetch count per mint (see poc-16-wmf).

Assert declared bounds exist and hold, and that exceeding one degrades the
offending request rather than the workspace.

title: F4: hostile-peer byte fuzzer over correctly-addressed objects
description:
Content addressing proves an object's NAME matches its BYTES. It proves
nothing about its STRUCTURE: a hostile peer computes the hash of whatever it
likes and serves it at that oid. Every structural check downstream of
verified_object is therefore a trust boundary, and none of them is currently
fuzzed.

Build a fuzzer that takes a healthy published store, and for each object class
produces structure-aware mutants, RE-ADDRESSES each mutant to its own hash so
every hash check passes, and serves it to a syncing node:
  - root bytes (core/manifest.py decode_root)
  - RangeTree pages and Worker tree pages (core/btreap.py _decode)
  - home-leaf piles (core/close.py decode_pile, core/manifest.py range_members)
  - closure siblings (core/sync.py _sibling_keys)
  - fact blobs (core/fact.py decode/from_json)
  - action evidence piles (core/suppression_state.py validate_evidence)

Mutations: field deletion and addition; type substitution (str<->int<->list<->
dict<->null); numeric extremes and non-canonical spellings; duplicate JSON
keys; very long strings; deep nesting; truncation; child oids pointing at
siblings, at ancestors (cycles), at themselves, at nonexistent objects, and at
objects of a DIFFERENT class (a fact blob served where a tree page is
expected); count/depth metadata that lies both high and low; separators that
are not valid fact keys; leaf piles whose members do not match their
separator.

Assertions for every mutant:
  - the syncing node never advances its root
  - the failure is a ValueError or a recorded sync failure -- never an
    unexpected exception type, never a hang, never unbounded memory
  - object fetches for the dial stay under a declared budget
  - the local store is unchanged apart from quarantine records

This target immediately catches two confirmed defects: poc-16-62e
(RecursionError escapes the codec doors) and poc-16-mjq (unbounded tree
enumeration on a remote root).
notes:
Coverage audit: there is NO byte-level fuzzing in the repo today. Exactly four
hand-written corruptions exist, each a single fixed mutation:
  objects[oid] + b" "                       tests/test_btreap.py:179
  a fetch returning None
  a leaf replaced by encode_pile([])        tests/test_props.py:152
  b"not the claimed object" for one evidence oid
                                            tests/test_suppression_state.py:433
Nothing flips bits, truncates, or splices fields at randomized offsets. Peer
responses are never fuzzed at all -- peer_for/LocalPeer always serve honest
bytes, and RemoteStore/Peer.objs are tested for batching and ordering only.

Good hand coverage already exists for: foreign manifest oid, injected
removals/globals, wrong layout stamp, missing composite trees, a missing
suppression slot failing closed, the subtree-graft attack
(test_pruned_subtree_is_still_validated_against_inherited_bounds), hidden or
misplaced facts, and poison piles. Add these specific holes to the mutant set:

  - a root whose trees[*]["count"] or ["depth"] disagrees with the actual page.
    _commit_facts asserts only the honest direction.
  - a FETCHED root claiming depth > MAX_PAGE_DEPTH. Today that is rejected at
    build time only; decode_root caps it (manifest.py:318) but the interaction
    with Reader's per-descriptor budget deserves a mutant.
  - a page whose left/right points at itself or at an ancestor. Reader.items
    has an explicit `seen` guard and neighbors is bounded by the page budget,
    but btreap.update's split/merge/insert/delete recurse over load() with no
    cycle guard -- worth confirming that is unreachable from remote bytes.
  - a manifest entry whose sep breaks sorted order.
  - an oversized page or pile driving unbounded memory (ties to poc-16-62e).
Extend the hostile correctly-addressed object corpus to failed/meta and failed/pile. Re-address malformed metadata so its key hash is valid, then vary schema, field types, source length, payload id/link, missing/wrong payload, record count, size, nesting, and cross-class substitution. Assert bounded deterministic status/audit failure and no false legitimate rejection row; tracked concretely by poc-16-itm.8.
Reusable witness-substitution method from F10: a content/hash-valid failed/meta record is still not a classification proof. Include semantic cross-class mutants that pair syntactically valid InvalidPile metadata with a valid pile and KernelRejected metadata with bytes whose family handler has a program failure; the destructive checker must deterministically reclassify exact bytes and reject both. Concrete checker fix tracked by poc-16-kgp.27; broader status hardening remains poc-16-itm.8.

title: F2: randomized N-writer convergence fuzzer against the real Node
description:
A seeded stateful fuzzer runs N in [2,6] real Node instances over one shared
F1 adversarial bucket, each with an independent SQLite catalog. It executes a
random operation mix with controlled interleavings and crash points: post,
remove, evict, invite/join, file send, sync dial, rebuild, and process restart.

Check after EVERY applied CAS, not just the terminal state:

  1. Complete closure: every object reachable from the root was acknowledged
     before the root CAS and is hash-valid.
  2. Placement: resident(root.manifest) re-derives byte-identical manifest
     bytes.
  3. Tree/fact agreement: all published authenticated trees equal a canonical
     full build of the logical rows implied by that same root's resident facts.
  4. Pinned readability: WorkerView decisions opened at root_k remain fully
     explainable by root_k alone after later commits.
  5. Linearizable history: replay each applied CAS at a point where its opaque
     expected token matched the current root. Do NOT assert global uniqueness
     of expected-token strings; A->B->A may legitimately reuse a token.
  6. Convergence: after fair retries, all nodes expose byte-identical roots
     equal to a serial rebuild from the union of durable surviving intents.
  7. Unknown-outcome recovery: a CAS that applied but lost its response does
     not duplicate, discard, or falsely retire intent.

Run the algorithm in the compliant atomic-CAS harness. Retain a non-atomic CAS
mode only as a mutation test proving the required law fails; it does not model
current direct S3 or R2, both of which offer conditional writes.

The fuzzer must shrink a failure to a minimal replayable script. Preserve the
existing working historical-root recompilation checker and ensure every writer
gets fair post-race turns so retry-of-a-retry schedules occur. Fixed seeds run
in ordinary CI; a separate long-soak command is opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed CI seed corpus and optional long soak run 2-6 real Nodes with independent SQLite catalogs over one compliant adversarial bucket. Every applied root is closed, placement-valid, tree/fact-equivalent, and independently Worker-readable; terminal fair retries equal a serial reconstruction. History replay proves CAS linearizability without assuming globally unique token strings. Failures shrink to replayable schedules.
notes:
Coverage audit: current concrete coverage has two writers and hand-picked pauses; no N>=3 retry-of-retry schedule, multi-turn stale index, index-ahead-of-store case, or pairwise gossip-to-quiescence. Real crash seams remain unswept inside the emit loop, between manifest and tree emission, and inside Publisher.stamp; existing crashes are Python exceptions rather than SIGKILL. A working historical-root checker already reconstructed 7/7 additive commits and 5/5 deletion commits in a virgin Node and reproduced byte-identical roots. Preserve it and check every commit, not only the final one. The atomic harness validates the algorithm under the required provider contract. A non-atomic harness is a negative control, not current S3/R2 behavior. Add ambiguous-success schedules separately: the root changes but the caller receives Unknown. Give every writer fair post-race turns. Invariant 5 is history linearizability, not uniqueness of ETag/token strings across ABA.
Add applied-then-superseded unknown recovery and X->Y->X value-ABA schedules. The durable-intent oracle must include locally staged receipts and owned ingress, and shrinking must preserve the unknown-response point.

title: F1: adversarial ObjectStore contract and failure harness
description:
Build tests/adversarial_bucket.py as the substrate for the shared-bucket
fuzzing program. It models the exact contract in poc-16-sgg, plus failure
outcomes that a compliant remote provider may expose.

Conforming mode must provide per-key linearizable reads and conditional writes,
strong visibility after acknowledged success, and opaque tokens unrelated to
content hashes. It injects independently and in combination:

  - a definitive stale conditional write;
  - an operation rejected before mutation;
  - create or CAS committed but its response lost (outcome unknown);
  - transport errors, throttling, and retryable service errors;
  - bounded LIST pages/cursors, short pages, and additions between pages;
  - opaque tokens, including token reuse/ABA schedules where permitted;
  - actor crash immediately before or after every linearization point.

The API must not collapse a timeout/5xx into the same value as a failed
precondition. Acknowledged object creation followed by invisibility, stale
successful direct GETs, two replacements of one unchanged CAS generation, and
object destruction are nonconforming mutation modes. Keep them as negative
controls that demonstrate which design law fails; do not describe them as
ordinary current S3/R2 behavior.

Cached custom-domain access and asynchronous replica reads are separate
unsupported adapters. A test may prove that routing authoritative reads through
either fails conformance, but the main harness must not weaken the direct API.

Reuse the deterministic gate/history machinery in tests/shared_bucket.py. Add
a reusable conformance suite exercised by FsStore, ScriptedBucket, the S3
adapter, and the R2 adapter. Provider-specific live tests are opt-in and belong
to the provider conformance bead, not ordinary CI.
acceptance_criteria: The harness deterministically explores opaque tokens, definitive conflicts, ambiguous create/CAS completion, transport failure, throttling, pagination, concurrent page changes, and crashes while preserving direct-read strong consistency in conforming mode. Separate mutation modes violate linearizability or visibility and prove the laws fail. Every schedule is seeded and replayable; FsStore and provider adapters share one conformance suite.
notes:
Coverage baseline: tests/shared_bucket.py is a strictly linearizable deterministic scheduler and tests/test_store.py exercises local POSIX atomicity. Preserve both. Extend the scheduler with typed Applied/Stale/Unknown outcomes and opaque tokens. Do not make a conforming direct-bucket mode return stale data: AWS S3 and Cloudflare R2 direct APIs are strongly consistent. Cache/replica modes are explicit nonconforming adapters. LIST coverage should target cursor pagination, page boundaries, concurrent insertions, and bounded drains rather than stale per-key visibility. The repository currently has no pytest marker/config scaffolding; add explicit unit/live/soak markers as part of this bead or poc-16-x1p.3.
High-value schedules from the token audit: atomic body/token pair reads; applied-response-lost and not-applied-response-lost creates/CASes; pending original CAS while another writer wins; hidden SDK retry after apply; token alias across different bytes as a negative control; 513+ short LIST pages; and real subprocess crashes at object-link/root-replace/post-CAS/pre-stamp boundaries.
close_reason: Accepted seeded adversarial ObjectStore harness: typed outcomes, exact linearization history, opaque ABA tokens, strong direct reads, bounded changing LIST, crash boundaries, negative refinements, and shared Fs/Scripted/S3/R2 conformance.

title: Shared-bucket adversarial test and fuzzing program
description:
Goal: prove that N concurrent writers and readers against one shared object
store cannot produce a broken root, an invalid tree, a divergent replica, or a
wedged node -- and that a hostile participant cannot make any of those happen
cheaply.

Why now: the current concurrency evidence is one abstract BFS model
(tests/shared_bucket_model.py, 2 writers + 1 reader over a 2-branch toy
snapshot) plus a handful of hand-scripted 2-writer scenarios in
tests/test_shared_bucket_node.py. Both are honest-participant, fixed-schedule,
and fixed-topology. Nothing randomizes the schedule, the writer count, the
operation mix, or the bytes. Manual probing during this review found three
confirmed defects in under an hour, all of which a fuzzer in this program
would have found automatically.

Scope of the program:
  F1  adversarial object-store harness (the substrate)
  F2  randomized N-writer convergence fuzzer
  F3  tree differential fuzzer (incremental vs full)
  F4  hostile-peer byte fuzzer
  F5  adversary-chosen-address resource fuzzer
  F6  kernel context differential fuzzer
  F7  widen the abstract model to N writers and the real snapshot shape

Definition of done: each fuzzer runs a fixed seed corpus in CI within the
existing suite budget, plus a long-soak entry point; every fuzzer shrinks a
failure to a minimal reproducible schedule/input and prints it.

title: Delete the legacy removal index and all post-seal dual paths
description:
## Background
Shadow migration is temporary. Keeping the monolithic removal object, fingerprint, full-object sync, globals, decoder, or dual Worker path after S5 would preserve the complexity the cutover exists to remove.

## Scope
After the fenced conversion seals, delete legacy removal-slot serialization, fingerprint comparison, pull_removals, removal globals, full-view authorization, shadow double writes, and runtime compatibility decoding.
design: Retained immutable migration evidence remains certifiable, but no legacy decoder or publisher remains callable after the seal. A rebuild-forcing format break is preferred to dual reads.
acceptance_criteria: Existing deletions survive the atomic cutover; post-seal source contains no authoritative removals oid/fp slot, pull_removals path, legacy removal globals, or fallback Worker consult; old-format roots fail closed or require explicit re-anchor; mutation tests prove no deletion gap and no old writer can publish.
close_reason: Current-format suppression actions are admitted and published without the legacy removal index or dual decoder.

title: Use one bounded B-treap and one composite-root publisher
description:
## Background
Three authenticated indexes and multiple publication paths can multiply codecs, page logic, and atomicity bugs.

## Scope
Implement one generic capped uniquely represented B-treap codec for FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree and one composite-root publication transaction.
design: Tree differences are typed key and value codecs plus caps, not separate balancing or page implementations. One CAS publishes all component roots and certification metadata.
acceptance_criteria: All three indexes use the same tree implementation; randomized, forward, reverse, incremental, and bulk construction of equal logical rows under one layout seed produce byte-identical pages and roots; capacity failures occur before publication; a fault between component builds cannot expose a mixed root; no independent component HEAD is authoritative.
close_reason: Fact, Suppression, and Authority indexes share core/btreap.py; canonical construction and one root CAS are covered by permutation, incremental/bulk, budget, fault, and root tests.

title: Keep reverse action lookup derived and Worker reads rebuild-free
description:
## Background
A second authoritative removal-fid index duplicates evidence, while rebuilding SQLite or scanning facts on every Worker request is unbounded.

## Scope
Keep removal-fid reverse lookup as a local rebuildable cache over canonical ActionRecords and make Worker authorization use only bounded exact FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree reads.
design: The reverse database is never part of root identity or authorization. It may update incrementally and rebuild out of band after deletion or corruption.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting the reverse database and rebuilding yields identical audit rows; a stale or absent reverse database cannot change authorization; Worker tests enforce an exact lookup budget and fail if code scans FactTree, reads removal evidence by fid, or rebuilds SQLite during a request.
close_reason: Implemented persistent authenticated trees, derived reverse projections, and extracted tree/Worker/action modules; covered by the green runtime suite.

title: Simplify family policy into one executable registry
description:
## Background
Suppression selectors, direct action targets, one-time authorization guards, and continuing authority liveness are currently spread across prose and handler conventions.

## Scope
Create one typed executable family-policy registry consumed by authoring, admission, certification, and Worker lookup. Keep handlers declarative and eliminate duplicate policy lists and generic dependency inference.
design: Every registered family has exactly one policy record. Handler modules may expose family-specific construction and validation, but no second table may redefine selector, direct-target, or liveness policy.
acceptance_criteria: Registry coverage tests enumerate every registered family; SELF, Parent, Ancestor, NEVER, DIRECT_TARGETS, AUTHORIZATION_GUARDS, and AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS use named resolved edges; deleting or duplicating one family policy makes a named test fail; simple OWNER and ADMIN delete handlers validate through ordinary needs and offers; no caller-supplied owner or naked suppression id is accepted.
close_reason: All 18 registered families are covered by one executable policy registry consumed by kernel admission and content actions.

title: S4: Build shadow capped trees and the bounded Worker lookup library
description:
Background: the monolithic removal object is O(n) per change; a secondary-index miss alone cannot prove completeness; the probabilistic fact manifest leaves Worker membership unbounded; full minting must detect omitted committed authority without rejecting a fresh request signature or rebuilding SQLite; existing valid facts can contain large bodies and deep authority; and replacing the legacy removal slot before backfill would resurrect deleted content.

Scope: build the uniquely represented B-treap codec for FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree; pin layout_seed; store bounded FactRecords over unchanged chunked raw facts; create reserved suppression/action slots; derive shadow exact CLEAR/ACTIVE suppression values and exact/ANY authority rows; preserve the authoritative legacy slot/globals and feature-gate Workers; place local certification outside root identity; publish the shadow tuple through one CAS; diff by oid; and build TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint, and RevocationLiability support for S5.
design: S4 is storage shadow mode, not semantic cutover. Legacy slot/globals remain authoritative. FactTree contains bounded proof records and reserved ActionSlots; SuppTree has one exact SuppSlot per admitted sid; AuthorityTree serves bounded canonical providers and preserves empty keys as NO_PROVIDER. TargetRegistry and AuthorityImpactRegistry are service-side certification support, not Worker trees. Shadow certification reports deep legacy authority, computes conservative fixed-key revocation liability, and supports zero-provider MemberPrincipal receipts without enabling them before S5. Equal logical sets under one seed must yield byte-identical pages and roots.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection around B-treap builds and shadow CAS never drops legacy deletion state; S4 bounded grants remain disabled and distinct cert keys retain byte-identical roots. An existing oversized message keeps its fid through raw-fact chunks without changing its fid; deep legacy authority yields exact checkpoint input. Golden vectors build the same set forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk and prove identical pages. Every page, tree row, ActionRecord, root, proof, lookup, ordinary-insert, fixed-value-update, and 867-subrequest bound is executable. A maximum ExactSids spec remains out of line and its ActionSlot pointer fits 512 bytes. At most 7 proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; only afterward does its receipt EvidenceRef produce the maximum 8-ref ActionRecord, and a self-digest cycle rejects. Exact SuppSlot hit and absence authenticate CLEAR/ACTIVE or fail closed on a missing reserved key; no prefix or removal-fid Worker index exists. Dropping suppression, action pointer/evidence, authority, TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, future escrow, service reserve, admit-cell byte reserve, either legacy map, migration-seal object/byte reserve, attempt reserve, certificate reserve, pending isolation, or liability prevents certification. Support stages complete bundles outside ordinary keys, validates TargetBinding, separates at most 8 evidence FactRecords, 13 total base logical records, one base tree path, 64 effects, and a fixed-point union of 64 transitive authority consequences, and retains terminal liability. Ordinary publication updates impact scopes and rejects consequence 65. Revocation caps at 129 fixed paths and 1,032 copied pages. Attempt fencing uses fixed scratch keys, live-generation gateway checks, definitive write-lease drain, and a pre-CAS next-certificate claim. Worker lookup never scans or rebuilds SQLite and I4 remains until S5. Full suite passes. Shadow certification reconstructs complete AuthorityCandidateRegistry values, rejects candidate 65 for one NeedKey, and selects fallback or NO_PROVIDER from at most 64 candidates without scanning FactTree. Across 64 affected NeedKeys a removal examines at most 4,096 refs. It also proves migration seed derivation is acyclic and separately charges TargetRegistry and AuthorityCandidateRegistry rows/bytes. Shadow certification accounts independently for LegacyIamAttestation objects/bytes and per-publisher served-cell/inclusion-witness rows/bytes, rejects an absent or undersized mandatory slot, and exercises maximum legal 80-byte keys in ActionRecord/tree capacity fixtures. Shadow vectors retain one unpublished fid in several publisher inventories and converge on the same lowest-origin row/digest in every enumeration order. Migration sizing includes normal ActionSlot(Sid) plus SuppSlot structural backfill for a legal quarantine-only target, not only LegacyMask Migration slots. Shadow whole-cutover capacity preflight derives a provider-signed LegacySourceCeiling, proves the complete first-root manifest fits both canonical occupancy and a disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope, and fails while S4 remains writable if either is short. It distinguishes the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and never assigns a layout seed or exact namespace before the frozen snapshot. Shadow preflight persists content-hash-matching CapacityCeiling and LegacySourceCeiling objects and charges their rows/bytes. Before each retry it reruns whole-cutover sizing and pins a fresh bootstrap/fallback pair while the current S4 generation remains writable. Shadow certification rederives candidate scopes only from declared liveness guards and rejects closure-wide candidate masking. Whole-cutover preflight charges every generation-staged service row/byte, proves each bounded batch plus the constant-size final activation, and fails while S4 is writable if any dimension or operation cap is unavailable. title: S1: Harden the removal-index door and recover poisoned ingress
description:
## Background
The removal index can permanently poison a workspace because malformed closure keys reach inconsistent parsers, published-slot decode sits outside its guard, and a failing ingress pile replays forever.

## Steps to Reproduce
Admit a fact with a negative or ambiguous timestamp key and a deletion whose removal closure references it; turn, restart, rebuild, and sync a peer. The index encode/decode disagreement prevents publication and the same pile retries indefinitely.

## Scope
Reject malformed address keys at admission, make published-slot decode fail closed, quarantine or retire poison without replay loops, surface sync failure state, and align all key parsers.
design: This repair is independent of the new suppression format and must not add compatibility decoding.
acceptance_criteria: Real hostile-input tests cover malformed, ambiguous and negative timestamp keys at local ingress and remote sync; restart and rebuild recover; an unrelated valid pile continues; status exposes the failure; mutation of each guard makes a named test fail; full suite passes. The fact-address door accepts only a non-boolean integer timestamp in 0..999999999999999 plus exactly 64 lowercase hex fid characters, yielding one 80-byte canonical key. Negative, boolean, 16-digit-positive, explicitly signed, whitespace-padded, uppercase and ambiguous-colon forms reject before Fact or index admission; boundary tests use FACT_TS_MAX.
notes:
Review closure 8 makes fact-key width a door invariant rather than assuming Python's minimum-width :015d formatter is a maximum.
Review closure 11 distinguishes the new strict key door from sealed legacy state: an existing out-of-range key is reported and causes writable S4 fallback or explicit re-anchor, never silent drop or rekey.
close_reason: Exact fact-address validation, isolated durable ingress quarantine, guarded published-index decode, surfaced sync failures, and hostile restart/sync tests are implemented; full suite passes.

title: S2: Freeze suppression, authorization, receipt, and bounded-proof contracts
description:
## Decision

Every registered family declares NEVER or an exact SELF/Parent/Ancestor suppression policy, a DIRECT_TARGETS matrix, and separate named AUTHORIZATION_GUARDS. SELF expands only after fid integrity. New facts structurally create every required exact SuppSlot and the reserved ActionSlot for any directly targetable sid or principal. Removal admission only fills existing fixed-width values. The three request-time trees use one uniquely represented B-treap whose priority and iterated weight-leader layout are pinned by layout_seed. Admission uses a separately provisioned service-exclusive key and workspace.body.pk is forbidden. Each Worker-authorizable role declares a compositional worst-case ProofBudget.

## Rationale

Explicit type ownership distinguishes cascade parents from incidental references. Exact CLEAR and ACTIVE slots let a Worker answer by fid without scanning removal evidence. Preallocation makes an already-admitted target removable without future structural insertion. A second authoritative removal-fid tree would duplicate evidence without serving the Worker. Unique representation makes equal logical state converge to equal page bytes independent of insertion order.

## Alternatives Considered

A suppression tree ordered by (sid, removal_fid) requires a prefix query and can structurally split during a later revocation. A second tree ordered only by removal fid duplicates evidence and serves no Worker authorization query. Rebuilding SQLite from the full fact tree on each request is unbounded. A conventional B+tree is insertion-history-dependent; globally repacking it after each write is unbounded. Synchronously releasing descendant liabilities makes ancestor removal proportional to descendant count.

## Scope

Freeze the exhaustive family matrix; selector, guard, target, SuppSlot, ActionSlot, receipt, service-key, capacity-envelope, B-treap, NeedKey, proof-budget, and Worker lookup encodings. Land callable skeleton APIs plus realistic named contract and golden-vector tests before bodies.
design: No implementation body starts before this decision and its skeleton contracts land. One workspace-global admission/publication service serializes cap-compliant roots. FactTree ActionSlots point at immutable action evidence; SuppTree has exactly one preallocated CLEAR or ACTIVE value per sid; AuthorityTree retains keys with NO_PROVIDER. A local reverse removal-fid database is cache only. Fixed-key removal updates are distinct from bounded ordinary structural insertions.
acceptance_criteria: The family matrix covers every registered family with NEVER or exact SELF/Parent/Ancestor, DIRECT_TARGETS, independent AUTHORIZATION_GUARDS, and per-authority-offer AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS. Hostile selector and target tests reject naked sids, wrong paths, inherited-selector direct actions, absent slots, and a founder admission key. Canonical shapes cover SuppSlot, fixed-oid ActionSlot, bounded out-of-line ActionRecord, pre-receipt proof_refs, post-receipt EvidenceRef, TargetBinding, ExactSids, MemberPrincipal, LegacyMask, LegacyUniverseMap, LegacyEntryMap, LegacyMigrationSeal, MigrationBootstrapCommitment, CapacityCeiling, LegacySourceCeiling, CutoverCapacityEnvelope, S5CutoverBinding, CutoverObjectManifest, CutoverServiceManifest, CutoverServiceGeneration, TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint, BaseRevocationRecords, RevocationActionBundle, PublicationAttempt, AttemptWriteLease, CommittedAdmission, AdmissionCommitProof, CapacityEnvelope, PendingCapacityEnvelope, ContentCapacityEnvelope, and RevocationLiability. A maximum ExactSids ActionRecord with at most 7 proposal/support proof refs plus exactly one receipt ref fits 16 KiB while its ActionSlot fits 512 bytes. Golden construction vectors prove proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt before the receipt EvidenceRef determines the ActionRecord; a self-digest cycle rejects. BaseRevocationRecords has at most 13 logical records and only one base tree path. Exact SuppSlot reads authenticate CLEAR and ACTIVE and fail closed on a miss. Golden vectors prove forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk construction yield byte-identical B-treap pages under one layout_seed. Every exact binding has unspent liability; the independent terminal reserve survives per-fid masking. Complete transitive authority impact is capped at 64. The post-commit signer accepts only durable stored rows and a failed-CAS orphan receipt never certifies. Effects and consequences are separate from base records; removal is at most 129 fixed-key paths and 1,032 page objects, while ordinary insertion is at most 13 keys times 17 pages (221 pages). Capacity encodings separately charge admit cell count/bytes, both legacy maps, one capped migration-seal object/bytes, retained bootstrap/final-binding objects, certificate objects/bytes/write leases including one pre-CAS next-root reservation, and leased-root retention/reclaim rules. The pre-fence source ceiling and whole-root cutover staging dimensions are disjoint from the later single-operation attempt reserve. Fresh exact and ANY NeedKey, compositional budgets, bounded FactRecord and chunked raw bytes, three isolated quotas, and per-fid screening are pinned; full suite remains green with only explicit body skips. Canonical shapes also cover cutover_basis_digest, AuthorityCandidateRef, and AuthorityCandidateRegistry. Golden dependency vectors order logical universe rows, basis digest, candidate seed, LegacyUniverseMap root, then final cutover_digest and reject the cyclic derivation. A NeedKey has at most 64 complete candidates, one action examines at most 4,096 refs, fallback never scans FactTree, and capacity encodings charge TargetRegistry plus AuthorityCandidateRegistry rows and bytes. Pin FACT_TS_MIN, FACT_TS_MAX, MAX_FACT_KEY_BYTES, MAX_LEGACY_IAM_ATTESTATION_BYTES, MAX_SERVED_CELL_BYTES and MAX_INCLUSION_WITNESS_BYTES. Specify and golden-test the retained LegacyIamAttestation object and the served-cell/inclusion-witness row-and-byte CapacityEnvelope dimensions; the maximum ExactSids ActionRecord uses only longest legal keys. Freeze LegacyUniverseRows so PUBLISHED wins and otherwise the lowest verified publisher id is the single bounded quarantine origin; conflicting fact/derived bytes abort. Freeze distinct normal Sid and LegacyMask Migration owner-slot shapes for grandfather backfill. Existing-workspace migration retains capped canonical CapacityCeiling and LegacySourceCeiling preimages by oid; after restart a certifier content-hash-verifies and decodes them, then compares the exact CapacityEnvelope componentwise against the ceiling vector rather than against a digest. Candidate sorted_action_scopes derive only from exact family-declared continuing liveness guards on canonical proof-DAG authority edges; incidental support and one-time admission guards never become ambient revocation policy. Capacity shapes charge canonical root/frontier/active-generation cells and the retained cutover generation descriptor, while CutoverCapacityEnvelope separately charges inert service-row staging and pins bounded batch and activation work. Raw-content contracts distinguish raw_root_oid from the running envelope fid, use monotonic ContentCommitPin epochs for post-ABORTED retry, declare the cutover pin-generation state machine, and cap ordinary structural publication at 13 paths and 221 pages. Canonical shapes and hostile vectors also cover LegacyActorAdmissionRecord, LegacyActorAdmissionCommitProof, ActorAdmissionEvidence, AdminSubject, AdminAuthorityRef, key-signed DevicePrincipal target eligibility, and rejection of current-state legacy owner reconstruction.
notes:
Offering a selector means the fact may be suppressed; it grants no direct action. V1 content exact actions select SELF, while user/device revocation uses authenticated family-declared MemberPrincipal or DevicePrincipal scopes; parent and ancestor selectors only propagate. AuthorityImpactRegistry is a monotonic conservative superset including losing and fallback provider closures; only authority_consequences(action) is the exact fixed-point change set. PublicationAttempt carries a never-reused generation and OPEN, SEALING, ABORTING, or COMMITTED_COPYING phase. Publishers have no metadata-write credential. A manifest-bound gateway writes only fixed scratch slots under durable AttemptWriteLease records. Sealing drains definite write outcomes and CAS charges canonical occupancy before authority-exclusive copies. Existing removal keys are fixed-value updates with MAX_TREE_PAGES_PER_VALUE_UPDATE equal to depth; ordinary B-treap inserts use the separate prospective cap. V1 never walks descendants to release liability. Ratchets retain the post-commit signer, failed-CAS orphan receipt, target-specific liabilities, and terminal reserve.

Authority candidates are proof-closure identities, not only provider fids: candidate_id binds NeedKey, provider and proof_closure_digest. MASKED stores the deterministic minimum effective action witness, so equal logical state is arrival-order independent.

Review closure 12 splits the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and adds a separately provisioned whole-corpus CutoverCapacityEnvelope/CutoverObjectManifest. Review closure 14 separates continuing AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS from proof closure and one-time authorization, and adds the bounded, generation-staged CutoverServiceManifest/CutoverServiceGeneration path.
Review closure 15 freezes CommitBinding DirectRoot versus CutoverGeneration, CutoverPayloadManifest, CutoverCommitAnchor, its retained capacity fields, and MAX_ACTION_IMPACT_SCOPES=65. AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS expand only from the candidate-producing edge plus explicit FollowAuthority paths. guard_actions(Sid) uses effective_actions so a MemberPrincipal or DevicePrincipal action masks that provider candidate in either arrival order.

Review closure 17: AuthorityCandidateRef has mandatory sorted_provider_sids distinct from AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS; provider suppression always masks its candidates, while NEVER contributes no provider sid. Review closure 20 contracts: AuthorityProofRecord caps exact fact bindings/ordinal edges and is rooted by each candidate ref; FactTree ADMITTED rows never disappear on suppression, shadow, or projection quarantine, while membership alone never proves eligibility.
Review closure 21 freezes acyclic AuthorityProofRecord and post-hash candidate-rank shapes; RequiredCoOffer is a sorted exact component of NeedKey and all candidate/impact indexes; LegacyDisposition distinguishes ORDINARY, EFFECT_SOURCE, EFFECT_EVIDENCE, and INERT_REMOVAL; LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint binds source_candidate_id, proof-record oid/digest/depth/cost, and both exact source scope sets.
Review closure 21 supplement: freeze capped LegacyAuthorityProofRecord page/manifest encodings and capacity dimensions for over-budget source preimages. Review closure 22: LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint refs use certified LEGACY_SOURCE_RANK(source proof depth, source fid, source candidate id), never the flattened checkpoint proof/provider, preserving mixed native/legacy winner order. Principal-provider, authority-candidate, and authority-impact registries store content-addressed bounded RegistryValueObjects behind 256-byte atomic pointers. title: S3: Implement explicit suppression selectors and dependency-closed masking
description: Background: direct-only deletion leaves attachment chunks projected and makes live/rebuild state diverge. Scope: implement SELF/Parent/Ancestor resolution, named dependency and guard-source validation, family author helpers, exact hostile-wire admission, compositional ProofBudget validation for new state, migration reporting for sealed over-budget legacy providers, many-to-many local victim rows, one mask for live/rebuild/ingress, and dependency-closed file deletion while the legacy removal slot remains authoritative through S4.
design: A deletion targets an explicitly bound, family-approved offered key. Every exact proposal references the target fact and names the selector token; admission recomputes TargetBinding and rejects naked or inherited capabilities not in DIRECT_TARGETS. Direct and group removals enumerate local victims through the same supp table. Authorization guards are computed separately and are never offered by a NEVER fact. No read-time graph walk and no generic inheritance from all deps.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a file retracts descriptor and chunks live, rebuilt and cold-joined; deleted blobs are no longer demanded; SELF is non-circular; missing/extra/non-ancestor/NEVER selectors and guard substitutions reject; multi-parent diamonds deduplicate. Every exact removal recomputes its target ref, target-family DIRECT_TARGETS permission, selector token and sid; naked sids, wrong refs and inherited parent/member selectors used as direct device/content targets reject, while removing the ancestor by SELF still cascades. Selector and winner-independent role budgets hold for newly authored state; every current family derives bounded proof-only metadata; the 519-hop legacy chain is reported for S5 LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint rather than rejected before S4; oversized new Worker-authorizable proofs reject; the attachment-bearing suppression theorem passes without waiting for S5 receipts; full suite passes.
notes:
S3 enforces MAX_FACT_RECORD_BYTES and compositional proof caps for new Worker-authorizable facts. Oversized raw content retains the same fid and uses S4 chunks. Existing valid recursive authority remains available on S4 and is surfaced to the fenced S5 checkpoint migration.
Review closure 2: the family matrix adds PRINCIPAL_TARGETS. Device revoke derives DevicePrincipal(pk) from an authenticated target FactRecord and masks every matching current/future provider; a naked pk or exact SELF-selector shortcut is rejected, while the authenticated self-bound device FactRecord may be the capability target. Duplicate valid device facts with distinct labels/timestamps are the required regression.
Review closure 11 caps family-declared terminal scopes per fact and makes a later membership+device provider consult both committed typed tombstones before choosing one canonical SuppSlot witness.
Application policy closure (review-corrected): the exhaustive family matrix declares DELETE_OWNER or NEVER and normalizes each directly deletable target to DeleteOffer(content.delete, SELF, OwnerBinding). A bare device_invite is membership/grant evidence, never ownership consent; only a durable target-key-signed DeviceOwnerConsent exposes a DEVICE actor edge. Actor classification checks for any admitted shape-valid direct-member claimant, including masked claimants, before considering a consented device edge. OWNER and ADMIN remain separate conjunctive proposal modes; NEVER and families without a matching DIRECT_TARGETS row emit no delete offer.
Independent review closure 27: the target matrix says a bare device_invite is never a DevicePrincipal target. Only the target-key-signed self-bound device row or DeviceOwnerConsent creates that action; once legitimate, the key-wide action still masks every invite/provider for the key.
Independent review closure 28: device_invite offers exact SELF to device.grant.delete so its retained owner or any live admin can retract that one provider without the invited key. This is distinct from DevicePrincipal: it neither expands to same-key providers nor pre-tombstones the key.
close_reason: Explicit SELF/PARENT/ANCESTOR selectors, exhaustive family policy, owner/admin deletion, dependency-closed masking, blob-demand suppression, hostile-wire tests, and the attachment-bearing theorem are landed and the full suite is green.

title: Post-cutover recovery: explicit suppression keys and indexed Worker reads
description:
## Background

The 2026-07-27 audit and design discussion supersede the previous open bead frontier. docs/TODO.md is the sole temporary implementation plan.

## Scope

Deliver explicit type-owned suppression offers and separate live authorization guards; immutable service-signed removal admissions; uniquely represented capped FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree B-treaps; exact preallocated SuppSlots and reserved ActionSlots; service-exclusive, capacity-checked atomic composite-root publication in an IAM-isolated metadata namespace; bounded Cloudflare Worker reads; poisoning recovery, product commands, ingress screening, regression coverage, performance repair, and documentation consolidation.

## Bankruptcy rule

Closed bead history is preserved, but every previously active bead is retired as superseded. No requirement survives unless docs/TODO.md restates it and a child of this epic owns it.
