design: docs/TODO.md is authoritative. Facts explicitly offer SELF, Parent, and Ancestor suppression selectors or NEVER, independently of authorization guards. Workers exact-read one preallocated SuppSlot per selector; a certified CLEAR or ACTIVE value is sufficient and a missing slot fails closed. Actions fill reserved FactTree ActionSlots with one fixed-width ActionRecord oid; full target specs live in capped immutable ActionRecords. There is no second authoritative removal-fid tree; a reverse audit database is rebuildable cache only. All request-time trees use the anchor-pinned uniquely represented B-treap layout. S4 retains legacy authority in shadow mode. S5 cuts to the service-exclusive IAM namespace, preserves legacy effects without granting illegal current DIRECT_TARGETS authority, and certifies isolated control, pending, and content envelopes plus conservative RevocationLiability before bounded Worker reads.
acceptance_criteria: All children derived from docs/TODO.md complete with realistic tests. S4 preserves legacy deletions while shadow-building byte-canonical B-treaps and reserved suppression/action slots. Equal logical states under one layout_seed have byte-identical pages and roots in every construction order. A maximum ExactSids target spec, at most 7 pre-receipt proof refs, and exactly one post-receipt self ref fit a capped out-of-line ActionRecord while its fixed pointer fits one 512-byte ActionSlot; the proof digest authenticates the proposal/support refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization and never includes the receipt that it determines. BaseRevocationRecords is capped at 13 logical records but only one base tree path. S5 authenticates the frozen published-plus-quarantine legacy universe with root-bound LegacyUniverseMap and a separately capped LegacyMigrationSeal object, atomically enables commit-proof-derived ActionSlot and SuppSlot value updates, and removes legacy slot/globals only after revoking and draining legacy metadata writers. Every durable admit cell has both an object count and MAX_ADMIT_CELL_BYTES reserve for its full signed receipt; both migration maps and the seal have object/byte capacity. Illegal legacy direct-target pairs use victim-specific LegacyMask, and zero-provider globals precreate their principal ActionSlot. ExactSids and MemberPrincipal remain terminal and capacity-safe. AuthorityImpactRegistry caps the exact fixed-point transitive NeedKey consequence union at 64. PublicationAttempt uses monotonic generation fencing, fixed scratch slots, definitive write-lease drain, precharged canonical copies, and a pre-CAS next-certificate reservation. Certificates for current and leased roots are charged and reclaimed only after their last served-root lease or witness is fenced/released. Fixed-key revocation uses at most 129 changed paths and 1,032 page objects; ordinary insertion is separately capped at 13 times 17 pages. Descendant liabilities are not synchronously released. Pending and content quota exhaustion cannot consume control/revocation capacity, and direct admission bypasses a full optional pending pool. Workers use bounded exact reads without rebuild or per-hit evidence fetch. Malformed, cyclic, under-reserved, orphaned, unwritable, or uncertified state fails closed. Full black-box and mutation suites pass; README.md and DESIGN.md become the surviving records. Review closure 7: legacy migration derives layout_seed from layout-independent cutover_basis_digest before LegacyUniverseMap root and final cutover_digest. AuthorityCandidateRegistry caps each NeedKey at 64 candidates and each action at 4,096 pre-indexed refs, pairs atomically with AuthorityImpactRegistry, and forbids fallback scans. TargetRegistry and AuthorityCandidateRegistry both reserve row and byte capacity. Review closure 8: the migration fence revokes and definitively drains every legacy metadata writer before hashing the legacy universe; the first S5 root retains a capped, content-addressed LegacyIamAttestation with verifiable provider evidence. Fact addresses have an exact 80-byte canonical door with bounded 15-digit timestamps, and the maximum ActionRecord fixture uses that boundary. Every publisher preallocates row and byte capacity for its served cell and inclusion witness, and publication proves those slots plus the next witness before CAS. Review closure 9: LegacyUniverseMap chooses PUBLISHED or the lexicographically lowest verified publisher origin for a multiply retained fid, independent of inventory enumeration order. Fenced backfill precreates the normal Sid owner ActionSlot and SuppSlot for every legal grandfather target, including a quarantine-only victim; LegacyMask uses its distinct Migration owner only for illegal current target pairs. Review closure 12: existing-workspace cutover authenticates a provider-signed pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment that contains no snapshot-derived values, then a root-bound post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding. A physically disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope stages the complete first-root corpus; PublicationAttempt remains post-cutover and single-operation.
notes:
S5 is a coordinated workspace cut owned by the service-exclusive admission/publication authority. FactTree stores bounded FactRecords plus preallocated ActionSlots; SuppTree stores one exact CLEAR or ACTIVE SuppSlot per admitted suppression id; AuthorityTree retains fixed NeedKeys with NO_PROVIDER when empty. The key set plus pinned layout_seed uniquely determines B-treap pages. TargetRegistry and AuthorityImpactRegistry support certification and publication, never Worker reads. RevocationLiability reserves base records, up to 64 effect value updates, the fixed-point union of up to 64 authority consequences, path-copy pages, and durable service rows. V1 releases only directly named action liabilities and never enumerates descendants. CapacityEnvelope and ContentCapacityEnvelope are physically and IAM isolated. Publishers have no metadata-write credential; a generation-gated gateway writes only fixed scratch slots. AdmissionCommitProof is minted only after rereading committed cells. Worker reads remain 100 routed lookups and 867 cold-cache subrequests.
Review closure: ActionSlots contain only fixed ActionRecord oids; MAX_ACTION_RECORD_BYTES carries maximum target specs. PendingCapacityEnvelope is a third physically isolated quota. Fenced backfill precreates principal/migration slots, and a legacy normal selector is reused only when its exact current DIRECT_TARGETS pair is legal and resolves to the old victim.
Review closure 2: Device revocation is DevicePrincipal(public_key), a typed key-wide terminal tombstone covering every current and future device-provider fid; an exact SELF-selector shortcut is not the revoke action, although a key-signed self-bound device FactRecord can authenticate the DevicePrincipal target. SuppSlots contain one deterministic canonical witness, while every overlapping committed action keeps its own filled ActionSlot. CapacityEnvelope separately charges FactRecord and raw-fact-chunk objects/bytes for proposals, support, signatures, and receipts.
Review closure 3: ActionRecord roots a bounded EvidenceRef list through FactRecords to raw chunk trees, so sync/restart/GC cannot lose proposal, signature, support, or receipt evidence. The first S5 root also binds a frozen paged LegacyEntryMap: each old slot entry maps to one canonical lowest-fid action, while duplicate entries are evidence rather than impossible second receipts.
Implementation closure: PrincipalProviderRegistry is a capped exact service-side set of membership/device provider fids, maintained atomically with ordinary publication. Principal actions enumerate this set without a FactTree scan; Workers never read it.
Review closure 4: Separate MAX_ACTION_EVIDENCE_REFS=8, MAX_REVOCATION_BASE_RECORDS=13, and MAX_REVOCATION_BASE_TREE_PATHS=1; fixed-key publication is p+m+c <= 129 paths and 1,032 pages. The first S5 root authenticates LegacyUniverseMap plus LegacyEntryMap under LegacyMigrationSeal so quarantine-only reingestion cannot trust a naked fid or mutable inventory. CapacityEnvelope charges certificate objects/bytes/write leases, reserves the next certificate before CAS, and reclaims an old sidecar only after the last served-root lease/witness ends.
Review closure 5: CapacityEnvelope charges admit_cells plus admit_cell_bytes for the complete retry receipt. LegacyMigrationSeal has its own bounded object/byte dimensions and fixed 4 KiB cap; the potentially unbounded registered-publisher attestations are individually capped rows in LegacyUniverseMap, not inline seal data.
Review closure 6: proof_refs contains at most seven proposal/support refs; those refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt. Only after the receipt fid and FactRecord/raw root exist does ActionRecord evidence append its one receipt EvidenceRef, for eight refs total. Hashing that self ref into proof_digest is a rejected content-hash cycle.
Review closure 7 breaks the cutover digest/seed cycle with a logical LegacyUniverseRows digest and adds the bounded forward authority-candidate index missing from the reverse impact map. TargetRegistry terminal escrow now includes bytes, not only rows.
Review closure 8 closes the old-writer snapshot race, bare IAM-digest retention, mandatory serving-metadata quota, and unbounded fact-key findings.
Review closure 9 closes nondeterministic duplicate quarantine provenance and the absent normal owner-slot path for quarantine-only grandfather targets.
Review closure 10 breaks the LegacyMask content-hash cycle: the pre-record legacy_mask_namespace comes only from fenced legacy source state before any migrated FactRecord or LegacyUniverseRows digest, and LegacyMigrationSeal binds it beside the final cutover digest.
Review closure 11 adds the writable S4 abort generation, aggregate proof transport cap, complete multi-scope tombstone witness rule, explicit root-bound layout seed, and publisher-count-independent root publication.
Review closure 12 splits the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and adds a separately provisioned whole-corpus CutoverCapacityEnvelope/CutoverObjectManifest. Snapshot-derived seed and namespace values never appear before the drain; the normal PublicationAttempt pool never stages the first S5 root.
Review closure 13 retains canonical capacity/source ceiling preimages for restart-safe comparison and provisions a distinct writable S4 successor before every retry fence.
Review closure 14 derives authority masks only from declared continuing liveness guards and activates a pre-staged service generation with a bounded root/frontier transaction.
Review closure 15: grandfather CommittedAdmission rows use only CutoverGeneration(service_generation_id); a bounded activation-tail CutoverCommitAnchor binds the already-computed root/frontier/descriptor and pre-root certificate reservation, so descriptor-bound service rows contain no root hash cycle. Sid liveness uses effective_actions, and principal actions query both terminal and affected provider-Sid impact scopes, making candidate masking arrival-order independent.
Review closure 16: ordinary DirectRoot admissions retain an atomic admit-cell/CommittedAdmission DirectCommitPair that alone regenerates proofs after the live root advances, old root GC, restart, and passive-cache loss. Worker minting must execute the request-family ephemeral gate with service-trusted time and preserve request.VERBS plus expiry checks before grant.
Review closure 17: every authority candidate carries mandatory sorted_provider_sids in addition to family-declared liveness guards, so a suppressed provider—including a LegacyMask victim—cannot remain LIVE. Migration freezes a LegacyEffectCensus before any migrated FactRecord, retains its authenticated proof closure plus the exact chunked reconciled-S4-root preimage, and binds both oids in the seal/root. authorize_serve atomically claims a fixed WorkerReadLease that holds the exact root/certificate through all reads and any root-bound grant. Raw revocation liability charges eight FactRecord envelopes but only the 56 KiB aggregate proof plus one 32 KiB receipt.
Review closure 18: every live TargetBinding and PrincipalBinding carries target_fact_record_oid, and ActionRecord reachability pins each exact target FactRecord/raw root independently of the eight admission EvidenceRefs, so quarantine and historical-root GC cannot erase selector-policy evidence. Cutover converts old effects while the S4 decoder exists, then seals a service-signed S5-native LegacyTranslationAttestation; post-seal certification hash-checks the retained S4 preimage but never imports the old decoder.
Review closure 19: terminal-principal expansion retains a capped PrincipalProviderBinding for every provider, roots each exact FactRecord/raw closure through quarantine, and keeps quarantined providers charged against the terminal provider cap.
Review closure 20: every authority candidate roots a bounded content-addressed AuthorityProofRecord containing its exact FactRecord bindings and ordinal proof edges; S5 FactTree is a grow-only ADMITTED archive, so ordinary facts survive canonical-provider quarantine and historical-root GC without trusting local quarantine bytes.
Review closure 21: AuthorityProofRecord hashes only closure digest, ordinal-DAG depth, and cost; candidate id and canonical rank are derived after its oid. NeedKey includes the complete canonical required-co-offer tuple. LegacyDisposition keeps inert/effect removal proposals out of ordinary FactTree slots, and each LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint binds one exact source candidate, proof-record oid, closure digest, and flattened liveness scopes.
Review closure 21 constructibility supplement: deep legacy checkpoint sources use paged LegacyAuthorityProofRecord manifests/pages charged by the signed legacy ceiling and cutover envelope; the 64-fact AuthorityProofRecord cap remains the Worker bound. Candidate refs carry the exact co-offer match state so selection-before-requirement can yield NO_PROVIDER without falling through.
Review closure 22: LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint refs use certified LEGACY_SOURCE_RANK(source proof depth, source fid, source candidate id), never the flattened checkpoint proof/provider, preserving mixed native/legacy winner order. Principal-provider, authority-candidate, and authority-impact registries store content-addressed bounded RegistryValueObjects behind 256-byte atomic pointers. NeedKey/co-offer and reverse-value bytes are capped. Every live target carries an AtomicCommitBudget; publication rejects before upload unless the complete 162-object/44,630,016-byte registry set, attempt manifest, and at-most-193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction fit. Mandatory mutations: checkpoint-reranks-legacy-candidate, inline-registry-values-overflow-atomic-commit, unbounded-authority-impact-value, and unbounded-required-cooffers.
Review closure 23: Worker suppression reads only the request fact selectors, the selected provider selectors, and that family edge’s declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS/FollowAuthority scopes; incidental proof support, unselected edges, and one-time authorization guards confer no liveness authority. BaseOfferNeedKeyRegistry and AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry give symmetric bounded discovery: a new full NeedKey finds all retained providers, and a new provider updates every admitted full NeedKey for each exact/ANY base, recording COOFFERS_MATCH or COOFFERS_MISMATCH without a FactTree scan. Atomic publication now charges at most 162 registry value objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction. Boundary fixtures use distinct target/evidence records and a 128-edge unique acyclic proof DAG. Required mutations: worker-suppresses-all-proof-evidence, provider-scans-or-omits-full-needkeys, and unclaimed-recovery-epic.
Review closure 24: authority proof admission is immutable once a CommittedAuthorityProof and post-commit AuthorityProofCommitProof bind the exact admission-basis proof; later canonical-winner changes do not re-resolve it, and only mandatory provider selectors plus declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS may mask it. Authority records separate bounded transport depth/cost from logical proof depth; NEED/REF descendants of a LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint propagate source depth with DERIVED_LEGACY_RANK. Ordinary raw facts use a separately sealed paged RawFactContentCommit in the isolated content envelope, so the fixed metadata PublicationAttempt carries one commit reference rather than every chunk. Required mutations: reresolve-admitted-proof-against-current-winner, checkpoint-descendant-uses-transport-depth, and inline-raw-fact-chunks-overflow-publication-attempt.
Review closure 25: AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry is discovery-only and stores no full candidate id or winner rank; every exact full NeedKey derives its own candidate id/rank, including legacy checkpoint tie breakers. Each base candidate value enforces a 64-scope union in both provider-first and NeedKey-first order. Raw manifests bind chunk ordinals and byte ranges, RawFactContentCommit identity excludes upload generation, and a strong ContentCommitPin transitions PENDING to ROOTED with metadata CAS; only a fenced ABORTED pin is collectible, while cutover uses a paged pin set plus bounded anchor. A fact that both consumes and provides authority is budgeted for 162 registry objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction including the pin transition. Required mutations: reuse-base-rank-for-full-needkey, late-needkey-multiplies-candidate-scopes, sort-raw-manifest-by-chunk-oid, content-generation-in-canonical-commit, and collect-sealed-content-before-metadata-cas.
Review closure 26: raw_root_oid authenticates the complete canonical fact bytes, while the running codec recomputes body hash and envelope fid; raw JSON hash is never substituted for fid. Deterministic ContentCommitPins use monotonic epochs so a fenced/drained ABORTED attempt can become a higher-epoch PENDING retry before re-upload without ABA. Cutover content lifetime uses an explicit STAGING/SEALED/ROOTED/ABORTED generation row, paged set, and atomic root anchor. Ordinary publication budgets 13 structural inserts and 221 prospective pages. Required mutations: hash-raw-bytes-as-fid, aborted-content-pin-blocks-retry, and collect-sealed-cutover-generation.
Final independent review after closure 26 reported no discrete actionable defects. Validation: 49 focused repository-layout tests and 345 full-suite tests passed, with one planned skip.
Independent review closure 27 settles the remaining ownership edges: legacy target ownership requires admission-time committed evidence, device-wide tombstones require target-key consent, and device-targeted admin grants remain key-scoped while owner-admin use is an explicit separate proof.
Independent review closure 28: a bare device_invite offers exact SELF only to device.grant.delete, letting its retained owner or an admin retract the grant without cooperation while never creating a terminal DevicePrincipal tombstone. Every receipt authenticates a service-derived ActionAuthorization containing the exact action-time actor binding and, for ADMIN, exact scoped admin provider/proof. S4 records device-signed contextual S4_DEVICE_INVITE_ACCEPTANCE as a non-reusable per-target compatibility basis; the successful target CAS atomically debits every record, commit-row, proof-slot, proof-object byte and proof-lease dimension.
Independent review closure 29: LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint identity uses legacy_authority_checkpoint_namespace derived only from fenced S4 source bytes, never cutover_digest, so migrated owner FactRecords are constructible before LegacyUniverseRows and the seeded map root. S4 invite fallback requires a device signature over workspace, target, owner and exact invite; the ordinary target signature is insufficient. Historical CommittedAuthorityProof timing governs one-time guards, and an ambiguous pre-recorder delegated-admin grant with a removed grantor blocks S5/requires re-anchor. Actor shadow capacity is debited atomically with a winning target CAS; losing attempts fence, drain and reclaim scratch without consuming the cell.
Independent review closure 30: fenced LEGACY_SLOT and LEGACY_GLOBAL receipts use a non-callable GRANDFATHER(LegacyEffectAuthorizationRef) bound to the exact LegacyEffectCensus row and old source, so valid S4 cross-user deletions survive without being falsely labeled OWNER/ADMIN and LIVE_GUARDS can never choose it. Every first-publication or on-demand authority closure is separately committed and post-commit-proved before a LegacyActorAdmissionRecord may cite it, including a preexisting provider and an alternate closure; finite S4AuthorityProofCapacityCell accounting is idempotent and a losing proof CAS consumes nothing. LegacyActorAuthorityTransport preserves the record original authority ref while a distinct authenticated CHECKPOINT transport binds and replays its exact paged source proof/candidate into the new checkpoint provider; the future checkpoint identity never overwrites the S4 record.
Independent review closure 31: ActionAuthorization verification is action-scoped for LIVE_GUARDS and grandfather actions, outside the direct-target OwnerBinding branch, so terminal MemberPrincipal/DevicePrincipal and LEGACY_GLOBAL actions cannot bypass it. Proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; the later receipt EvidenceRef only determines ActionRecord. S4AuthorityProofScratchSlot and S4ActorAdmissionScratchSlot precharge object/byte/write-lease capacity before upload, preserve disjoint scratch plus canonical coexistence after a winning CAS, and fence/drain every losing attempt before reuse. An actor closure above the native proof bound is committed and post-commit-proved before the target CAS as PAGED_S4(S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef) over the canonical LegacyAuthorityProofRecord; cutover reuses that exact source to construct CHECKPOINT transport instead of inventing migration evidence later.
Independent review closure 32: S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef retains the paged proof oid as well as its strong commit id, so certification and GC never scan for the sidecar. A pre-fence bounded authority proof keeps its immutable DirectRoot commitment/proof through cutover; only a never-committed closure may receive CutoverGeneration, and a second row at the deterministic id aborts. S4 actor/proof canonical balances are workspace-global, initialized once, and never refill across fallback generations; an abort drains and rebinds only the separately precharged scratch pool while preserving both canonical cells byte-for-byte. Fixed row/proof caps and retry ratchets cover all three failure modes.
Independent review closure 33: AuthorityProofCommitProof is deterministically addressed by authority_proof_commit_id and a committed row with a missing sidecar takes restart recovery, never a conflicting cutover rewrite. Each paged S4 proof has an atomically RESERVED/FILLED S4PagedAuthorityProofSlot; its ref retains the filled proof oid, and restart deterministically recovers the sidecar before any target or cutover may cite it. The workspace-global actor/proof capacity cells have deterministic ids, retained capped envelope preimages, explicit cell/slot row-and-byte charges, and scratch-only fallback handoff. Final independent review reported no actionable findings; 51 repository-layout tests and 346 non-network tests passed with one planned skip.
close_reason: Bankruptcy recovery is implemented end-to-end and verified by 208 passing tests.

title: Make the ingress-retirement obligation oracle workspace-bound
description: The workspace-anchor cutover updated production decode_pile and Fact construction but missed the independently developed F10 obligation checker/tests. tests/ingress_obligations.py calls decode_pile(raw) without the authenticated workspace, poison helpers omit workspace, and hostile Fact fixtures omit ws. As a result the full suite reports decoder program failures and leaves every valid pile obligation live, so the destructive-retirement proof tests no longer test production behavior.
design: Thread the exact trace workspace into every oracle decode and construct every hostile fact/pile under that same anchor. Preserve the intentional malformed property while making ambient-workspace mismatch impossible. Update the static delete-call line ratchet only after re-running its AST inventory.
acceptance_criteria: All F10 publication, lost-CAS, pagination, rejection, recreation, and static-delete inventory tests pass after workspace binding; at least one mutation still demonstrates that wrong-workspace bytes cannot discharge an obligation.

title: Model root CAS conflicts and ambiguous retirement deletes in staging
description: The staging corpus now erases actor state and covers crashes after validate, promote, durable root commit, pile delete, and object delete, but it does not yet model a competing root CAS winner, an unapplied/ambiguous CAS result, or an ambiguous DELETE response.
design: Compose promotion histories with the shared-bucket CAS token model and F10 ObligationTrace. Reconcile an unknown CAS against authenticated root bytes before retirement; treat DELETE outcome as unknown until exact pile read-back; preserve idempotence under a competing publisher.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded histories cover CAS win/stale/unapplied/applied-response-lost and pile/object DELETE applied-response-lost. Only a read-back authenticated root discharges the exact pile, concurrent winners converge, and every first failure has a minimized replay.
notes: Implemented as a refinement, not a stronger abstract event oracle: real Node/Publisher creates authenticated root bytes over AdversarialBucket opaque tokens; ObligationTrace decodes manifest and every WorkerView tree before pile discharge. Eight bounded seeded cases cover win, stale competition, definitely-unapplied CAS, applied/lost CAS with cold actor read-back, and before/after ambiguous pile/object DELETE. core.object_store.retire_exact is the shared running exact-value/read-back primitive; its create-only/body-bound address precondition is checked at Node's pile call boundary. Weak CAS-attempt and unknown-DELETE controls retain replayable first failures.

title: Split broker mint authorization from provider-visible PUT authority
description: The design corpus currently presents workspace, member, object class, and digest as independent UploadRequest fields even though an S3/R2 PUT sees only endpoint, bucket, key, headers, conditions, and bytes. A combined model can accidentally claim that a provider enforced issuer-only metadata.
design: Model two refinements: a broker mint request/policy that validates workspace/member/class/digest and derives an exact key, then a provider wire PUT whose authority is only its actual signed URL, path, headers, expiry, condition, and body. Bind semantic metadata through the derived key or explicitly signed metadata values; run mutations at the correct boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove issuer swaps cannot mint a capability, wire mutations cannot exceed the minted capability, no oracle credits a provider for invisible fields, and live adapter tests inspect the actual signed request surface.
notes:
Implemented the credential-free split model in tests/direct_upload_method.py. BrokerMintRequest carries only pinned MintAuthorization plus canonical descriptor bytes; BrokerImplementation checks pinned workspace/member/evidence, active membership, descriptor commitment/canonicality, workspace/member agreement, class/digest/size/type, then derives the exact key and signed PUT values from trusted provider configuration. WirePut contains only endpoint, method, bucket, key, actual headers, credential expiry/time, and body; WirePutCapability represents only verified signed provider claims. Object issuer identity is deliberately erased at this boundary, while pile member identity is bound by the derived key. Field-inventory, seeded broker/wire mutation, planted-weak-policy, issuer-swap, replay, collision, and missing-signed-claim tests ratchet the split. The abstract-body-sha256 claim remains symbolic contract-model vocabulary, not S3/R2 evidence. Actual presigner/query/header inspection remains in x1p.3, x1p.17.1, and x1p.17.7.
Self-review found a second broker-only invariant: equality to pinned authority is insufficient before path interpolation. The model now requires workspace to satisfy core.shape.valid_fid and member to be exactly 16 lowercase hex characters, even when malformed values carry otherwise accepted model evidence and match the descriptor. Authenticated slash-bearing workspace/member cases plus weak-policy controls prove omission can escape the derived prefix.
Final local validation on codex/upload-wire-authority: focused direct-upload gate 58 passed; full repository gate 650 passed, 2 expected skips. git diff --check clean before export. Live provider evidence is intentionally not claimed by this closure and remains required on linked open beads.
close_reason: Split the design corpus into canonical broker-mint and provider-visible wire-PUT boundaries; seeded positive, mutation, replay, planted-negative, issuer-erasure, signed-surface, and path-shape tests pass. Linked open provider beads retain actual presigner/live evidence.

title: Erase process state at every direct-upload crash boundary
description: The first staging model called the retry through the same closure and retained process-local rooted state, so a cache-only publisher was indistinguishable from one that reconstructs from durable storage. This is a general false-positive mode for serverless crash tests.
design: Crash metamorphism by process-state erasure: give every suffix a fresh actor generation, retain only explicitly modeled bucket/root values, and require safety plus eventual progress from those durable values. Plant a cache-only-root candidate that must fail.
acceptance_criteria: Every crash case records distinct actor generations, root-crash retirement occurs in a later generation from a durable root commit, a cache-only root cannot justify retirement, and the failing seed/prefix replays.
notes: Implemented by promotion_history actor generations. A crash-after-root trace commits the abstract durable root in generation 1 and retires in fresh generation 2; PromotionImplementation(durable_root=False) is a planted cache-only negative that the retirement oracle rejects.
close_reason: Fresh actor generations reconstruct from durable bucket/root state; cache-only root negative is rejected and crash boundaries replay.

title: Preserve non-target constraints in capability mutations
description: A one-field negative control can be falsely reassuring when it also violates another enforced constraint. The first body-binding mutant changed body length, so an implementation that ignored SHA-256 still rejected it on size and the corpus appeared to prove a body check it had not exercised.
design: For every nominally one-dimensional authority mutation, preserve all other constraints exactly. The body-binding case flips one byte without changing length; coherent multi-field substitutions remain separate cases. Keep an intentionally weak implementation for each dimension and require the corpus to report that dimension in its first failing seeded trace.
acceptance_criteria: The unchecked-body negative control fails on a same-length key/body mismatch, the exact implementation rejects without storing bytes, the full mutation inventory remains seeded and replayable, and a test ratchets coverage of every authority dimension.
notes:
Implemented in tests/direct_upload_method.py: key-body-mismatch flips one byte while preserving length, while body-checksum-substitution remains a separate coherent multi-field case. tests/test_direct_upload_method.py plants ignored-body and exact-state negative controls and ratchets full dimension coverage plus deterministic replay.
Final ratchet also handles empty bodies without a length-changing false negative: a standalone abstract binding-algorithm mutation exercises the body check while preserving zero length. Extra signed constraints are accepted as safe tightening; missing required conditions fail. Every authority dimension has an ignored-policy negative control.
close_reason: Constraint-preserving same-length and zero-length binding mutants plus per-dimension weak-policy ratchets pass in the direct-upload corpus.

title: Method: inventory every production ingress-delete call site
description: Reusable F10 coverage ratchet: statically walk the running core AST and enumerate every ObjectStore-style delete call whose argument is an ingress source. Require all such calls to remain centralized behind Node._retire_ingress_exact, then exercise that seam through both valid committed-root discharge and typed-rejection discharge with the same ghost-obligation checker. A new direct deletion path must fail CI before it can bypass the proof obligation.
acceptance_criteria: The AST inventory reports exact file/function/line identities, fails on any new ingress-source delete outside the one reviewed retirement seam, and tests demonstrate that every current caller of that seam is covered by either committed-root or durable-rejection trace evidence. The method has no string-only whitelist that silently accepts renamed/moved calls.
notes: Implemented as an AST reference inventory, not a call-only grep: it reports direct, aliased, and literal-getattr method capabilities with file/function/line/receiver/use. Production is ratcheted to the sole direct st.delete reference in Node._retire_ingress_exact and both callers are exercised through publication/rejection proof. Alias/getattr mutation fixture proves the inventory cannot be evaded by deleter = st.delete.
close_reason: AST capability inventory and both production proof callers are ratcheted, including alias/getattr mutation controls.

title: Diagnose intermittent second-invite join HTTP 500 in daemon blackbox
description: During the final full suite on codex/x1p-s3, tests/test_blackbox.py::test_alice_bob_carol returned HTTP 500 when Carol joined the second invite immediately after Bob joined the first (pytest temp run 3643; all three daemons were alive and logs contained no exception detail). The exact isolated test then passed in 10.49s, so this is an intermittent core/daemon failure rather than a deterministic adapter regression.
acceptance_criteria: Make the second-invite sequence reliably expose its server-side exception/response body, identify the race or transient failure, and add a deterministic regression test proving two immediate independent joins never produce an unclassified HTTP 500.

title: Deny version-specific ACL changes on authoritative S3 objects
description: The bucket guard denies s3:PutObjectAcl but AWS authorizes ACL changes to a request carrying versionId through the distinct s3:PutObjectVersionAcl action. A writer with that permission can alter read/access control for an authoritative root or object version without hitting the current deny.
acceptance_criteria: Both threat-profile policies deny s3:PutObjectVersionAcl on the exact root and obj resources; exact-action tests ratchet the versioned and unversioned ACL pair; documentation continues to state the ACL/Object Ownership boundary.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 2fce775: the authoritative metadata guard now denies s3:PutObjectVersionAcl beside s3:PutObjectAcl on the exact root/obj resources under both profiles; focused adapter/deployment gate passes (204 tests).

title: Deny ETag-preserving S3 encryption-key mutation
description: AWS UpdateObjectEncryption can change an existing object to a KMS key while preserving its ETag and checksums. A principal with s3:UpdateObjectEncryption can therefore make authoritative bytes unreadable to the gateway without invalidating the root CAS token or content identity checks.
acceptance_criteria: Both bucket-policy profiles deny s3:UpdateObjectEncryption on root and obj resources; tests ratchet the exact action/resource/principal mapping; the README identifies encryption and KMS administrators who can replace the guard as trusted.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 2fce775: the guard denies ETag-preserving s3:UpdateObjectEncryption on authoritative root/obj resources under both profiles, with exact-action tests and the KMS-admin residual boundary documented; focused gate passes (204 tests).

title: Method: validate cache validators through a standards-strict HTTP boundary
description: Handler dict-equality tests cannot reveal invalid entity-tag syntax or intermediary normalization. A reusable wire probe should cross daemon, Function URL, and workerd boundaries with an RFC-validating parser or strict proxy.
acceptance_criteria: The harness varies quoted strong tags, weak tags, whitespace, lists, duplicates, header casing, malformed validators, and 304 behavior across daemon/Lambda/Worker transports; it reports the first divergent parse and is linked to poc-16-x1p.10.2 without claiming provider CAS tokens are HTTP validators.

title: Fail host cloud-store startup on an incapable SDK
description: The new no-I/O SDK smoke is only an operator command. S3Store construction still checks Config endpoint-isolation incidentally but does not inspect the PutObject service model, so a host can start and serve reads with an old or patched botocore, then fail only on its first conditional publication. The same capability function should guard SDK-backed store construction before any provider client or workspace I/O.
acceptance_criteria: Constructing a non-injected S3/R2-S3 store invokes the provider-free capability check before client creation; a fake old service model fails startup with the missing fields named; injected test clients and provider-free imports remain unaffected.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 87ad8cb is 989ccef on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 87ad8cb: every non-injected S3/R2-S3 store runs the no-I/O Config/service-model capability check before boto3 client creation; a fake old model names missing IfMatch and records zero client calls; injected clients bypass the installed-SDK probe. 130 focused tests pass.

title: Deny unbounded S3 annotation mutation on authoritative objects
description: Current AWS docs expose PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation (up to 1,000 mutable 1 MiB sidecars per object) and ReplicateObjectAnnotation. Annotations do not alter the parent ETag or bytes, so the current bucket guard and byte/CAS tests cannot observe them. A publisher with annotation permission can attach large mutable metadata/cost to every authoritative root/object despite the declared mutation guard.
acceptance_criteria: The chosen bucket-policy threat profiles explicitly deny direct annotation put/delete on authoritative resources or document a deliberate trusted-principal exception; replication/configuration authority is classified; tests ratchet the current action names and README states the residual admin boundary.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit b53917c is a01bab0 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit b53917c after current AWS annotation-surface audit: direct PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation are denied on root/obj under both profiles; tests assert exact actions/resources/principals; docs explicitly retain ReplicateObjectAnnotation/config administrators as a residual boundary. 112 focused tests and cfn-lint pass.

title: Authenticate and bound shared rejection status records
description: Node.ingress_failures() treats shared failed/meta/* objects as durable evidence/status but reads them through the generic object ceiling, accepts any JSON dict, and does not verify that the key suffix equals h(raw), that the schema is exact, or that the referenced failed/pile/<id> exists and matches. Retirement remains safe because its writer performs an exact post-write read before delete, but a fabricated shared record can amplify status reads or masquerade as rejection evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Rejection metadata and linked payload reads have dedicated byte/count budgets; every meta key authenticates its exact bytes; the schema and field types are exact; the payload id/key/content link is verified; invalid or excessive records fail closed with bounded work and cannot appear as legitimate ingress failure status. Existing concurrently written valid immutable records remain deterministic.

title: Method: audit bead identity collisions across parallel worktrees
description: Reusable tracker-integrity probe: before accepting parallel worktree exports, compare each issue id's immutable creation identity (title/body/created provenance) across branches and reject one id with divergent origins. Also verify the union cardinality and all newly reported finding titles after reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A script or test consumes two independently exported issue sets, reports divergent same-id creations with both origins, and proves a collision cannot silently replace one finding. The agent handoff checklist runs it before main export.

title: Prevent concurrent worktrees from reusing and clobbering bead IDs
description: CONFIRMED during the provider/harness parallel run: one worktree created kgp.15 for the real-process crash-sweep method while another independently created kgp.15 for the shared-retirement diagnostic schedule. Reconciliation left only the latter, so a legitimate method issue silently disappeared and had to be recreated as kgp.23. Parallel agents must not overwrite distinct issue identities during export/merge.
acceptance_criteria: Document and automate a collision-safe parallel-bead workflow (or configure globally unique allocation); a realistic two-worktree test creates distinct children concurrently, exports/reconciles them, and proves both titles/descriptions/dependencies survive. Existing duplicate-id conflicts are detected and fail loudly rather than last-writer-wins.

title: Method: sweep real process exits across publication boundaries
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: run actual FsStore/Node code in a subprocess and terminate with os._exit immediately before or after an immutable-object create, root replacement, and the post-CAS/pre-catalog-stamp boundary. Reopen from a separate process and check durable state instead of treating an in-process Python exception as crash evidence. Every child has a finite deadline so a deadlock becomes a bounded failure.
acceptance_criteria: Real subprocess tests bracket immutable create and root replacement, terminate after applied root CAS before the SQLite stamp, reopen independently, and prove acknowledged bytes survive and root/catalog recovery converges. The probe times out a deliberately hung child.
notes: Recreated under a fresh id after concurrent worktree exports assigned kgp.15 to two different legitimate method findings. Close only after the F1 source commit is integrated on main.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted in main source commit 1f747aa: real FsStore/Node subprocess exits cover object/root boundaries and post-CAS/pre-stamp recovery with finite child deadlines; focused 88-test root review and agent full 502-test suite passed.

title: Clear loser diagnostics after shared ingress retirement
description: When one worker wins publication and retires a shared pile, a CAS-losing peer records a node-local ingress attempt error. Future turns iterate only live pile keys, so the peer never revisits that source and the diagnostic leaks indefinitely despite the durable obligation having succeeded. Reconcile node-local attempt rows against the conforming store's strong current pile/ listing; absence clears presentation state only and performs no destructive action.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic two-Node shared-bucket race leaves a loser diagnostic immediately after the CAS conflict, the winner retires the exact shared pile, and the loser's next strong-list turn clears the phantom diagnostic without issuing a delete or losing any live-pile error. Repeated races do not grow stale local status.
notes: Implemented reconciliation at the start of every turn from the already-required strong pile/ listing; extended the real concurrent CAS winner/loser test.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Method: smoke provider SDK capabilities before host deployment
description: Reusable discovery method: inspect the running botocore service model and Config surface before any bucket I/O so an old or distribution-patched SDK cannot reach deployment without conditional PutObject or endpoint-isolation support.
acceptance_criteria: A provider-free unit test plus an operator command prove PutObject IfMatch/IfNoneMatch/ChecksumSHA256 and Config.ignore_configured_endpoint_urls are present; failure names the missing capability and touches no bucket.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: README exact optional host SDK install and S3/R2 --store-config examples; provider-free capability module checks endpoint isolation and conditional/checksum model fields without bucket I/O and is reused by Lambda. 128 focused tests pass; actual boto3/botocore 1.43.51 smoke reports ok.

title: Document the optional host provider SDK install
description: The strict --store-config host path lazily imports boto3/botocore, but README setup installs only PyNaCl and pytest and never tells an operator which optional provider SDK is required. A host deployment therefore fails at startup after configuration, while local and Cloudflare paths intentionally do not need that dependency.
acceptance_criteria: README gives an exact optional install path and host --store-config examples for S3 and R2-S3 while ordinary local and Cloudflare imports remain provider-free.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: README exact optional host SDK install and S3/R2 --store-config examples; provider-free capability module checks endpoint isolation and conditional/checksum model fields without bucket I/O and is reused by Lambda. 128 focused tests pass; actual boto3/botocore 1.43.51 smoke reports ok.

title: Give ScriptedBucket has its own atomic gate and history event
description: F1 re-review found BucketHandle.has delegated to get, so a scheduled op='has' fault could never trigger and histories mislabeled HEAD-style existence checks as GET. This leaves one ObjectReader operation outside the before/after crash sweep and makes the advertised fault surface inaccurate.
acceptance_criteria: ScriptedBucket has records one atomic has event with its own before/after gates; replay validates the boolean against the exact state/token at that point; the F1 pre/post crash matrix covers has; transport faults scheduled for has are exact RetryableStoreError with no fabricated mutation outcome.
close_reason: has now has its own atomic gates, history event, replay rule, typed transport fault, and pre/post crash coverage.

title: Make ScriptedBucket unconditional put match the no-result store contract
description: F1 re-review found ScriptedBucket.put returned its newly assigned internal VersionToken even though FsStore, S3Store, R2S3Store, and the ObjectStore protocol expose unconditional non-authoritative put as a no-result operation. The fake-specific result could let code or tests depend on a capability unavailable from real providers.
acceptance_criteria: BucketHandle.put returns None while the history event still records the resulting token/state for replay; the shared conformance schedule asserts unconditional put returns None for FsStore, ScriptedBucket, S3, and R2 host adapters; existing history and Node tests pass.
close_reason: ScriptedBucket.put now returns None; sync and async shared conformance ratchet no-result put plus immediate visibility across implementations.

title: Avoid repeated full proof rebuilds for isolated failed staged receipts
description: The safe isolation fix excludes staged receipts from other piles, but the current implementation detects any disallowed staged fid and forces a filtered full proof rebuild for every later pile until the failed pile commits. A persistent provider/program failure can therefore amplify healthy ingress work even though it no longer corrupts standing or wedges the queue. Design a first-class per-intent staging boundary or incremental eligibility path that preserves exact retry ownership without rebuilding the entire admitted proof graph.
acceptance_criteria: With one permanently retryable staged pile and a long sequence of healthy independent piles, publication remains correct and work is bounded by the healthy delta plus explicitly affected authority; no failed candidate publishes through another pile and restart retains the failed intent.

title: Audit the full S3 authoritative-object mutation surface
description: A reusable policy review must enumerate operations that can alter authoritative bytes, visibility, ACLs, tags, versions, or lifecycle outcomes. Reviewing only PutObject/DeleteObject misses metadata mutations that can weaken availability or access without changing bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The policy harness maps each authoritative mutation action to an explicit deny or documented trusted-admin boundary under bucket-wide and single-publisher profiles; exact resources/principals are asserted and the audit is repeated when supported S3 actions change.
notes:
2026-07-29 re-opened: the live AWS S3 API now exposes PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation and ReplicateObjectAnnotation. The first audit enumerated ACL/tag/version/lifecycle actions but missed this newly documented mutation surface; method must ratchet against the current authoritative action inventory.
2026-07-29 final audit: current AWS permissions also split PutObjectVersionAcl from PutObjectAcl and added UpdateObjectEncryption, which preserves ETag/checksums while changing the KMS key. ReplicateObject, ReplicateDelete, ReplicateTags, ReplicateObjectAnnotation, and ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner are classified as the trusted replication-admin boundary rather than silently omitted.
close_reason: Completed the current-action-inventory ratchet in source commits a01bab0 and 2fce775: direct annotation, versioned/unversioned ACL, tag, delete, lifecycle, and ETag-preserving encryption mutations are mapped to exact denies; the five S3 replication actions are asserted/documented as the trusted replication-admin boundary. Focused gate passes (204 tests).

title: Differentially validate SAM inputs against Lambda runtime configuration
description: A reusable deployment probe should compare CloudFormation-accepted parameter domains and generated resources with the runtime adapter's validators and budgets, rather than testing a few happy-path YAML strings.
acceptance_criteria: CI parses/transforms/lints the SAM template, differentially exercises boundary-valid and invalid bucket/prefix/deployment/KMS/alarm values against runtime validators, and asserts timeout, IAM, output, alarm, and physical-key ceilings remain aligned.
notes:
Manual cfn-lint 1.53.3 passes the current transformed SAM template and runtime boundary tests pass, but transformed-template lint is not yet installed/codified in ordinary CI; keep open as the reusable method gap.
Final audit reran cfn-lint 1.53.3 successfully against deploy/aws_lambda/template.yaml and the integrated suite passed 551 tests with 2 expected live skips. Transformed-SAM differential CI remains unimplemented.

title: Probe bounded R2 reads through every Worker request route
description: Adapter-only size tests do not prove wrapper and callback layers preserve the bounded-read capability. A reusable request-boundary sentinel should fail if arrayBuffer is reached for route-specific N+1 metadata, including proof/tree fetches after a healthy mint root.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic Worker harness covers root, invite, single page, batch, and mint object-fetch paths; each returns its defined 413/503 outcome and an allocation-failing oversized R2 sentinel records zero arrayBuffer calls. Mint serves a healthy root and proves at least one oversized obj/* fetch was attempted.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Bound real-process crash probes so deadlocks fail CI
description: F1 review found that the new object-link/root-replace and post-CAS/pre-stamp subprocess probes called subprocess.run with check=False but no timeout. A durability or lock regression could therefore hang the entire test job instead of producing the bounded replay diagnostic the crash method exists to provide.
acceptance_criteria: All F1 crash subprocesses run through one helper with a finite default deadline; a realistic sleeping-child test proves expiration raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired promptly; the real crash-boundary probes still pass and report their exact exit codes.
close_reason: All F1 subprocess probes use a 10-second default deadline; a realistic sleeping child proves prompt TimeoutExpired behavior.

title: Probe fragmented response-body amplification at provider read boundaries
description: A reusable provider probe should vary legal response fragmentation independently of total bytes. Byte-limit tests using one or two chunks miss per-fragment memory/CPU amplification and accidental assumptions that read(n) fills n bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The deterministic harness drives a moderately large body as one-byte legal short reads, an exact body, early EOF, and N+1; it asserts bounded read requests, complete close behavior, correct bytes/errors, and is referenced from every streaming provider adapter that retains fragments.
notes:
The one-byte probe also exposed independent CPU amplification after contiguous accumulation removed retained-fragment memory. That concrete behavior is tracked separately as poc-16-x1p.1.11; closing this method bead does not claim the behavior fixed.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 1f9e645 is 408f72e on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 1f9e645: contiguous bounded accumulation plus a 64 KiB one-byte-fragment probe; 106 focused tests and the 496-test integrated suite pass.

title: Method: stress opaque LIST cursors across long and changing scans
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: force one-key and alternating short LIST pages, opaque cursors, a scan longer than 513 pages, a strict page budget, and an insertion between pages after the current cursor. Replay every page against the object-map history so pagination bugs cannot hide behind an all-at-once list fake.
acceptance_criteria: The seeded harness records and replays page input/output cursors, passes a 514-page bounded drain and a concurrent post-cursor insertion, fails at the configured page budget, and a repeated-cursor mutation is detected rather than looping.
close_reason: Implemented replayable opaque-cursor pages, short/514-page drains, strict budgets, concurrent post-cursor insertion, and repeated-cursor negative control.

title: Method: mutate a hidden SDK retry after an applied conditional
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1/provider review: wrap one logical conditional mutation so the first provider attempt applies, its response is hidden, and an internal retry repeats the unchanged precondition and returns stale. Run the shared conformance schedule against the wrapper to prove it detects the false-stale logical result. This guards SDK retry configuration as part of the ObjectStore refinement.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic negative control applies a CAS, internally retries the same precondition, reports the retry's stale result, and is rejected by the shared seeded conformance schedule with provider/seed diagnostics. Production mutation clients remain configured for one total attempt.
close_reason: Implemented applied-then-hidden internal CAS retry mutation; the shared seeded conformance schedule rejects its false-stale result.

title: Method: ratchet ObjectStore laws with explicit nonconforming refinements
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: keep direct-store semantics strong and expose opt-in mutation controls for acknowledged-write invisibility, stale successful reads, accepting one CAS precondition twice, token aliasing across different bytes, destructive immutable deletion, and repeated LIST cursors. Each control must make the history/conformance oracle fail, proving the positive tests are not vacuous. Cached and lagged replica readers remain separate read-only negative adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Every named nonconforming mode has a deterministic test that demonstrates the bad observation and is rejected by replay or the shared conformance oracle; the default harness still passes strong visibility and linearizable history; lagged sync/async readers expose no mutation surface.
close_reason: Implemented explicit failing controls for invisibility, stale reads, double-CAS acceptance, token alias, object destruction, repeated cursors, lagged readers, and exact fault taxonomy.

title: F14: race shared retirement against loser diagnostic lifecycle
description: Generate the schedule where independent workers list the same live pile, one publishes and retires it, while a CAS loser records retryable node-local status after authoritative restore. Advance each worker through later strong listings, new unrelated piles, restart-equivalent empty local state, and repeated races. The oracle separates the durable shared obligation from ephemeral per-worker diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable seeded two-or-more-worker probe proves: no diagnostic clears while its exact source remains live; a strong listing clears every diagnostic whose shared source is absent without another destructive action; restart and quiescence agree; repeated winner/loser races leave bounded local status. Emit a replayable schedule and integrate with the F10 ghost-obligation trace.
notes:
The first concrete real-Node regression extends tests/test_shared_bucket_node.py. This bead owns general schedule generation and shrinking across adapters.
Tracker-integrity note: an earlier close interaction on this same textual id belongs to the independently created process-exit method that was clobbered during parallel worktree reconciliation. That method now lives at kgp.23; this F14 issue remains open. See poc-16-506 and poc-16-d3f.

title: F13: differential staged-candidate and failure-taxonomy probe
description: Exercise the same independently closed piles under a reference serial schedule and under injected decoder, kernel, merge, object-create, root-CAS, stamp, restore, and retirement failures. Include two piles offering the same canonical address so a failed staged lower-fid candidate exposes leakage into a later healthy settlement. Compare roots, eligible facts, staged receipts, live piles, and rejection evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic seeds cover every typed permanent versus retryable/provider/program boundary and every before/after-commit phase. The implementation under test matches a serial oracle: only typed input-local failures retire to exact evidence; all others retain intent; disallowed staged candidates never alter a later root; successful retry converges byte-identically. Failures shrink to boundary, pile order, and conflicting address.
notes:
poc-16-itm.2 adds the first restart-backed two-pile regression. This bead owns the reusable cross-boundary differential matrix and shrinking rather than another one-off assertion.
poc-16-itm found and covers two taxonomy/isolation counterexamples: family exceptions swallowed into ordinary invalidity, and a failed staged receipt leaking into the next pile's forced rebuild. F13 remains open to generate and shrink these differentially against a serial intent oracle.
Additional concrete counterexample from poc-16-itm.7: monkeypatching the fact decoder to raise generic ValueError previously manufactured InvalidPile. Include exception-class mutation at each nested codec helper, not just the top-level decoder.

title: F11: inject exact-evidence retirement boundary faults
description: Generalize poc-16-itm.1's deterministic negative controls into a reusable destructive-retirement probe. Inject wrong/missing/raised/applied-but-lost outcomes at rejection payload create/read, typed metadata create/read, exact-source precheck, delete, and delete reconciliation. The oracle follows the pile hash ghost obligation rather than retry count or worker identity.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable helper runs each boundary before/after its linearization point against local and provider-fake stores, asserts that every deleted pile has byte-exact durable typed evidence, prints the first unsupported event, and is consumed by ingress tests plus the F10 history checker. Include source changed/missing and metadata collision negative controls.
notes:
The initial real-Node matrix lives in tests/test_ingress_hardening.py under poc-16-itm.1. This bead owns extracting and applying the method across every provider adapter; it complements, not duplicates, F10's history-level oracle.
poc-16-itm now supplies a concrete deterministic matrix at rejection payload write/readback, metadata write/readback, delete-before-apply, and delete-after-apply. F11 remains open to lift this matrix into the reusable adversarial provider harness and sweep every equivalent boundary.

title: F12: barrier-race shared rejection and retirement
description: Generalize poc-16-itm.3's two-worker same-pile schedule. Barrier independent Nodes after LIST, after immutable rejection evidence, and before DELETE; permute winner, lost delete response, already-retired observation, metadata coalescing, and a concurrently inserted unrelated pile. The schedule detects false node-local assumptions and mutable shared diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable seeded schedule runs two or more independent Nodes over one shared store, proves exact immutable evidence and one idempotent retirement under every barrier permutation, continues unrelated work, validates the F10 ghost trace, and emits a replayable history. Provider-fake and real-Node variants share the same oracle.
notes:
The first deterministic two-Node barrier regression is implemented in tests/test_ingress_hardening.py. Keep this broader method separate from the concrete shared-metadata defect bead poc-16-itm.3.
poc-16-itm now supplies a concrete two-real-Node barrier race over one shared malformed pile, proving immutable content-addressed evidence and idempotent exact retirement. F12 remains open for seeded schedule generation, crashes, and shrinking across wider shared-retirement histories.
Concrete review counterexample poc-16-itm.9: wall-clock metadata produced one content-addressed object per retry/worker. F12 must assert exact record cardinality under repeated same-obligation schedules, not merely nonempty immutable evidence.

title: Use RFC-valid quoted HTTP validators for root cache tags
description: Daemon and serverless gateways emit the SHA-256 root content tag as a bare ETag and compare If-None-Match by raw string equality. HTTP entity-tag syntax is quoted; strict intermediaries or clients may reject, quote, combine, or weak-prefix it, causing unnecessary transfers or broken conditional reads. This wire cache tag remains distinct from provider CAS tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Root responses emit one quoted strong entity-tag, Peer and every gateway parse case-insensitive ETag/If-None-Match syntax rather than stripping arbitrary characters, and weak/multiple/malformed validators fail conservatively. Real HTTP black-box tests cross daemon, Lambda adapter, and workerd with a standards-strict client/proxy negative control while the logical snapshot identity remains h(root bytes).
notes: Reusable discovery method: validate protocol headers with a standards parser or strict proxy, not only dict equality in handler tests. Vary quoting, casing, weak prefixes, whitespace, duplicate/list syntax, and 304 behavior.

title: Make ScriptedBucket an exact opaque-token ObjectStore refinement
description: The F1 cross-implementation conformance lift found that ScriptedBucket derived its purported opaque CAS token from the value hash, implemented read_versioned as a get followed by token reconstruction instead of one atomic pair read, and rejected legal non-root conditional-create probe keys. Those shortcuts prevent the shared harness from detecting torn value/token reads and from running the same conformance schedule as FsStore and provider adapters. Refactor the existing deterministic history store to assign seeded opaque value-ABA tokens, read bytes/token under one lock and one history event, replay the token-to-bytes law, and accept the provider-neutral conditional-create surface while retaining authoritative-key guards.
acceptance_criteria: The shared conformance schedule passes against ScriptedBucket; a versioned read is one atomic history event; tokens are not content hashes and may safely repeat only for the same bytes; history replay rejects token aliasing across distinct bytes; existing deterministic Node schedules remain green.
close_reason: ScriptedBucket now assigns seeded opaque value-ABA tokens, atomically pairs bytes/token in one read_versioned event, accepts the provider-neutral conditional-create surface, and passes shared conformance.

title: Choose a rate-limited front door for the public Cloudflare Worker
description: Application grants protect workspace data, but the public Worker route still permits unauthenticated invocation, CPU/subrequest consumption, plausible-mint R2 reads, and availability or spend exhaustion. Body/query/fetch ceilings bound one request; they do not rate-limit a caller or preserve capacity for legitimate peers.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate Cloudflare rate limiting rules, WAF/custom rules, service bindings, Access, or another deployable front door against peer compatibility and application grants. Seeded hostile-request probes measure Worker CPU, R2 subrequests, platform throttling, and cost at the exact per-request ceilings, then prove the selected deployment rule limits abuse without turning ordinary peer churn into denial. Keep provider-only policy outside core and document remaining trusted account controls.
notes: Reusable method: distinguish per-request complexity ceilings from cross-request admission. Replay a valid-looking mint corpus at increasing concurrency and account separately for Worker invocations, R2 reads, denied requests, and legitimate tail latency.

title: Choose a rate-limited front door for the public Lambda Function URL
description: Application grants protect data but Function URL AuthType NONE permits unauthenticated invocation, concurrency exhaustion, plausible-mint Secrets Manager and S3 reads, and spend. Reserved concurrency and alarms bound or observe blast radius but do not rate-limit callers or preserve legitimate availability.
design: Keep this separate from data authorization. Do not claim alarms or reserved concurrency are preventive rate limiting.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate AWS_IAM, CloudFront plus WAF, API Gateway, or another deployable front door against client compatibility and application grants. Hostile-request probes measure invocation, secret/S3 read, throttling, concurrency, and cost behavior and prove the selected design rate-limits abuse without locking out legitimate peers.

title: Strictly reject malformed Function URL query encoding
description: urllib parse_qs accepts malformed percent escapes and replacement-decoded invalid UTF-8 while the Cloudflare edge parser is strict, creating cross-runtime request-boundary drift.
design: Validate percent triplets on raw ASCII, then parse with strict UTF-8 errors and bounded field count.
acceptance_criteria: Before gateway I/O, Lambda rejects lone or short percent escapes, non-hex escapes, and percent-decoded invalid UTF-8. Tests cover %, %2, %GG, and %FF plus one valid UTF-8 encoding while retaining byte and field ceilings.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bound attacker-controlled Lambda failure telemetry fields
description: Structured failure logging includes the raw Function URL method and path even though the record claims a bounded fixed shape. A public caller can force oversized log events and cost amplification without leaking a body or token.
design: Prefer short route classes plus bounded ASCII method/path fragments; do not log headers, query strings, exception messages, or request bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Every attacker-controlled field is classified or truncated to an explicit byte-safe ceiling. Exact-limit and one-over method/path tests prove the serialized record stays bounded and query, token, body, and workspace data never appear.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Probe stack identity races and possibly-applied cleanup
description: Management tests need a reusable fault method for mutations whose response may be lost after CloudFormation accepted them and for friendly-name replacement between preflight and mutation.
design: Treat friendly names as discovery only and immutable StackId as mutation authority. Inject failures at each boundary without AWS credentials or sleeps.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fake models absent, owned, unrelated, replaced, possibly-created, and dual-failure states. Tests assert exact immutable IDs reach mutation calls, possible application triggers owned cleanup, unrelated collisions are never mutated, and both primary and cleanup exceptions survive.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bound AWS SAM Docker and CLI management subprocesses
description: Build, deploy, delete, artifact smoke, and AWS metadata subprocesses have no timeout, so automation can hang indefinitely and live-smoke cleanup may never report an outcome.
design: Use a longer bounded deployment/build timeout and a short metadata timeout; keep HTTP readiness separately bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Mutation/build commands and read-only metadata commands have explicit finite operational deadlines, timeout exceptions are preserved, and injected hanging-command tests inspect both timeout classes without actually sleeping.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bound Cloudflare deployment control-plane subprocesses
description: Ordinary Worker deploy and remove invoke Wrangler without a timeout. A hung provider response, credential helper, or CLI can hold an automation runner indefinitely; only smoke cleanup previously had a deadline.
design: Keep finite control-plane deadlines in deploy/cloudflare_worker management code and pass them explicitly to every mutating Wrangler subprocess. Timeout remains an ambiguous mutation outcome, so ownership/postflight and rerun behavior must not assume no change.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy, ordinary remove, and smoke cleanup pass explicit finite subprocess deadlines in negative-control tests. Timeout errors remain observable, secrets are not printed, and documentation states that a timed-out mutation may have applied.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: deploy and ordinary remove have a shared 120-second subprocess deadline; smoke cleanup retains 60 seconds. Tests intercept the pywrangler boundary and ratchet both ordinary deadlines; docs state a timeout may have applied.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in source commit c331d25; focused Cloudflare/gateway/R2/async/layout suite passes 71 tests.

title: Eliminate or externally fence Worker ownership preflight TOCTOU
description: The direct settings-owner check and later Wrangler upload/delete are separate control-plane operations. A concurrent administrator can create or replace the script between them, so the marker prevents accidental targeting but is not concurrent destructive safety.
design: First verify whether Cloudflare exposes a conditional script/version mutation or deployment primitive that can bind the observed version. If not, supply a deployment lock/fence outside the Worker script control plane, identify its failure and lease model, and require all deploy/remove/smoke operations to hold it. Retain postflight ownership verification as detection, not atomicity.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic two-administrator schedule pauses after preflight, installs a different deployment, and proves this tool cannot overwrite or delete it. A second schedule covers lease expiry/client failure without leaving an unbounded lock. Documentation names the exact Cloudflare or external serialization guarantee and no longer relies on probabilistic names for ordinary deployment safety.

title: Codify Cloudflare deployment boundary fault probes
description: Deployment safety needs a reusable method that exposes destructive-target ownership mistakes, ambiguous control-plane responses, post-apply CLI failures, cleanup failure composition, and pre-parser query amplification instead of relying on happy-path workerd calls.
design: Keep deterministic local negative controls under deploy/cloudflare_worker and add opt-in live probes only for Cloudflare-only semantics. Use sentinels that fail if body or provider work begins after a preflight rejection, and model mutation as possibly applied before the client observes success.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable tests cover exact/missing/mismatched ownership markers, malformed and oversized settings responses, explicit first creation, post-deploy verification, apply-then-error cleanup, dual primary/cleanup failure, exact N/N+1 query bytes and fields, malformed percent encodings, and no R2 mutation. Each probe is referenced by the behavior bead it protects.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: bounded/malformed control-plane responses, owner sentinels, explicit creation/postflight, apply-then-error cleanup, dual-error composition, exact query budgets, malformed encodings, exact cleanup config, and no-R2-I/O assertions. The newly exposed concurrent-admin schedule is separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.5.10.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in source commit c331d25; focused Cloudflare/gateway/R2/async/layout suite passes 71 tests.

title: Bound Cloudflare raw-query parsing
description: The Worker bounds bodies but calls parse_qs on the entire public URL with no raw-byte or field-count ceiling. Add hard URL query and field limits before decoding and use parse_qs max_num_fields so a hostile query cannot consume unbounded CPU/memory inside the application budget.
acceptance_criteria: Exact N/N+1 raw query and field-count tests prove over-limit input is rejected before Gateway/R2 work. Malformed percent encodings and URL parsing fail as bounded 4xx responses, and the ordinary ws query remains unchanged.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: encoded query <=4096 bytes and <=8 fields before parse/gateway/R2, strict UTF-8 and percent encoding, exact N/N+1 negative controls.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in source commit c331d25; focused Cloudflare/gateway/R2/async/layout suite passes 71 tests.

title: Reject non-finite S3/R2 timeout configuration
description: S3Config validates connect_timeout/read_timeout only with numeric type and value <= 0. IEEE NaN passes because every ordered comparison with NaN is false; Infinity also passes as positive. Python's json.loads accepts NaN/Infinity by default, so strict host JSON can carry either into Botocore request policy. R2S3Config delegates to the same validation and inherits the bug.
acceptance_criteria: S3Config and R2S3Config reject NaN, positive/negative Infinity, booleans, zero, and negatives for both timeout fields; strict host JSON rejects non-standard NaN/Infinity syntax before client creation; finite positive integer/float values remain valid. Tests cover direct mapping and file loader paths.
notes:
Reusable discovery method: for every numeric boundary predicate, probe NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity, and bool in addition to ordinary min/max values; JSON decoders must opt out of language-specific non-standard constants when claiming strict JSON.
Fixed on codex/x1p-conformance as part of the host selector audit: S3Config uses math.isfinite for both timeouts, R2 inherits through as_s3(), and the strict JSON loader rejects Python's non-standard NaN/Infinity constants. Direct S3, R2, mapping, and file-path regressions are in the focused 100-test provider/host gate.
close_reason: Non-finite provider timeout values and non-standard JSON constants now fail before any client or bucket access; realistic S3/R2/host tests pass.

title: Make warm-sync cost regression prove shared manifest pages deterministically
description: tests/test_cutover.py::test_warm_sync_fetches_no_closure_siblings assumes three delta facts leave at least one manifest page shared with the prior tree, but workspace/fact keys derive from fresh random keypairs. The full suite on 2026-07-29 failed at held_pages & pages == empty, while an immediate isolated rerun passed. The behavioral assertions about fetched leaves/pages may be correct; the fixture's random geometry does not guarantee its stated precondition.
acceptance_criteria: Construct or grind a deterministic key/range shape that guarantees at least one old manifest page survives the delta, assert that precondition before measuring reads, and repeat the test across enough seeds or schedules to prove it cannot fail solely from treap geometry. Preserve the existing negative assertion that warm sync fetches no closure siblings.
notes: Discovery method: separate the fixture-shape assertion from the behavior assertion and immediately rerun the isolated case.
