The failing full-suite world had disjoint held_pages/pages; the next fresh-key isolated world passed, demonstrating that random address geometry—not selector code—controls the precondition.
close_reason: Fixed the randomized fixture itself: pair() now derives the source identity from a fixed signing secret, making workspace/fact addresses, range cuts, and treap pages byte-stable. The real warm-sync test retains old manifest pages and still proves no closure-sibling fetches; isolated regression and all 22 cutover tests pass.

title: Black-box deployed gateway failure and boundary semantics
description: Existing handler smoke omits provider-real missing-key IAM behavior, plain text Function URL events, well-formed stale proofs, cold secret reuse, boundary responses, and teardown ownership verification.
design: Reuse deterministic provider-neutral scenarios locally and add opt-in AWS assertions only for behavior that emulators cannot establish.
acceptance_criteria: The real Peer and HTTP boundary exercise missing root/object/invite, denied existing data, binary and text events, exact and over-limit payloads, stale valid proofs, two cold instances sharing grants, mutation 405s, and owned-only teardown against opt-in deployed stacks.
notes:
Local handler/provider/management probes now cover most deterministic cases in commits 542b945/e200a1b, but no deployed AWS stack, real execution role, two cold sandboxes, or owned teardown was exercised here; keep open for the black-box live boundary.
Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and e200a1b are 90bc5cf and e6a1987, respectively.

title: Resolve legal large-object compatibility at serverless response ceilings
description: Core accepts objects up to 64 MiB while buffered Lambda and Worker gateways cap individual responses near 4 MiB, and Peer.obj has no ranged or adaptive fallback. A valid large fact or leaf can therefore be unsynchronizable through the serverless profile.
design: Do not paper over the mismatch by raising buffered response limits beyond provider quotas. Preserve whole-object hash verification across any range protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Publish and pull a single valid object above the serverless cap. Either a hash-verifiable range/chunk protocol succeeds without exceeding deployment limits, or the deployment profile rejects creation/selection of such snapshots with an explicit documented compatibility boundary.
notes: The same compatibility gap exists below the object ceiling: Cloudflare advertises a 64 KiB root limit while the canonical protocol accepts roots up to CORE_MAX_ROOT_BYTES. The acceptance test must grow a legal composite root across the edge limit as well as a large immutable object and prove either adaptive transport or an explicit publication/deployment rejection boundary.

title: Codify Lambda deployment boundary fault probes
description: Deployment safety needs a reusable method that exposes pre-I/O bounds, provider/IAM ambiguity, target-runtime drift, handled-error observability, and destructive cleanup mistakes instead of relying on happy-path handler calls.
design: Keep deterministic local probes in tests and expose opt-in live variants for AWS-only semantics. Shrink configurable ceilings rather than allocating production-sized hostile payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable test helpers cover N and N+1 streaming reads with an unbounded-read sentinel, execution-role missing versus denied keys, provider failure to HTTP plus metric mapping, target artifact/runtime identity, and negative-control stack removal. Each probe is referenced by the behavior bead it protects.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Support or explicitly reject SSE-KMS Lambda buckets
description: The deployment accepts an arbitrary external S3 bucket but has no KMS key parameter or kms:Decrypt grant, so customer-managed SSE-KMS buckets fail only at runtime.
design: Prefer an optional KmsKeyArn parameter with a conditional exact-key policy statement; retain SSE-S3 as the zero-configuration default.
acceptance_criteria: The template either supports an explicit KMS key ARN with least-privilege decrypt permission and documented deployment input, or rejects/documentedly excludes SSE-KMS before deploy. Tests prove no wildcard KMS access is emitted.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bound public query and duplicate-batch amplification
description: The public Function URL parses the complete raw query without a byte or field bound, and repeated OIDs in one page request trigger repeated sequential S3 GETs.
design: Use parse_qs max_num_fields after an encoded-byte gate and request-local OID memoization; do not change wire order or response envelope accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Raw query bytes and parsed field count are bounded before parse. A 256-entry duplicate batch preserves response order and misses but fetches each distinct OID at most once. Exact-limit and one-over hostile inputs are tested.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: F9: exercise directed peer topologies with detached immutable objects
description: The fact-only-pile cutover passed symmetric unit tests but failed the real star topology: Bob could push file facts to Alice while Alice had no outbound route back to fetch Bob's separately stored Bao objects. Generalize this into a deterministic topology test/fuzzer over directed peer graphs, object availability, simultaneous authors, and reordered or failed object/fact transfers. The oracle must distinguish allowed delayed completeness from permanent unreachable content and must verify that roots/fact convergence never falsely stands in for blob completeness.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed seed corpus includes one-way edge, star, chain, partition/heal, and simultaneous multi-origin attachments. It checks transfer ordering, retries after injected failure, exact bytes at every reachable replica, and prints a minimal graph/schedule on failure. The ordinary CI corpus is bounded and a longer soak is documented.

title: Remove the Cloudflare PyNaCl EM_ASM compatibility patch when workerd supports libsodium
description: Cloudflare workerd/Wrangler 4.115.0 cannot load either the Python 3.13 Pyodide PyNaCl 1.5.0 wheel or the tested Python 3.14/PyNaCl 1.6.2 wheel unchanged: libsodium's browser-randomness EM_ASM exports trigger an Internal Emscripten code tried to eval failure. The Worker package therefore applies an exact-layout build patch, defers sodium initialization, and uses request-context entropy with deterministic PyNaCl primitives for sealed boxes. Track removal of this compatibility layer once upstream can load native PyNaCl safely.
acceptance_criteria: An unmodified pinned PyNaCl PyEmscripten wheel imports in local workerd and a deployed Worker; Ed25519 signing/verification and standard sealed-box interoperability pass inside request context; deploy/cloudflare_worker no longer rewrites the wheel and crypto_compat.py is removed only if native SealedBox entropy is request-safe.

title: Finish FsStore crash durability and classify post-linearization fsync failure
description: The WIP FsStore fsyncs a created child directory but does not durably record newly created obj/, pile/, or other directory entries in their parent. In addition, fsync failure after link/replace means the mutation may have happened and must not be reported as an ordinary no-write error. Pre-create or durably create layout directories, fsync every newly created parent edge, and map failures before versus after the linearization point to RetryableStoreError versus OutcomeUnknown. Keep local POSIX as a tested refinement, not a production adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Subprocess/fault-injection tests cover directory creation, object link, root replace, and directory fsync boundaries; acknowledged writes survive restart/crash under the stated filesystem assumptions; post-linearization durability failures are OutcomeUnknown and can be reconciled, while temporary files never become authoritative.

title: Bound shared-ingress LIST with opaque cursors and remove the unused GET route
description: Direct S3/R2 LIST calls are strong but paginated, and a multi-page scan is not one transaction. Replace list(prefix)->unbounded list with bounded pages/cursors and drain the shared idempotent ingress workset fairly across short pages plus concurrent insertion/retirement. The member segment authenticates the producer; it is not exclusive consumer ownership. Audit daemon GET /pile and remove it if no client uses it rather than exposing an unbounded listing.
acceptance_criteria: 513+ key schedules with short provider pages, insertions and retirements between pages, and repeated/missing cursors terminate within explicit budgets and eventually revisit every unretired ingress unit under fair turns. Concurrent workers may retire another producer's pile only under the shared retirement proof in poc-16-ilr. Dead GET /pile is removed or explicitly bounded and justified.

title: Split writable publication stores from read-only peer object sources
description: RemoteStore adapts an HTTP Peer for content reads, while FsStore/S3/R2 implement versioned root reads and mutations. Do not let the HTTP cache ETag look like a provider CAS token. Define a minimal ObjectReader protocol for root/object fetches and a WritableObjectStore protocol for conditional create/CAS/LIST/delete. Type Publisher and Node against the writable side; keep sync/Worker fetch paths on the reader side. Tests use deliberately incompatible opaque HTTP and provider tokens and prove no read-only source can be passed to Publisher.
acceptance_criteria: Core exposes separate reader and writable-store protocols; RemoteStore has no read_versioned or mutation surface; Publisher cannot consume an HTTP peer token as a CAS validator; existing remote sync and injected writable-node tests pass.
close_reason: ObjectReader is separated from writable ObjectStore and RemoteStore no longer exposes mutable version/CAS semantics; tests ratchet the boundary.

title: Black-box existing Peer against Lambda and Cloudflare read-only gateways
description: Exercise the actual core.walk.Peer and sync client over HTTP against each deployed handler, rather than only invoking handler functions. Seed one canonical snapshot, mint and decrypt a grant, perform conditional root and ordered page reads, pull a remote-only fact set, verify an ahead client honors read-only capability without PUT, rotate the root during a pinned decision, and repeat across cold service instances. Cloudflare mode uses a polling external publisher only in a separate ingress scenario; the read-only gateway never pretends to settle data.
acceptance_criteria: One provider-neutral black-box scenario passes against local Lambda events/HTTP emulator and workerd, with opt-in live variants for deployed staging URLs. Network faults and response truncation are replayable, grants minted by one cold instance validate on another, and no unsupported mutation route is called.
notes: Legitimate transport bug found while implementing the Lambda live-smoke path: core.walk.Peer.root looked up only the exact dictionary spelling 'ETag', although Function URL/proxies may normalize it to 'etag' or 'Etag'. Fixed by case-insensitive response-header lookup with a lowercase-header regression. Reusable black-box probe: vary casing of every semantically case-insensitive HTTP header at the deployment boundary.

title: sync mixes an unlocked store-root read with locked SQLite reads
description:
core/sync.py reads the store root OUTSIDE node.lock (sync.py:92, 122, 147, 196)
and reads SQLite INSIDE it (sync.py:134, 161, 274, 302). It never calls
_sync_index, so nothing forces the two to describe the same snapshot.

The concrete hazard is in frontier(). `mine` is decoded from local_root's
manifest (sync.py:147, 154-157) while `my_keys` comes from SQLite
(sync.py:160-161). frontier (sync.py:213-215) then assumes they agree: for any
remote entry whose oid matches one of ours, it credits their_keys with
chunks.get(entry.sep, ()) derived from my_keys. If my_keys is AHEAD of mine,
keys the peer does not actually have are credited as held and drop out of
push_keys -- a silent failure to push.

Two further effects of the same split:
  - it gives the action_etag defect (poc-16-3oj) a second, entirely
    non-malicious trigger: local_before's action_etag is read unlocked at
    sync.py:122/130-132 while the actions rows are read locked at
    sync.py:134-139.
  - a plain in-process race: push_fids derives from my_keys under one lock
    acquisition, then walk.py:93 re-reads node.fact_of under a second. A fact
    deactivated in between yields None into close()'s
    sorted(news, key=lambda f: f.key) and raises AttributeError -- an
    unhandled crash, not a clean sync failure.

Fix: pin one snapshot for the whole dial -- take the root and the SQLite-derived
key set under the same lock acquisition, and make frontier's precondition
explicit rather than assumed.

title: Centralize and verify immutable object establishment before root CAS
description: Define one ensure_object(store, oid, raw) operation and use it everywhere immutable authoritative bytes are established: Publisher emission, action evidence, ingress-supplied blobs, and attachment/blob fetches. Created and verified Exists both establish the required postcondition. On collision, GET and verify the exact incumbent bytes and its content address. On OutcomeUnknown, authoritative GET may prove success; if absent, retry without allowing root CAS. Acknowledged-but-invisible create is a nonconforming adapter mutation mode, not ordinary S3/R2 behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Every immutable-object write path goes through ensure_object; Created and verified Exists are accepted, conflicts fail, OutcomeUnknown is reconciled, and no root CAS occurs until all referenced bytes are proven present. Shared conformance/provider tests exercise applied-response-lost, unknown-and-absent, collision, and lying-adapter negative controls.
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending contract/conformance parent closure): ensure_object is now the sole production obj establishment path and tests cover collision plus ambiguous outcomes.
close_reason: ensure_object is the sole production immutable-object establishment path and verifies collisions/unknown outcomes before publication; deterministic and provider conformance tests cover the boundary.

title: Every lost CAS costs a full corpus rebuild; no backoff, and an arbitrary 8-attempt cap
description:
The retry path for a losing publisher is correct but not bounded in cost, which
matters exactly when the premise of this design -- many writers on one bucket
-- is met.

A lost CAS raises RootChanged (publication.py:184-186). runtime.turn catches
it, calls _restore_authoritative_state (runtime.py:59-60), which calls
_sync_index (node.py:261), which sees the stamp no longer matches the store's
root and calls rebuild (node.py:254). rebuild replays resident(root.manifest)
(node.py:470) -- a full walk of every leaf pile in the corpus -- then
force-settles the entire retained catalog and recompiles.

So the loser pays O(corpus) per lost CAS, on a path whose whole point is that
ordinary work is O(path). With N writers contending, aggregate cost is
quadratic in N and each retry is slower than the winner's commit, which is the
classic livelock shape: the more contention, the less likely any given loser
ever wins.

There is also no backoff and no jitter anywhere, and _sync_index gives up after
a hardcoded 8 attempts (node.py:245) with a raise that reaches the caller.

Work:
  - measure it: extend the F2 fuzzer (poc-16-kgp.2) to report per-writer retry
    counts and objects touched per commit as writer count rises. Confirm or
    refute the quadratic before optimizing.
  - make the loser's retry proportional to the delta rather than the corpus.
    The incremental publication path already exists; the loser needs to reach
    it, which means reconciling its intent against the winning root without a
    full resident() replay.
  - add backoff with jitter, and replace the 8-attempt constant with something
    derived from a stated policy.

title: Coherence: publication is SQLite-only, so the CF path can read but never write
description:
The clearest structural gap between DESIGN.md and the code.

DESIGN.md says the client catalog "is an optimization and durable-intent
cache", and that "a store-backed publisher, whether locally hosted or moved to
an edge later, can use the same bounded RangeTree neighbor operation without
constructing SQLite."

Today it cannot. core/indexes.py build() derives every published row by
querying SQLite -- actions (indexes.py:113,124,135), proofs (281), fact_index
joined to proofs (193-206, 302-307), edges (145-147), supp (291-292). The
manifest side is the same: publication.py:164 calls node.keys(ws), which is a
fact_index/proofs join (node.py:297-304). So the three authenticated trees and
the RangeTree are functions of one writer's local relational state, and the
composite root is the CAS'd serialization of that state.

The read side genuinely is database-free -- core/mint.py and core/worker.py
take root bytes plus a fetch and nothing else. That half of the claim holds.

Two consequences worth deciding on explicitly rather than leaving implicit:

1. A Cloudflare Worker can authorize but cannot publish. Every write must go
   through a node that owns a SQLite index for that workspace. That is a
   deployment-shape decision, and DESIGN.md currently reads as though it were
   already an edge-capable writer.

2. Because each writer's trees come from its own index, two writers with
   divergent indexes can each publish a root whose trees describe their own
   eligibility computation. The CAS serializes BYTES, not SEMANTICS.
   Convergence is recovered by the loser's retry path, but nothing today
   asserts that a published root's trees agree with that same root's manifest.
   That assertion is invariant 3 in poc-16-kgp.2 and is the single highest-value
   check in this whole review.

Decide: either state plainly that publication is a client-only operation and
the edge is read-only, or build a store-only publisher (the RangeTree neighbor
operation already is one; the three Worker trees are not).
close_reason: Decision made and DESIGN corrected: current Lambda/CF path is database-free read-only; current publication requires the client SQLite catalog for eligibility, tree inputs, and staged intent. A future store-only publisher is a separate construction. Root/tree semantic-equivalence testing remains tracked by kgp.2.

title: RecursionError escapes the codec doors; piles and roots have no size limit
description:
CONFIRMED by measurement during review.

core/close.py decode_pile documents a total contract: "foreign bytes leave here
as a ValueError or not at all, so a caller can say `except ValueError` and mean
it." It calls json.loads with no guard (close.py:52). json.loads raises
RecursionError, not ValueError, on deeply nested input -- verified: 2,000
levels parse fine, 100,000 levels raise RecursionError.

Same unguarded json.loads at:
  core/manifest.py:286   decode_root, called on REMOTE root bytes (sync.py:129)
  core/sync.py:325       _sibling_keys, whose docstring makes the same promise

core/btreap.py:136-139 is the counterexample that shows the right defense: it
guards json.loads AND caps raw at MAX_PAGE_BYTES = 8 KiB, so nesting can never
reach the limit. Pages are safe; piles and roots are not, because neither has a
size cap anywhere:

  core/walk.py:33        r.read() with no cap -- a hostile peer's /root or
                         /page response can be arbitrarily large
  core/daemon.py:100     _body() reads whatever Content-Length claims, then
                         do_PUT hashes it and writes it to disk (daemon.py:153)

Callers mostly swallow it by accident (runtime.turn and WorkerView.mint both
catch bare Exception), which is exactly why this has gone unnoticed. Node.rebuild
does not, so an unreadable local object can make a workspace fail to open.

Fix: cap ingress bytes at both HTTP doors and at the pile/root codecs, and make
the two codecs' stated ValueError contract true (guard json.loads, and consider
a nesting-depth check for anything not already byte-capped).
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending commit): all externally supplied JSON codecs now reject bytes above declared ceilings before parsing and translate parser RecursionError into ValueError; this includes piles, roots, closure siblings, fact blobs, and btreap pages. Pile encoders and immutable-object publication enforce the same reader ceilings. Daemon request bodies reject oversized Content-Length before read, reject transfer encoding/short reads, and bound pile, mint, page, and control doors. Peer response reads are streaming-bounded even when Content-Length is absent; root/object/control responses have distinct limits. Reusable problem-finding probes added: deeply nested JSON that fits inside a nominal byte cap, monkeypatched tiny ceilings plus a NeverRead/NeverWritten sentinel proving rejection happens before I/O, and a hostile response that returns limit+1 bytes without Content-Length.
close_reason: Bounded codec and HTTP doors are implemented with realistic recursion, pre-I/O rejection, and streaming response tests.

title: Sync enumerates a remote peer's trees with a 1,000,000-page budget
description:
core/btreap.py Reader.items defaults its page budget to 1_000_000 when
max_pages is not passed (btreap.py:230). No production caller passes it:

  core/sync.py:254        action_rows enumerates a REMOTE root's SuppTree
  core/manifest.py:204    compare enumerates a REMOTE RangeTree
  core/manifest.py:248    decode enumerates a local RangeTree
  core/node.py:345        _validate_root_actions enumerates a local SuppTree

The two remote ones are the problem: each page is an HTTP GET against a peer
we do not trust. The root descriptor already carries the honest `count`
(manifest.py:309-321 validates it, and worker.py checks the descriptor shape),
so the bound is available and simply is not used. The structural checks inside
items() do catch a lying count -- but only after the walk has already paid for
it.

Also worth noting for DESIGN.md accuracy: core/btreap.py's module docstring
says Workers "never rebuild a database or enumerate the tree", and items() is
commented "maintenance-only". Sync's action leg constructs a real WorkerView
and then calls view._reader(indexes.SUPP).items() -- reaching through a
private accessor to do the thing the docstring says does not happen. Either
the claim or the code should move.

Fix: pass max_pages=descriptor["count"] at every call site, and give
action_rows/compare an explicit remote-fetch budget for the whole dial.

title: One /mint request has no aggregate object-fetch budget
description:
CONFIRMED by measurement during review.

core/worker.py bounds the SUBMITTED closure (MAX_PROOF_FACTS = 64,
worker.py:12,144) and each individual tree read (btreap.Reader budget resets
per lookup, btreap.py:205-206, with max_page_depth taken from the published
descriptor at worker.py:33-35). Nothing bounds the TOTAL work of one mint.

Measured: a 3-fact request pile against a 60-message workspace with tree depths
15/14/16 cost 63 object fetches. The declared maxima are 64 facts, 8 selectors
per fact (indexes.MAX_SELECTORS), 64 liveness scopes per fact
(facts.MAX_AUTHORITY_SCOPES), each read costing up to depth fetches. With the
depth the attacker can manufacture in poc-16-xjk, one unauthenticated POST
/mint is worth on the order of 10^5-10^6 object GETs.

/mint is deliberately the one unauthenticated verb (core/daemon.py:186-190,
walk.py:52 posts it with auth=False), so this is a pre-authentication
amplifier, and on the intended Cloudflare deployment each fetch is a billed
subrequest against a limit.

Fix direction: give WorkerView one fetch budget for the whole mint, shared
across every Reader it constructs, sized from the published tree descriptors
and the declared closure maxima. Fail closed when it is exhausted -- that is
already the correct answer for an over-large request.
close_reason: Both synchronous daemon mint and async Worker mint now enforce aggregate unique-fetch and byte budgets. Real-snapshot tests cover exact limits, exhaustion, memoization, corruption, and root replacement during an awaited fetch.

title: F6: kernel context differential fuzzer (MemoryContext vs Context)
description:
There are two implementations of the judgment context and they are selected by
duck typing, not by a declared interface:
  - core/kernel.py MemoryContext -- database-free, used by drain()/kernel(),
    which is the Worker authorization path and the ingress door
  - core/kernel.py Context -- SQLite-backed, used by Catalog._accept, which is
    the client admission path
Dispatch between them is hasattr(db, "resolve_offer") at kernel.py:138 and
hasattr(db, "rank") at kernel.py:200. Their interfaces are not even the same
shape: Context has no has_fact() at all, so _judge() would raise on it. Any
future divergence in provider selection or rank between these two is a
silent authorization split between the Worker and the client.

Fuzzer: generate random valid fact closures (and near-miss invalid ones), then
judge each through both contexts with the same fact set loaded, and assert:
  - identical accept/reject verdict
  - identical resolved edges, including role assignment
  - identical canonical provider for every need, including the requires=
    co-offer path (facts/auth/device_invite.py:77 is the only live user)
  - identical proof ranks

Then follow up by replacing the duck typing with one explicit protocol so the
fuzzer is enforcing a declared contract rather than an accident. See
poc-16-ele.

title: F3: tree differential fuzzer -- incremental path-copy vs full rebuild
description:
core/indexes.py:36-38 states the load-bearing claim: "Both paths must produce
the same roots for the same logical maps." tests/test_props.py
test_incremental_equals_full checks it for one scripted sequence. Replace that
with a stateful randomized differential fuzzer.

Layer A -- core/btreap.py against a dict reference model. Random sequences of
insert / update-in-place / delete / re-insert / no-op-rewrite. After each op:
  - btreap.update(...).root == btreap.build(sorted(model)).root
  - count and depth metadata match a recomputed walk
  - Reader.neighbors(k) matches the reference sorted order for keys present,
    absent, before the first, and after the last
  - every emitted page decodes, and no page is orphaned or repeated
Boundary cases to include deliberately: a value canon'ing to exactly
MAX_VALUE_BYTES and one byte over; a page at exactly MAX_PAGE_BYTES; a tree at
exactly MAX_PAGE_DEPTH; the empty tree; single-row trees; delete-to-empty then
re-insert.

Layer B -- core/indexes.py build() incremental vs full over the real Node.
Random op sequences that exercise what the incremental path handles specially:
  - changed_sids with CLEAR -> ACTIVE -> CLEAR transitions (an action winner
    that loses and is restored)
  - the old_fid != current_fid branch at core/indexes.py:247-250, where a
    superseded action's FactRecord must be rewritten or dropped
  - authority-winner changes and deactivations, which are supposed to force
    the full path via publication.py:138-140 -- assert that they DO, and that
    the escape hatch is not reachable with a stale root
  - actions whose evidence oid is rebound (suppression_state.bind_evidence)
Assert the resulting three tree roots equal a full rebuild every time.

Layer C -- core/manifest.py changed_ranges/update vs build. The additions-only
neighbor path (manifest.py:115-185) is the trickiest code in the repo: it
infers a home leaf from a bounded predecessor/successor read plus the
boundary rule. Fuzz random key insertions, including keys that land before the
first separator, after the last, exactly on a boundary fid, and immediately
after a boundary. tests/test_range_tree.py covers randomized batches; extend
it to assert byte-identical roots against build() for every intermediate
state, and to assert the "changed range already present" path is unreachable
from any legitimate settlement (see poc-16-itm).
notes:
Coverage audit confirms the framing precisely: tests/test_props.py
test_incremental_equals_full (lines 745-763) is deterministic and PURELY
ADDITIVE -- create, add_member, 60 messages, a file, a straggler, an evict, and
not one cmds.remove. Deletions get only one-shot checks
(test_action_publication_path_copies_only_its_changed_sid,
test_ordinary_append_reads_only_exact_action_slots) and authority-winner
changes get exactly one (test_resident_action_winner_delta_matches_full_fact_tree).

That matters because Publisher.publish gates on
`incremental = ... and not deactivated and not authority_changed`
(publication.py:138-140). The BRANCH SELECTION is the thing under test, and a
randomized interleaving of adds, deletes, and authority changes is the only way
to stress it. Randomized deletion coverage today exists only at the codec layer
(test_btreap.py test_sequential_insert_delete_and_bulk_have_one_root, seed 91).

title: Make CLI a fact-family command passthrough
description: WHY: core/cli.py and core/daemon.py duplicate every application command in central if-chains even though fact families own construction and queries. WHAT: adopt the POC-17 pattern: families declare their CLI verbs; one checked registry dispatches them; the CLI transports a command path and arguments without owning command semantics. Preserve daemon-only lifecycle/status/sync/rebuild plumbing as explicit core operations. Add realistic command-registry, CLI subprocess, HTTP error, file, deletion, and compatibility tests, and retain the change only if total code and central policy branches decrease.
design: Adapt POC-17's family-owned CLI mapping and generic daemon dispatch to POC-16's HTTP control plane. Prefer a single JSON command envelope over inventing per-family daemon routes. Do not put Node/SQLite policy into CLI; handlers call existing family commands and queries through a narrow host/node context.
acceptance_criteria: All application CLI verbs are registered by exactly one fact family and dispatched generically; core/cli.py contains no application-command branch table; daemon lifecycle/core operations remain explicit; existing public CLI behavior or a deliberately documented simpler replacement is covered end-to-end; tests prove unknown commands, malformed arguments, authorization failures, file transfer, and command discovery; production LOC/central branch count do not increase.
close_reason: Replaced central CLI/daemon application switches with one family-owned checked command registry and one raw argv control envelope; canonical CLI, file paths, errors, discovery, help, ts=0, three-daemon behavior, and extensibility are tested. Full suite 241 passed independently; production physical LOC decreased.

title: Make inactive catalog receipts portable or safely terminal
description: WHY: The stable catalog retains locally ineligible facts and action proposals so canonical winner changes can restore them, but those receipts are intentionally absent from the published eligible manifest. A fresh replica may therefore lack a proposal that an older replica can later reactivate, and unbounded local retention is not a complete protocol. WHAT: Define the minimal authenticated receipt/retention mechanism that gives equal delivered knowledge equal future settlement, or prove a terminal state that permits collection. Reuse content-addressed evidence and avoid restoring delete-to-JSON quarantine complexity.
design: Prefer one immutable candidate/evidence catalog with authenticated discovery over another mutable root. Separate intrinsic kernel validity, receipt existence, canonical eligibility, and active projection in both schema and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh, rebuilt, and long-lived replicas converge through winner changes that deactivate and later reactivate a candidate; retention has an explicit bound or GC proof; inactive bytes never gain authority merely by being retained; tests cover action proposals and ordinary shadowed candidates.
close_reason: Cancelled by design: inactive receipts are local durable intent, not a second replicated fact set. They may be published if a retaining node later reactivates them, but fresh replicas need not receive latent candidates and loss after every holder disappears is acceptable.

title: Test stale CF reads and mint decisions against pinned roots
description: Run database-free Worker authorization while writers advance the same bucket. A Worker may use an older complete root, but all FactTree, SuppTree, AuthorityTree, manifest, and evidence reads for one decision must be pinned to that root and understandable from already written immutable objects.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial tests prove a mint never combines tree descriptors or authority/suppression state from different roots, never requires SQLite, and either returns the decision for one valid pinned snapshot or fails closed.
close_reason: Added a stale-root mint schedule that forbids SQLite and proves one pinned root supplies the complete authorization decision.

title: Stress authenticated-tree integrity and recovery after races
description: Generate concurrent additions, suppression transitions, canonical-winner changes, and retries against one bucket, then validate every successfully published composite root and compare the terminal root with a serial canonical rebuild of the same admitted union.
acceptance_criteria: No schedule produces missing children, count/depth drift, malformed pages, split tree generations, or a root that rebuild rejects; randomized histories shrink to a deterministic regression when a law fails.
close_reason: Concurrent addition/suppression and retained-receipt schedules validate every tree and converge to the serial canonical union, including restored Bao progress.

title: Build a deterministic shared-bucket concurrency harness
description: Create a realistic Store test double that schedules individual get, put-if-absent, list, and root-CAS operations across concurrent Worker publications without sleeps. It must inject lost races, delayed visibility where allowed, retries, and crashes while retaining an inspectable operation history.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can replay a seed/schedule exactly, compare the concrete history with the reference model, and prove existing single-worker behavior still uses the same Store contract.
close_reason: Added a deterministic actor-tagged shared-bucket harness with explicit operation gates, replayable history, and structural validation.

title: Test immutable writes and root CAS under adversarial schedules
description: Exercise same-object/different-object write races, two publications from one base root, crash-before-CAS, crash-after-CAS, stale retry, and idempotent replay. A losing writer may leave harmless immutable objects but must never overwrite different bytes or clobber the winning root.
acceptance_criteria: Every bounded schedule leaves a hash-consistent grow-only object map; each visible root is exactly one successfully CASed, fully closed snapshot; all nonterminal writers can reread and safely retry to a deterministic union.
close_reason: Hardened immutable object creation and cross-handle root CAS; adversarial schedules prove losers cannot clobber winners and retries converge.

title: Specify the shared-bucket state machine and safety laws
description: Write an executable small reference model before touching production storage. Model content-addressed put-if-absent, root read/CAS, pinned stale reads, publication retries, and crash points. Define no-clobber, referential closure, snapshot coherence, tree validity, monotone object knowledge, and retry convergence precisely.
acceptance_criteria: The model explores bounded interleavings for at least two writers and one reader, reports minimal counterexample schedules, and its laws distinguish acceptable stale views from incoherent or destructive outcomes.
close_reason: Added an executable BFS model for grow-only content-addressed objects, one composite-root CAS, pinned stale reads, retries, crashes, and shortest mutation counterexamples; 9 focused tests pass across 18,456 crash states.

title: Model and test concurrent CF Workers on one shared bucket
description: WHY: Multiple database-free CF Workers may read and write one object bucket concurrently. Stale-but-valid snapshots are acceptable, but no worker may clobber committed data, publish a root that names missing or malformed objects, derive a mint from an incoherent snapshot, or corrupt an authenticated tree. WHAT: Start from an abstract state machine for immutable put-if-absent objects plus one versioned root CAS, state the safety/convergence invariants, then build deterministic adversarial schedules and realistic shared-store tests. Keep the scope mathematical and compositional; if the concrete harness gets sprawling, return to the state machine before adding mechanisms.
design: Treat immutable objects as a grow-only map O: oid -> bytes with content-hash equality, and root as a single compare-and-swap register R=(etag, snapshot). A publication is prepare(all immutable objects), validate closure, then CAS R. Linearization is only the successful CAS; losing writers reread R, understand every written object, recompute from the union visible at that root, and retry. Reads pin one root and may be stale but never mix descriptors from different roots.
acceptance_criteria: A checked reference model and a bounded adversarial test suite cover immutable-object races, root-CAS races, stale readers and minting, crash cut points, retry convergence, and full tree/root validation; every failure has a minimal schedule; no solution requires a Worker database.
close_reason: Completed the executable model, deterministic harness, production hardening, database-free stale reads, recovery races, and full authenticated-tree validation.

title: Deliver terminal tombstones to disconnected removed replicas
description: A removed replica can lose its cached grant before it learns the terminal member action when it has no inbound peer. Remote authorization is closed, but its local trusted control plane can continue producing isolated state. Add a safe recovery path that lets it learn terminal actions without restoring upload authority.
design: Separate read-only root/action recovery from mutation authorization. Permit an unauthenticated or narrowly authenticated pull of hash-verified terminal action evidence, while continuing to require a live grant for every upload or mint-capable operation.
acceptance_criteria: After partition, eviction, and grant expiry, the removed replica can dial and install its terminal tombstone; it cannot upload ordinary facts or mint a grant; delivery is idempotent, evidence-verified, and covered by a daemon-level partition test.
close_reason: Cancelled by design: a removed offline replica need not learn a terminal tombstone. It may continue isolated local authorship; stale peers may legitimately accept it, while peers that know the removal refuse new grants and eventually stop further sharing.

title: Replace author timestamps with admission receipts
description: The current convergence rule orders facts and suppression actions by author-controlled (ts,fid). A colluding live relay can backdate a newly signed durable effect so it appears to predate a removal. Introduce a serialized, verifiable admission frontier that distinguishes genuinely pre-removal authorship from post-removal replay without requiring a full fact-set read.
design: Bind each durable admission to a service-issued monotone receipt/frontier and publish the proof under the composite-root CAS. Replicas compare authenticated admission positions, not author timestamps, while Worker reads remain exact and bounded.
acceptance_criteria: A fact admitted before removal remains valid regardless of delivery order; a fact signed or first admitted after removal is rejected even with a backdated timestamp; replicas converge under opposite arrival orders; receipt verification survives restart and does not enumerate FactTree.
close_reason: Cancelled by design: removal is a knowledge/connectivity boundary, not a global authorship-time cutoff. Facts accepted by a peer whose pinned snapshot still authorizes the sender are legitimate workspace history; informed peers eventually close sharing through grant expiry and exact Worker checks. No admission frontier is wanted.

title: Replace prose ratchets with tests of running behavior
description:
## Background
Repository-layout and decision-model tests currently account for a majority of test code and many assertions merely match words in TODO or bead prose.

## Scope
Move security and format claims into realistic tests of callable codecs, admission, publication, sync, and Worker behavior. Retain only small structural repository and documentation ratchets.
design: Behavioral tests and hostile mutations are the authority for running code. String-presence assertions may protect routing or intentional documentation invariants only.
acceptance_criteria: Every S2-S9 safety claim has a running-code or realistic black-box test; removing the corresponding runtime guard makes a named test fail; tests/test_repository_layout.py is reduced to actual repository, bead-frontier, link, and stale-reference boundaries; no acceptance claim passes solely because prose contains a phrase.
close_reason: Running behavioral, hostile-input, confluence, and black-box tests replace prose-only ratchets; full suite passes.

title: Keep Node thin by extracting tree and admission services
description:
## Background
core/node.py is the largest runtime file and currently combines storage, projection, publication, suppression, and removal-index behavior.

## Scope
Place canonical tree, admission, certification, and Worker-read logic in focused modules. Leave Node responsible for workspace orchestration and lifecycle wiring.
design: Extraction must remove duplication and clarify ownership rather than merely moving methods. Event policy remains in facts modules; storage codecs and publication transactions remain in core services.
acceptance_criteria: Node contains no B-treap balancing, action authorization policy, receipt encoding, or Worker proof algorithm; realistic lifecycle tests exercise the extracted running services through Node; the old removal methods are deleted at S5 rather than wrapped.
close_reason: Implemented persistent authenticated trees, derived reverse projections, and extracted tree/Worker/action modules; covered by the green runtime suite.

title: S9: Complete adversarial, confluence, and mutation-proven coverage
description:
Background: the cutover suite lost 63 tests, leaves integrity branches uncovered, and its named suppression theorem is vacuous without attachments.

Scope: integrate S1-S8 under real daemons and sockets across cold join, partition/heal, proposal-before-admission, receipt-before-later-eviction, removal-before-victim, rebuild, authority shadow/restore, uniquely represented B-treap orders, exact CLEAR/ACTIVE slots, zero-provider migration, sealed deep-authority checkpointing, revocation and content/control reserve exhaustion, IAM cutover, fresh/committed authority lookup, malformed stores, and deterministic time; mutation-prove every contract.
design: Prefer product-level black-box tests; use unit tests for pure codecs, bounds, IAM adapters, and hostile branch pins. Equal logical state must yield byte-identical tree bytes. Request-time behavior uses exact SuppSlots only; removal evidence and reverse caches stay off the Worker path.
acceptance_criteria: Attachment-bearing live/rebuild/cold theorem and real daemon removal/auth lifecycles pass under partitions and hostile inputs. Failed-CAS receipts cannot replay, post-CAS copy/proof recovery precedes certification, and observed uncertified roots fail closed. ExactSids partial redundancy and target escalation reject; a successful B-only retry remains possible. Terminal eviction survives pre-masked, current-zero, future-provider, and opposite arrival orders. Capacity faults at detached signature, service record, full-size admit-cell bytes, reserved slot, registry, fixed scratch, write lease, either legacy map, migration-seal object/bytes, next-certificate reservation, retained certificate sidecar, and isolated content/control quotas cannot strand revocation. Delayed old writers cannot create arbitrary or canonical metadata keys; old tokens, read grants, and content credentials cannot address meta-s5. Transitive AuthorityImpactRegistry changes every fixed-point NeedKey; consequence 65 rejects the new provider. Forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk B-treap builds are byte-identical; priority, leader, padding, missing-slot, prefix-scan, removal-fid-index, insertion-history, eager-descendant-release, and shared-quota mutants fail. Zero-provider migration, sealed 519-hop checkpoint, provider 65, deterministic time, and exact 867-subrequest tests pass. Legacy-universe mutations drop a quarantine-only row, substitute its FactRecord/raw root, remove a registered-publisher attestation row, or trust a naked fid after restart and each fails certification. Migration-seal mutation omits its object/byte reserve or exceeds 4 KiB and fails before S5 CAS. Certificate-capacity mutation proves a missing next-root reserve blocks CAS, stale served-root fencing releases and deletes its sidecar, and a removal then publishes without borrowing escrow. Receipt-cycle mutation includes its receipt EvidenceRef in proof_digest and cannot construct a canonical receipt; named vectors pin 7 pre-receipt refs, then one receipt ref and an 8-ref ActionRecord. Evidence/base/path boundary tests pin 8, 13, 1, 129, and 1,032 independently. Every recorded mutation makes a named test red and the full suite passes repeatedly. Candidate-registry mutations drop a losing provider, revive a MASKED ref, choose a nonminimal fallback, exceed 64 candidates, or scan FactTree and each fails a named test; the 64-by-64 action stays at 4,096 refs. Cutover-cycle mutation derives layout_seed from a digest containing the seeded map root and fails. Target-row-byte and candidate-registry-byte capacity mutations fail before signing or publication. Legacy-fence tests delay an accepted old-prefix write across revocation and prove no snapshot/seal precedes definitive drain; post-fence writes reject. IAM mutations delete, redirect, oversize, alter prefixes, invalidate provider signatures, or GC the retained LegacyIamAttestation and each fails certification. Capacity mutations independently exhaust served-cell, inclusion-witness, PublisherCapacityCell, and certificate rows/bytes; registration or the publishing deployment fails before CAS, while a nonpublishing observer fails closed and repairs independently without blocking the canonical root. Fact-key mutations cover negative, boolean, 16-digit-positive, signed, whitespace, uppercase and ambiguous keys; the maximum 32-target/8-evidence ActionRecord uses exact 80-byte FACT_TS_MAX keys. Multi-origin quarantine tests enumerate identical signed inventories in opposite orders and require the same lowest origin, logical digest, seed and root; a first-seen-origin mutant fails. A legal legacy removal of a quarantine-only fact must create and fill its normal Sid ActionSlot/SuppSlot, while an omitted-slot or forced-LegacyMask mutant fails; conflicting same-fid bytes abort migration. Binding-order mutation pre-fence-final-binding assigns a seed or exact namespace before the drained snapshot and fails. Capacity mutation single-operation-cutover-scratch attempts to stage the first S5 root in the later one-operation pool and fails on a corpus larger than that pool; the whole-cutover fixture succeeds only with a complete, disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope and sealed CutoverObjectManifest. Capacity mutation digest-only-capacity-ceiling removes or GC-collects the canonical ceiling preimage and must fail after restart; redirected, oversized, and schema-mismatched ceiling/source objects likewise fail. Retry mutation reuse-active-fallback-on-retry attempts a second fence without a newly provisioned successor and fails while writable S4 remains authoritative. Mutation closure-wide-candidate-masking treats every proof-support fact as a continuing guard and fails paired grantee-only/grantor-only fixtures. Mutation workspace-sized-service-row-plan applies the full legacy service corpus in the final CAS and fails on a capacity-compliant corpus larger than one transaction; capped inert batches plus bounded pointer activation pass. Mutation cyclic-cutover-generation-manifest makes the service descriptor hash a manifest/root tail that already contains its oid and is rejected as an unconstructible content-hash cycle. Mutations hash-raw-bytes-as-fid, aborted-content-pin-blocks-retry, and collect-sealed-cutover-generation each make a named test fail.
notes:
Integration covers DIRECT_TARGETS escalation, exact binding, grandfather barrier, retained quarantine, zero-provider cases, deep checkpoints, terminal future providers, service and fixed-scratch boundaries, 1,032-page fixed-key publication, 221-page ordinary insertion, generation-fenced recovery, stale served-root fencing, orphan receipts, proof recovery, exact CLEAR/ACTIVE slots, canonical B-treap orders, IAM writer revocation, content quota exhaustion, high descendant count, and exact Worker maximum. Attempt injection delays an old put across OPEN to SEALING and ABORTING and proves unsettled leases block clear. Authority fixtures fill 64 and reject 65. Named receipt regressions include a failed-CAS candidate replayed after author eviction, a partially redundant ExactSids proposal followed by a successful B-only retry, and opposite arrival orders. V1 keeps descendant liabilities; optional capped LiabilityReleaseCheckpoint batches are off request.
Review-found mutations are mandatory: inline-target-spec makes a maximum ExactSids ActionSlot exceed 512 bytes; illegal-selector-reuse gives an illegal legacy direct target new authority; omitted-zero-provider-slot makes the zero-provider principal ActionSlot impossible to fill; and unbounded-pending-key or shared-pending-quota can strand revocation. Named tests keep ActionRecord out of line, force LegacyMask for illegal current DIRECT_TARGETS pairs, precreate migration/principal slots, fill PendingCapacityEnvelope, and prove direct admission still succeeds.
Review closure 2 mutations are mandatory: fact-only device revocation leaves a same-key provider live; overwriting a shared SuppSlot drops one action owner; tree-only capacity omits FactRecord/raw-chunk evidence; and closing the whole recovery epic makes the ledger ratchet vacuous. Named tests require DevicePrincipal future coverage, both overlapping ActionSlots plus canonical witness, explicit canonical-evidence capacity, and an active recovery epic until S10 retires the ratchet.

Tests traverse root to every EvidenceRef/raw chunk, delete each object in turn, build more duplicate entries than one map page, require one map row per entry and one canonical receipt/action, and reject a missing/misdirected row or duplicate receipt.
A named mutation drops one losing/fallback fid from PrincipalProviderRegistry; certification must fail before a principal receipt or Worker grant can publish.

Named tests independently pin 8 EvidenceRefs, 13 base records and one base path, authenticate both migration maps under LegacyMigrationSeal, reserve a next certificate before CAS, and reclaim leased-root certificates only after fencing/release.
Review closure 5 mutations are mandatory: count-only admit capacity exhausts the strong-service byte quota with maximum-size receipts, and an uncharged/uncapped LegacyMigrationSeal strands the first S5 root. Named tests fill admit_cell_bytes independently, cap the seal at 4 KiB, charge its object/bytes, and keep all publisher attestations as individually capped LegacyUniverseMap rows.

Tests require writable service-only S4 recovery, exact 56+8 KiB transport boundaries, dual-scope canonical witness selection, authenticated seed, and publisher-local off-request witnesses.

Tests cover LegacyMask authority fallback, restart/GC census proof, concurrent R/R2 reads, exact lease exhaustion, and aggregate raw-byte boundaries.
Review closure 18 mandatory mutations: drop-target-record-after-quarantine and post-seal-s4-decoder-dependency. Tests shadow all action targets, GC the historical root, and rederive selectors from pinned target FactRecords; migration deletes old pages/root cell/decoder and re-certifies through the signed S5-native census.
Review closure 19 mandatory mutation: principal-provider-bare-fid-after-quarantine. Shadow a non-target provider, collect the historical root, certify through its retained binding, restore it exactly, and prove the provider cap was never freed.
Review closure 20 mandatory mutations: bare-authority-proof-digest, drop-authority-proof-support-after-quarantine, and drop-post-s5-quarantined-fact-from-facttree. Collect historical roots, restart, certify fallback proof records, and restore an ordinary fact without local quarantine bytes.

Vectors prove post-hash rank construction, device_invite co-offer separation, inert retained-proposal cutover, and distinct same-provider checkpoint paths across GC and masking.

Review closure 23: Worker suppression reads only the request fact selectors, the selected provider selectors, and that family edge’s declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS/FollowAuthority scopes; incidental proof support, unselected edges, and one-time authorization guards confer no liveness authority. BaseOfferNeedKeyRegistry and AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry give symmetric bounded discovery: a new full NeedKey finds all retained providers, and a new provider updates every admitted full NeedKey for each exact/ANY base, recording COOFFERS_MATCH or COOFFERS_MISMATCH without a FactTree scan. Each base candidate value enforces a 64-scope union in both provider-first and NeedKey-first order. Raw manifests bind chunk ordinals and byte ranges, RawFactContentCommit identity excludes upload generation, and a strong ContentCommitPin transitions PENDING to ROOTED with metadata CAS; only a fenced ABORTED pin is collectible, while cutover uses a paged pin set plus bounded anchor. A fact that both consumes and provides authority is budgeted for 162 registry objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction including the pin transition.
