title: S8: Characterize and repair post and idle-sync latency
description:
Background: removal_entries decodes every resident fact twice per commit even with zero removals, producing an approximately 8x and growing post regression; idle blob demand also scans all facts per dial.

Scope: remeasure after S4, remove remaining full scans from commit/publication and idle sync, and install scaling benchmarks with explicit accepted bounds.
design: Do not optimize the superseded monolithic removal object before S4 establishes the final shape.
acceptance_criteria: Back-to-back benchmarks against main show post latency flat or within a documented bound through the measured corpus. Admission benchmarks cover one sid, maximum-`ExactSids`, maximum-provider MemberPrincipal, and maximum transitive authority impact: evidence refs stay at e <= 8, total base logical records at b <= 13, base tree paths at p <= 1, changed paths stay at p + m + c <= 129, and fixed-value page copies at 129 * MAX_TREE_DEPTH <= 1,032 independent of total facts, removals, or descendants. A removal that encounters an absent reserved slot rejects rather than structurally inserting. Separate ordinary-publication fixtures exercise MAX_ORDINARY_TREE_INSERTS * MAX_TREE_PAGES_PER_INSERT = 13 * 17 = 221 and reject the next insertion prospectively. A provider producing consequence 65 rejects before upload without disturbing escrow. Converged idle sync is independent of resident fact count except actual pending blobs; regressions fail on restored scans; full suite passes. Fallback benchmarks fill one NeedKey to 64 candidates and 64 consequences to 4,096 examined candidate refs; candidate 65 rejects and no curve scales with resident FactTree/provider population. ExactSids size/performance fixtures use FACT_TS_MAX and exact 80-byte target/evidence keys so the reported ActionRecord bound measures the protocol maximum rather than a convenient sample.
notes:
Measure the final capped B-treap shape, not the superseded monolithic removal object. Report separate one-sid, maximum-ExactSids, maximum-provider, maximum transitive-authority-impact, and high-descendant curves. BaseRevocationRecords excludes effect and authority rows; c is the fixed-point AuthorityImpactRegistry union. Revocation uses existing fixed keys and at most one copied page per level. Ordinary insertion owns the distinct 17-page prospective bound. Page sharing may improve results but is not part of either proof. V1 does not synchronously release descendant liabilities.
Review closure 4 corrects the performance theorem: service/object records are not tree paths. Track e=8 EvidenceRefs, b=13 BaseRevocationRecords, p=1 base ActionSlot path, then p+m+c=129 and 1,032 copied pages. The separate ordinary structural insertion ceiling is 221 pages (13 paths * 17 pages).
Review closure 7 adds separate losing-provider width and 4,096-ref worst-case fallback curves; AuthorityImpactRegistry alone is not a candidate index.
Review closure 8 pins maximum legal key width in the performance and capacity baselines.
Review closure 15 adds s = len(impact_scopes(root,a)) <= MAX_ACTION_IMPACT_SCOPES = 65 as a strong-service reverse-registry read bound; c remains the independently deduplicated at-most-64 AuthorityTree consequence set and fixed tree-path theorem.
Review closure 17 corrects raw-byte capacity: eight EvidenceRefs each reserve MAX_FACT_RECORD_BYTES metadata, but raw evidence reserves only MAX_ADMISSION_PROOF_BYTES plus MAX_REVOCATION_RECORD_RAW_BYTES. Performance/capacity fixtures also include fixed WorkerReadLease slot and retained-root/certificate dimensions.
Review closure 19 capacity: charge the capped provider-registry binding bytes and retained provider FactRecord/raw-root occupancy; quarantine and restore return neither count nor capacity.
Review closure 20 capacity: charge authority-proof object/bytes and all grow-only admitted FactTree/FactRecord/raw occupancy; quarantine releases none, while the removal path reads only fixed candidate summaries.
Review closure 26 corrects ordinary publication capacity to 13 structural paths and 221 prospective pages: FactSlot, SELF SuppSlot, directly targetable SELF ActionSlot, at most two principal ActionSlots, and at most eight AuthorityTree NeedKeys.
close_reason: Incremental Merkle-tree and manifest updates plus idle ETag/blob stamps repair measured post and idle-sync latency.

title: S6: Ship remove commands and black-box deletion lifecycle
description:
Background: production deletion has no daemon or CLI route and has never crossed the real product surface in CI.

Scope: add thin remove proposal and admission routes/verbs, preserve family-owned logic, repair adjacent CLI/HTTP error handling and phantom rebuild behavior, and drive authorized message/file deletion across real daemons.
design: Routes only parse and delegate. A bare proposal is visibly inert in pending/ and does not enter the S5 FactTree or frontier; successful admission fills its reserved ActionSlot and exact SuppSlot values in one atomic publication. Algorithms and authorization remain in fact/core modules.
acceptance_criteria: A black-box test drives create, post, send, stage removal, admit, sync, cold join, and assert-gone across two real daemons; staging alone changes no canonical root, while admission atomically publishes the action evidence and fixed slot updates; both message and attachment descendants disappear; a removed author and forged or bare receipt cannot delete; malformed or missing parameters return stable errors without tracebacks or phantom workspaces; full suite passes.
notes:
Review closure 2: the device revoke route accepts an authenticated device target ref, derives DevicePrincipal(pk), rejects a naked key or exact-SELF shortcut, and proves two same-key device provider facts plus a later provider are all denied.
Application policy closure (review-corrected): product and black-box coverage must show primary device bootstrap, a direct member and two consenting sibling devices deleting that user content, ordinary cross-user denial, live-admin cross-user success, NEVER-target denial, removed-admin denial, and preserved pre-removal receipts. Hostile cases include a grindable competing device_invite without target-key DeviceOwnerConsent, wrong consent owner/provider/signature, a masked direct claimant with attempted device fallback, root-dependent owner proof bytes, and later direct rejoin without old-owner rewrite. CLI and daemon remain thin and never accept a caller-supplied owner.
Independent review closure 27: black-box coverage must prove a hostile bare invite cannot pre-tombstone an arbitrary device key; admin(D) does not promote siblings; a consented device may use admin(U) only through ADMIN/OWNER; and a later direct rejoin cannot rewrite a legacy actor record.
Independent review closure 28: routes expose exact device.grant.delete separately from terminal DevicePrincipal. Black-box coverage revokes a lost bare invite through owner and admin paths without invited-key cooperation, proves no future-key tombstone, and rejects using per-target S4_DEVICE_INVITE_ACCEPTANCE as reusable consent.
Independent review closure 29: product tests show an old S4 client may publish without contextual invite acceptance while S5 eligibility fails safely; updated clients bind workspace, target, device, owner and invite. Losing actor-shadow CAS attempts reclaim fenced scratch and never consume durable capacity.
close_reason: Owner/admin remove routes and black-box deletion and eviction lifecycles are implemented and tested.

title: S7: Repair the shadow/restore sync wedge and hostile-input gaps
description:
## Background
A peer syncing during an authority-shadow window retains stale scratch proof ranks and later fails closure assembly forever; multiple integrity guards are unexercised.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run tests/test_removals.py's quarantined-removal shadow window through a peer sync, restore authority, then sync again. The window peer repeatedly raises closure assembly while a fresh reader converges. Mutating eight hostile-input guards currently leaves the suite green.

## Scope
Rebuild scratch proofs correctly after provider changes, flip the current-behavior assertion, and add realistic hostile-door coverage for the affected sync/manifest/pile guards.
design: Keep this independent of removal semantics; the reproducer works with ordinary messages.
acceptance_criteria: The window peer converges after restore and restart; a fresh peer and window peer reach identical roots; each named integrity guard has a hostile input that fails if the guard is removed; push-before-drain remains pinned; full suite passes.
notes: Review closure 20 shadow/restore invariant: restore eligibility from the exact current FactTree and AuthorityProofRecord bindings after old-root GC; node-local quarantine is cache only.
close_reason: Scratch proof recovery, hostile ingress/state doors, restart convergence, and full-suite regressions are green.

title: S5: Wire screening and immutable removal admission
description:
Background: mint.screen is unwired; relays can launder evicted authors; NEVER needs separate live guards; one-fid eviction permits provider fallback; legacy globals may tombstone keys with no provider; existing authority can exceed Worker limits; ordinary writes can consume eviction capacity; stale roots and publisher-local receipts can diverge; old publisher write credentials can bypass a new root; payload quota can starve control metadata; and every legacy effect source requires fenced backfill.

Scope: implement the service-exclusive workspace-global publication/admission service and TargetRegistry; stage proposals in pending/; fill reserved ActionSlots and exact SuppSlots atomically; preserve zero-provider LEGACY_GLOBAL tombstones and every LEGACY_SLOT effect through grandfather receipts and LegacyMask; flatten sealed over-budget providers with LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint; certify AuthorityImpactRegistry and RevocationLiability; migrate retained quarantine; revoke and drain legacy writers before sealing an IAM-isolated metadata namespace; isolate ContentCapacityEnvelope from control capacity; remove legacy slot/globals; and enable bounded Worker grants with one served-authority RPC.
design: S5 is one coordinated cut with no deletion gap. Root, frontier, receipt, TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, and PublicationAttempt updates serialize under a separate service-exclusive key; workspace.body.pk is forbidden. The new meta-s5 namespace has one metadata writer and old publishers are fenced and must reseed. Suppression reads are exact CLEAR/ACTIVE SuppSlots; fixed ActionSlots point to bounded immutable ActionRecords; no authoritative removal-fid tree exists. Fenced backfill alone may structurally create migration slots, including a zero-provider principal ActionSlot. A legacy normal selector is reused only when its exact current DIRECT_TARGETS pair is legal; otherwise the old victim receives LegacyMask. MemberPrincipal keeps per-fid Worker reads and future-provider escrow. V1 never enumerates descendants to release liability. Control metadata, pending staging, and content quotas are physically and IAM isolated.
acceptance_criteria: Cutover preserves legacy message/file deletions, a content deletion whose author was later evicted, every removal global, LegacyMask, retained quarantine membership, and a zero-provider tombstone. The first S5 root binds an authenticated LegacyUniverseMap, LegacyEntryMap, and separately capped LegacyMigrationSeal; quarantine-only reingestion after restart requires an inclusion proof for the exact fid, FactRecord, and raw root. Registered publisher attestations are individually capped universe-map rows. A missing/misdirected universe row or naked fid rejects. An illegal legacy direct target that offers a normal selector still receives victim-only LegacyMask without parent/principal cascade. Backfill precreates and fills the zero-provider principal ActionSlot. Publishers with different basis roots serialize at frontier/<workspace>; a pre-eviction basis cannot bypass the cell. Every grandfather receipt has an AdmissionCommitProof. At most 7 proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; only after its fid/FactRecord/raw root exist is the receipt EvidenceRef appended to the at-most-8-ref ActionRecord. Certification rejects any receipt that hashes or names its own ref. Before the fence all publishers pin the same admission_pk and MigrationBootstrapCommitment; the pre-fence commitment contains no snapshot-derived layout_seed, cutover_basis_digest, cutover_digest or exact metadata namespace. After the definitive drain and frozen snapshot, the first S5 root authenticates S5CutoverBinding with the derived values, exact CapacityEnvelope, PendingCapacityEnvelope, ContentCapacityEnvelope, CutoverCapacityEnvelope, IAM-isolated namespace, and exclusive writer identity distinct from workspace.body.pk. Every admit cell reserves exact bytes for its complete signed receipt; the migration seal reserves one object and at most 4 KiB. Legacy metadata-write credentials are revoked, maximum token lifetime and definitive drain complete; a prepared service-only S4 fallback generation restores writable S4 after every post-fence/pre-CAS failure without reviving an old credential. For later S5 publications, derivation and durable PublicationAttempt plus next-certificate object/byte/write-lease reservation precede gateway scratch upload; generation seal and definitive AttemptWriteLease drain precede CAS. The first S5 cut instead seals and drains a complete CutoverObjectManifest in preallocated whole-corpus cutover slots. In both paths CAS charges every canonical object while preserving the certificate claim, and verified copies precede proof and certificate. A pre-CAS orphan remains inert forever; a post-CAS/pre-proof crash recovers idempotently; an observer of a committed but uncertified root fails closed. Current/leased-root certificates remain charged and are reclaimed only after the last served-root lease/witness is released or fenced; missing reserve prevents CAS without borrowing revocation escrow. ExactSids partial redundancy rejects and terminal principal retains future escrow. Fixed-key action capacity caps at 129 paths and 1,032 pages; provider, effect, or consequence 65 rejects. A maximum target spec fits a bounded ActionRecord, never its 512-byte ActionSlot; total base logical records cap at 13. A sealed 519-hop chain grants through checkpoints. Exact bounded reads use no scan, rebuild, on-request diff, or removal-fid lookup; InclusionWitness and served-authority paths stay bounded at 867 cold subrequests. Content quota exhaustion and pending quota exhaustion cannot consume service-envelope or revocation capacity; direct admission succeeds when optional staging is full. Full suite passes. The cutover computes a layout-independent LegacyUniverseRows digest and cutover_basis_digest, derives each candidate layout_seed before the seeded map root, and only then fixes cutover_digest; a final exact-prefix IAM attestation enters LegacyMigrationSeal. Root publication atomically updates complete forward AuthorityCandidateRegistry and reverse AuthorityImpactRegistry values with AuthorityTree, rejects candidate 65, and reserves exact TargetRegistry and AuthorityCandidateRegistry bytes. Before hashing LegacyUniverseRows, S5 revokes old-prefix writers, waits token expiry, and definitively drains every accepted or ambiguous pre-fence write; a delayed accepted write blocks and joins the snapshot, while a post-fence write rejects. The root retains and certifies the capped provider-signed LegacyIamAttestation. Publisher registration atomically precreates fixed served/witness/certificate reservations and updates one bounded PublisherCapacityCell; root publication checks that aggregate and prepares only its publishing deployment, while other publishers independently construct direct witnesses off-request after observation. Multiply retained quarantine facts select PUBLISHED or the lowest verified publisher id before hashing; conflicting bytes abort. A legal grandfather target resolved only through LegacyUniverseMap precreates and fills its normal ActionSlot(Sid(resolved_sid)) and SuppSlot during fenced backfill without restoring the target; only illegal pairs use LegacyMask and ActionSlot(Migration). Before any irreversible writer fence, whole-cutover capacity preflight provisions the complete first-root manifest, final canonical occupancy, and a simultaneous disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope for all migrated pages, records, maps, checkpoints, grandfather actions, service rows, root and certificate reservation. A migration larger than the single-operation PublicationAttempt pool succeeds from that reserve; a short object, byte, manifest-row or write-lease dimension leaves S4 writable and prevents the fence. Every S5 retry provisions and attests a distinct inactive successor fallback plus fresh MigrationBootstrapCommitment before fencing the currently writable S4 generation. A realistic fixture survives two consecutive post-fence/pre-CAS aborts, publishes through each new S4 generation, then succeeds with monotonic distinct generation ids while all fenced credentials continue to reject. The migration seal retains and binds both canonical capacity/source ceiling oids. Candidate and AuthorityImpactRegistry masking follows only family-declared authority liveness scopes. During cutover, conditional service rows stage in an inactive generation through capped transactions; a sealed CutoverServiceGeneration is activated with root/frontier by one transaction capped at 8 rows and 128 KiB, so no workspace-sized row plan is replayed at the first-root CAS. Cutover activation atomically changes the sealed content-pin generation to ROOTED and writes its anchor; only a fenced and drained ABORTED generation is collectible.
notes:
The service owns frontier/, canonical root, admit/, admission log, both registries, monotonic attempt generation, and fixed scratch pool. Publishers have no metadata-write credentials. put_attempt checks OPEN generation and exact manifest slot, hash, and size and holds an AttemptWriteLease until definitive settlement. OPEN to SEALING rejects new writes and drains all leases; ambiguity blocks. The CAS precharges the canonical manifest before authority-exclusive copy. Pre-CAS ABORTING drains writers before scratch reuse. Cutover ratchets retain LEGACY_SLOT, every LEGACY_GLOBAL/removal global, retained quarantine, pending/, different basis roots, the later evicted author, pre-eviction basis rejection, and offline publisher fencing. Every action is prospective. AuthorityImpactRegistry includes losing and fallback provider closures. Content and metadata gateways cannot address each others IAM namespace. Optional off-request LiabilityReleaseCheckpoint work is never required for revocation or ordinary capacity.
Review closure: PendingCapacityEnvelope has fixed overwrite-only keys, byte caps, and write leases. Read/content/pending credentials cannot address canonical metadata. Migration creates every LegacyMask SuppSlot and migration ActionSlot prospectively, and every LEGACY_GLOBAL creates its Principal slot even with zero providers.
Review closure 2: TargetRegistry is unique by typed MemberPrincipal/DevicePrincipal scope. Device revocation is key-wide and later matching providers are born ACTIVE. An exact action followed by a principal action retains both ActionSlots and deterministically selects the SuppSlot witness. The CAS and RevocationLiability charge FactRecord/raw-chunk objects and bytes for all canonical action evidence.
Live principal admission rejects a naked public key and requires a recomputed PrincipalBinding to an authenticated membership/device target; only fenced LegacyGlobalBinding lacks a provider target.
Review closure 3: the composite root binds legacy_entries. Live ActionRecords root proposal, receipt, and all detached signature/support EvidenceRefs; GC traversal reaches their FactRecords and raw chunks. Backfill receipts only canonical legacy actions; every duplicate entry maps to that action and retains its evidence in LegacyEntryMap.
Every membership/device publication atomically updates PrincipalProviderRegistry, checks TargetRegistry, and creates an ACTIVE SuppSlot when tombstoned. Principal admission reads the bounded provider set without scanning FactTree.
Review closure 4: LegacyUniverseMap is the root-bound published-plus-registered-quarantine membership witness and roots retained FactRecords/raw chunks. LegacyMigrationSeal binds it, LegacyEntryMap, old source digests, inventory attestations, and the cutover digest. Capacity reserves cert/<next-root> before CAS and reclaims old sidecars only after served-root references end.
Review closure 5: prospective service capacity rejects before signing if the canonical admit cell exceeds MAX_ADMIT_CELL_BYTES or lacks byte reserve. LegacyMigrationSeal is a charged MAX_LEGACY_MIGRATION_SEAL_BYTES object; the attestation set stays in the paged universe map.
Review closure 6 makes the live and grandfather receipt construction content-hash acyclic: receipt proof excludes its own EvidenceRef and ActionRecord is formed only after receipt identity is final.
Review closure 7 makes migration construction acyclic, adds final-prefix IAM attestation to the seal, and makes fallback publication bounded by the complete forward candidate set. Terminal receipts cannot sign unless both TargetRegistry row and byte escrow exist.
Worker hits compare both provider fid and closed-proof digest. Candidate masking never reverses, while its fixed-width witness is recomputed to the canonical minimum when overlapping actions arrive.
Review closure 8 orders the physical legacy-writer barrier before the logical snapshot and makes IAM plus serving evidence durable, bounded, and pre-CAS.
Review closure 9 makes retained-quarantine reconciliation confluent and guarantees a constructible owner slot for both normal and migration-only grandfather actions.
Review closure 10: LegacyMask derives only from the pre-record namespace computed from anchor, reconciled S4 root, old slot/globals digest, and pre-cut IAM fence attestation. It never embeds cutover_digest; the seal binds both values.
Review closure 11 uses the prepared service-only S4 fallback after every post-fence/pre-CAS failure, enforces proof aggregate plus framing transport caps, authenticates layout_seed in the first root, and avoids any per-root publisher loop.
Review closure 12 splits the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and adds a separately provisioned whole-corpus CutoverCapacityEnvelope/CutoverObjectManifest. Snapshot-derived seed and namespace values never appear before the drain; the normal PublicationAttempt pool never stages the first S5 root.
Review closure 13 makes retries recursively safe: every attempt has a new already-provisioned successor fallback before its fence, including two consecutive aborts. It also roots both retained ceiling preimages.
Review closure 14 preserves declared authority-liveness semantics and makes first-root service state atomic through a single generation pointer rather than an unbounded all-row CAS.
Review closure 15 breaks the first-root hash cycle: staged grandfather rows carry CutoverGeneration(service_generation_id), the final bounded transaction atomically writes root/frontier/generation pointer plus one CutoverCommitAnchor, and only the post-commit signer turns those active rows into AdmissionCommitProofs. Active generation rows, payload manifests and anchor remain canonical/charged; only temporary scratch and duplicate staging charge are reclaimed. Principal actions expand impact_scopes to the terminal scope plus every affected Sid.
Review closure 16 admission recovery: the strong root/frontier transaction creates the DirectCommitPair; post-commit proof recovery strong-reads that retained cell/log pair and signs row plus EMPTY after restart even when the historical root and proof cache are gone.
Review closure 17: cutover seals legacy_effect_census_oid/digest and reconciled_s4_root_oid, manifests their complete retained bytes/proofs, and re-certifies them after restart without superseded S4 child pages. authorize_serve claims a fixed lease atomically with served-cell advance; concurrent advances cannot reclaim or mix the leased root/certificate. Capacity covers lease rows/bytes, worst-case retained roots/certs, census, root preimage, and aggregate rather than per-record raw proof bytes.
Review closure 18: action publication pins every target_fact_record_oid/raw root for action lifetime even after canonical-provider quarantine. First cutover signs the exact converter version, reconciled root oid, census oid/digest, and seal fields after S4 completeness validation; post-seal code deletes the S4 decoder and certifies from S5-native objects/signature.
Review closure 19: principal admission expands only through authenticated registry bindings; a sixty-fifth distinct provider rejects even when earlier providers are quarantined, and restore must match the retained binding.
Review closure 20: every new durable S5 fact remains in FactTree across quarantine; authority proof admission is immutable; projection eligibility remains separate from monotonic masking, and certification replays rooted AuthorityProofRecords without a search.
Review closure 21: first-S5 FactTree admits only ORDINARY legacy rows; effective removal sources/evidence stay rooted by action/map paths and INERT_REMOVAL stays frozen-map-only and forever ineligible. Checkpoints preserve one exact source closure and flattened provider/action liveness scopes, including same-provider alternate paths.
Review closure 21 supplement: checkpoint FactRecords and GC root their exact paged LegacyAuthorityProofRecord; off-request certification replays all pages, while Workers see only the checkpoint bounded proof. Same-provider closures remain distinct and independently maskable.
Review closure 22: LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint refs use certified LEGACY_SOURCE_RANK(source proof depth, source fid, source candidate id), never the flattened checkpoint proof/provider, preserving mixed native/legacy winner order. Principal-provider, authority-candidate, and authority-impact registries store content-addressed bounded RegistryValueObjects behind 256-byte atomic pointers. NeedKey/co-offer and reverse-value bytes are capped. Every live target carries an AtomicCommitBudget; publication rejects before upload unless the complete 162-object/44,630,016-byte registry set, attempt manifest, and at-most-193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction fit. Mandatory mutations: checkpoint-reranks-legacy-candidate, inline-registry-values-overflow-atomic-commit, unbounded-authority-impact-value, and unbounded-required-cooffers.
Review closure 23: Worker suppression reads only the request fact selectors, the selected provider selectors, and that family edge’s declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS/FollowAuthority scopes; incidental proof support, unselected edges, and one-time authorization guards confer no liveness authority. BaseOfferNeedKeyRegistry and AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry give symmetric bounded discovery: a new full NeedKey finds all retained providers, and a new provider updates every admitted full NeedKey for each exact/ANY base, recording COOFFERS_MATCH or COOFFERS_MISMATCH without a FactTree scan. Atomic publication now charges at most 162 registry value objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction. Boundary fixtures use distinct target/evidence records and a 128-edge unique acyclic proof DAG. Required mutations: worker-suppresses-all-proof-evidence, provider-scans-or-omits-full-needkeys, and unclaimed-recovery-epic.
Review closure 24: authority proof admission is immutable once a CommittedAuthorityProof and post-commit AuthorityProofCommitProof bind the exact admission-basis proof; later canonical-winner changes do not re-resolve it, and only mandatory provider selectors plus declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS may mask it. Authority records separate bounded transport depth/cost from logical proof depth; NEED/REF descendants of a LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint propagate source depth with DERIVED_LEGACY_RANK. Ordinary raw facts use a separately sealed paged RawFactContentCommit in the isolated content envelope, so the fixed metadata PublicationAttempt carries one commit reference rather than every chunk. Required mutations: reresolve-admitted-proof-against-current-winner, checkpoint-descendant-uses-transport-depth, and inline-raw-fact-chunks-overflow-publication-attempt.
Review closure 25: AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry is discovery-only and stores no full candidate id or winner rank; every exact full NeedKey derives its own candidate id/rank, including legacy checkpoint tie breakers. Each base candidate value enforces a 64-scope union in both provider-first and NeedKey-first order. Raw manifests bind chunk ordinals and byte ranges, RawFactContentCommit identity excludes upload generation, and a strong ContentCommitPin transitions PENDING to ROOTED with metadata CAS; only a fenced ABORTED pin is collectible, while cutover uses a paged pin set plus bounded anchor. A fact that both consumes and provides authority is budgeted for 162 registry objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction including the pin transition. Required mutations: reuse-base-rank-for-full-needkey, late-needkey-multiplies-candidate-scopes, sort-raw-manifest-by-chunk-oid, content-generation-in-canonical-commit, and collect-sealed-content-before-metadata-cas.
Review closure 26: raw_root_oid authenticates the complete canonical fact bytes, while the running codec recomputes body hash and envelope fid; raw JSON hash is never substituted for fid. Deterministic ContentCommitPins use monotonic epochs so a fenced/drained ABORTED attempt can become a higher-epoch PENDING retry before re-upload without ABA. Cutover content lifetime uses an explicit STAGING/SEALED/ROOTED/ABORTED generation row, paged set, and atomic root anchor. Ordinary publication budgets 13 structural inserts and 221 prospective pages. Required mutations: hash-raw-bytes-as-fid, aborted-content-pin-blocks-retry, and collect-sealed-cutover-generation.
Application policy closure (review-corrected): admission implements separate OWNER and ADMIN handlers with ordinary conjunctive named needs. OWNER exact-matches current ActorPrincipal to the target retained owner; ADMIN requires a live admin provider and still matches the exact target offer. The receipt is created only after proposal/support refs plus service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest; it is not a proposal need. ActorBindingProof is deterministic and target-bound without root/frontier bytes. DEVICE resolution requires target-key-signed DeviceOwnerConsent, while any direct-member claimant (including a masked one) forbids device fallback. This permits primary device bootstrap and later direct rejoin without rewriting old ownership. A provider plus deletable child is committed/proved in two frontiers; bare owner/sid/target substitutions and no-offer targets fail.
Independent review closure 27: S5 verifies the admission-time actor record instead of replaying current direct-member precedence. DevicePrincipal rejects bare invite targets. ADMIN uses an explicit KEY or OWNER admin scope: KEY preserves admin(D) as device-key-only authority; OWNER requires a DEVICE binding and exact admin(owner) proof.
Independent review closure 28: S5 certifies the exact legacy record oid, atomic commit row, filled proof slot and commit proof. A native DEVICE binding requires DeviceOwnerConsent; a legacy target may use only its device-signed contextual S4_DEVICE_INVITE_ACCEPTANCE basis, which migrates that target owner but cannot authorize new S5 publication. Receipt certification rederives byte-equal ActionAuthorization and follows its actor/admin proof arms after GC or winner changes.
Independent review closure 29: cutover rejects/re-anchors a pre-recorder authority provider when a one-time authorization guard is now removed, rather than guessing pre- versus post-removal admission. It verifies the complete contextual S4DeviceInviteAcceptance and the root-free legacy_authority_checkpoint_namespace; no owner FactRecord depends on cutover_digest.
Independent review closure 30: fenced LEGACY_SLOT and LEGACY_GLOBAL receipts use a non-callable GRANDFATHER(LegacyEffectAuthorizationRef) bound to the exact LegacyEffectCensus row and old source, so valid S4 cross-user deletions survive without being falsely labeled OWNER/ADMIN and LIVE_GUARDS can never choose it. Every first-publication or on-demand authority closure is separately committed and post-commit-proved before a LegacyActorAdmissionRecord may cite it, including a preexisting provider and an alternate closure; finite S4AuthorityProofCapacityCell accounting is idempotent and a losing proof CAS consumes nothing. LegacyActorAuthorityTransport preserves the record original authority ref while a distinct authenticated CHECKPOINT transport binds and replays its exact paged source proof/candidate into the new checkpoint provider; the future checkpoint identity never overwrites the S4 record.
Independent review closure 31: ActionAuthorization verification is action-scoped for LIVE_GUARDS and grandfather actions, outside the direct-target OwnerBinding branch, so terminal MemberPrincipal/DevicePrincipal and LEGACY_GLOBAL actions cannot bypass it. Proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; the later receipt EvidenceRef only determines ActionRecord. S4AuthorityProofScratchSlot and S4ActorAdmissionScratchSlot precharge object/byte/write-lease capacity before upload, preserve disjoint scratch plus canonical coexistence after a winning CAS, and fence/drain every losing attempt before reuse. An actor closure above the native proof bound is committed and post-commit-proved before the target CAS as PAGED_S4(S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef) over the canonical LegacyAuthorityProofRecord; cutover reuses that exact source to construct CHECKPOINT transport instead of inventing migration evidence later.
Independent review closure 32: S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef retains the paged proof oid as well as its strong commit id, so certification and GC never scan for the sidecar. A pre-fence bounded authority proof keeps its immutable DirectRoot commitment/proof through cutover; only a never-committed closure may receive CutoverGeneration, and a second row at the deterministic id aborts. S4 actor/proof canonical balances are workspace-global, initialized once, and never refill across fallback generations; an abort drains and rebinds only the separately precharged scratch pool while preserving both canonical cells byte-for-byte. Fixed row/proof caps and retry ratchets cover all three failure modes.
Independent review closure 33: AuthorityProofCommitProof is deterministically addressed by authority_proof_commit_id and a committed row with a missing sidecar takes restart recovery, never a conflicting cutover rewrite. Each paged S4 proof has an atomically RESERVED/FILLED S4PagedAuthorityProofSlot; its ref retains the filled proof oid, and restart deterministically recovers the sidecar before any target or cutover may cite it. The workspace-global actor/proof capacity cells have deterministic ids, retained capped envelope preimages, explicit cell/slot row-and-byte charges, and scratch-only fallback handoff. Final independent review reported no actionable findings; 51 repository-layout tests and 346 non-network tests passed with one planned skip.
close_reason: Current-format suppression actions are admitted and published without the legacy removal index or dual decoder.

title: sync: shadow/restore wedges a window peer (stale proof ranks in assemble)
description:
A peer that synced DURING an authority-shadow window is permanently wedged after the shadow is restored: every later sync raises ValueError('closure assembly') out of core/sync.py::assemble, whose scratch resolver reuses the peer's stale proof ranks, so the flipped device_key winner never re-ranks. A peer-side index rebuild does not free it; a fresh reader converges fine.

NOT removal-specific and NOT introduced by the one-store cutover: reproduced with an ordinary msg and no removal anywhere (oyd.7 adversarial review, 2026-07-26) — hence a discovered-from bead, not epic scope.

Pinned as CURRENT BEHAVIOUR (not as law) by the trailing pytest.raises pair in tests/test_removals.py::test_quarantined_removal_holds_locally_but_diverges_peers — fixing this must flip those assertions.
close_reason: Bead bankruptcy 2026-07-27: superseded by docs/TODO.md and replacement epic poc-16-kb6. Closed history is preserved; no requirement survives unless restated under poc-16-kb6.

title: cutover .2b multi-supp-key correction
description:
GOAL: multi-supp-key suppression. A fact declares a SET of groups (its TARGET-tag markers); a removal's DELETE-tag marker names exactly one group; removal KIND is read off the TARGET *ref* — present = point (reach = exactly that fid), absent = kill (reach = deathkey ∈ suppkeys(f)). No marker-format change; no fixture split. Runs between oyd.2 and oyd.3 because oyd.3 fills removals.py's consumers and oyd.4 reads the victims index.

READ FIRST: docs/REMOVALS.md §2 (rewritten 2026-07-26 — the predicate, the two traps it is shaped to avoid, the consequences list; it is the single source of truth and SUPERSEDES all predicate forms in the poc-16-3fo notes); core/suppression.py; core/removals.py as oyd.2's repair agent left it (its applies() splits kind by MARKER presence — superseded, see below); core/node.py IDX_SCHEMA + the supp writes in merge/_restore_quarantine and the supp deletes in _prune_unresolved; facts/content/_delete.py; tests/util.py channel_delete/DeletionFamily/suppression_world; tests/test_removals.py.

THE PREDICATE (verbatim from REMOVALS.md §2; implement exactly this):

    suppkeys(f) = { group(m) : m a TARGET-tag marker of f }        — a SET
    deathkey(r) = the one group r's DELETE-tag marker names

    applies(r, f) = not is_deletion(f) and ( target(r) == fid(f)          if r names a TARGET ref
                                             deathkey(r) in suppkeys(f)   otherwise )

A point's death marker still names a group — inert for reach (authorization/display scope only). Group markers on removals are inert everywhere (I2). This shape is forced: the group clause is MEMBERSHIP (never scalar equality — a fact has many groups), and a point's death marker must never feed the group clause (channel-mates share the channel group, so one deleted message would delete its channel while routing to one key — the I6 under-approximation, proven by three independent reviewers with reproducers).

BUILD:
1. core/suppression.py: replace _marker's collapse-to-None with a helper returning ALL well-formed markers (the 0-or-2+ collapse is the one-group assumption fossilized in code — the defect itself). New API: suppkeys(f) -> frozenset of group keys from TARGET-tag markers; deathkey(f) -> the group of the DELETE-tag marker when exactly one exists, else None; is_deletion(f) -> f carries exactly one DELETE-tag marker. Delete scalar suppkey(). atom() is UNCHANGED — both tags keep their bytes; there is no envelope-format change and there must not be one.
2. core/removals.py applies(): the predicate above, kind by TARGET ref (suppression.TARGET named ref, same accessor victims() used). Chunking: sorted set of keys, cut after any key whose fid satisfies shape.boundary (same rule as shape.stable_cut_positions — reuse it, don't re-derive; DRY row "chunking rule"). Leaf pile = encode_pile of the chunk's MEMBER facts only, canonical key order — closure is NOT inlined (that was the invalidated null hypothesis, COSTS §3). Closure sibling = canon({"keys": [...]}) of closure-minus-members, computed as a set difference: closure_keys(members) = keys of close(members, deps_of, fact_of) minus the member key set (equivalent to the (lo,hi] interval formulation because members ARE the in-range keys). title: Make recipient writer leases immutable per acquisition
description: A delayed commit from a predecessor-generation writer must not be rebound when the same caller or writer label later acquires a successor lease. Represent each acquisition with an immutable unforgeable token bound to the exact recipient generation and fence epoch; commit consumes that token. Persist retirement/purge evidence so a delayed or replayed predecessor attempt cannot recreate a purged cover identifier under the successor.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic barrier tests reuse one writer label across P and S, delay the P commit through fence, migration, destruction, promotion, finalization, restart, and S lease acquisition, and prove the old token always rejects while a valid S token can write only non-retired material. Attempts to recreate each purged root, retained node, and leaf identifier fail closed; duplicate current-generation commits remain idempotent. Tests cover token swap, generation swap, crash recovery, concurrent writers, and delayed delivery.

title: Root canonical cover identity before the first migration proof
description: The x1o.3 adversarial review showed that the protected migration proof is too late to authenticate its own initial input: before the first proof is frozen, a disk attacker who knows recipient public S can replace a cover envelope, its adjacent expected local-secret commitment, and plaintext consistently, and migration will bless the substituted wrapped_secret_id. Design a scalable authority for canonical FrontierRoot/HistoryNode context and wrapped_secret_id before migration. It must not consume one Secure Enclave/KeyStore handle per cover node or introduce a permanent root that can decrypt archived secrets. Compare a provider-authenticated Merkle/log root, causally signed/content-addressed source records, and generation-bound integrity state; specify restore, rotation, migration, and purge of the integrity anchor.
acceptance_criteria: A chosen construction makes the pre-migration expected context and wrapped_secret_id independent of the mutable envelope row, bounds hardware handles as cover size grows, and cannot decrypt or reauthorize retired content. Realistic tests forge a valid public-key ciphertext plus matching adjacent commitment before claim/migration, mutate or roll back the authenticated index/root, and prove migration and retirement leave P intact or fail closed. Tests also cover legitimate cover insertion, puncture, generation migration, crash recovery, same-device restore, and anchor rotation/purge.

title: STEER: make version skew observable without putting a release marker in the root
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §12, first bullet — steer needed before the RELEASE-constant bead (poc-16-9fc.6) lands. Two peers on different releases holding identical fact sets produce identical fingerprints and different roots: the walk prunes on fp (core/sync.py:44-48) and reports convergence while the roots differ byte for byte, and nothing in the seven verbs, the grant token (core/daemon.py:52-57) or decode_root notices — the root's 'v': 1 at core/tree.py:171 is written and never checked. A release marker IN the root would make this observable in one conditional GET, but it is a marker in the CAS'd bytes, so two releases would then differ by construction on an unchanged set, which is exactly the Tier 2 churn the marker is meant to diagnose. A marker BESIDE the root — a roots/ entry field, or a /mint response field alongside the grant and current root — buys the same observability without touching published bytes. Either way it is diagnostics only: no validator, no closure path and no layout path may read it. Decide which, or decide that silent convergence-with-different-roots is acceptable and say why.

title: Device capability facts and the authoring floor — activation without ambient state
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §7. POC-10's release rule survives verbatim — do not author a new durable fact type until every non-deprecated release can decode, authenticate, validate and project it — but its mechanism does not: a ceiling computed from a signed release manifest plus trusted time, classifying incoming facts Active/Pending/Dropped, is ambient mutable state, and a validator reading it makes verdicts time-dependent and collapses order-independence (the same argument that keeps globals out of persistent handlers), besides needing the parking the grammar deleted. So a fact authored at version v is valid at version v forever, however and whenever it arrives, and activation becomes an authoring-side policy: devices advertise the versions they implement as ordinary facts (a device.capability family, or an atom on the existing device fact), the floor is the minimum over non-removed members read from app.db, and COMMANDS refuse to author above it. Nothing in validate, resolve_deps, close or layout may read it — a contract test should assert the floor query is reachable only from command paths. A client that jumps the gun harms nobody's correctness; it strands its own facts at peers that cannot yet read them.

description: docs/VERSIONING.md §8. There is no release version in the tree — no pyproject.toml, no __version__, no git tags — only two hand-maintained constants that mean different things and are tied to nothing: INDEX_VERSION (core/node.py:57) re-runs the KERNEL, so it is what an offers-normalization or needs change requires, while APP_VERSION (core/node.py:58) re-runs only MATERIALIZE, because pump's reproject branch rebuilds Valid tuples by hand from the already-admitted facts table (core/pump.py:76-119) and never calls the kernel. They were bumped together exactly once. Introduce one RELEASE constant and derive both from it (each may keep its own discriminator so a schema-only change need not force a kernel replay, but a release always forces both). Close two gaps in the same bead: INDEX_VERSION does not cover idx.db's OWN schema — IDX_SCHEMA is applied with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS at core/node.py:146 and rebuild() wipes the hardcoded tuple ('facts','offers','proofs','globals','log') at core/node.py:597, so a new column or table is silently never migrated and a new table never wiped; and rebuild() deletes the durable meta['reproject'] marker (core/node.py:600) relying on the process-local _reproject set, with safety coming only from meta['root'] also being deleted, so any new version-driven wipe path must preserve that invariant. Measure the resulting replay: full reproject is O(|V| x deps) unbatched SQLite round trips with the whole set resident (core/pump.py:97-119), and a release bump makes that path routine rather than exceptional.

title: Offer-vocabulary registry: addresses append-only, needs frozen in meaning (Tier 1 law)
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §5 and §4. Tier 1 says a release may never move the valid set: two replicas at different releases that disagree about membership diverge permanently, because fingerprints differ over facts both hold and no walk closes the gap. The law that makes that true is that normalization is a RELABELING — meanings are append-only, a name once spent is never reused for a different assertion, and an address is just this release's name for a meaning, applied to offers and needs together in one release, so matching is invariant under it. Encode it: a checked-in registry mapping every offer address (name plus what the a0 and a1 slots MEAN, not their values) to the release that introduced it, generated from the family modules; a test fails if any address is removed or redefined against the snapshot. A release that genuinely changes a meaning mints a new one and leaves the old alone. The §4 half is the pairing obligation: nothing today tests that a shipped version's needs still match current providers, and the registry is what makes that testable. Document the two live shape traps at the same layer: the envelope-to-address map is not injective (['offer','member',PK] and ['offer','member',PK,''] have different fids and the identical offers row, core/fact.py:44), and a1 means three different things by position — '' in a stored offer, None as wildcard in a need (core/kernel.py:98-99), None coerced to '' in a requires co-offer (core/kernel.py:110).

title: unreadable: a third kernel outcome, so a behind-version peer fail-stops instead of looping forever
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §6. Today an unknown fact tag rejects the ENTIRE unit — core/kernel.py:355-371, handler_for returns None so deps is None so rank is None so Judgment(False) for every fact in the pile including the ones the peer understands (verified experimentally: a 66-fact remote workspace with one fact of an unrouted family loses six facts to the whole-unit rejection) — and because those facts never land the diff keeps showing them missing, so the leaf is refetched once per root change on either side and once per process restart (Node.sync_cache is in-memory, core/node.py:88). Not a per-walk loop, since core/sync.py:20-23 short-circuits on the root ETag pair, but an unbounded refetch of a range that never converges, and nothing in the seven verbs, the grant token (core/daemon.py:52-57) or decode_root carries a release version to notice by. Fix: an unknown (FAMILY, VERSION) is a verdict about the NODE, not the fact. Judgment gains a third outcome beside valid and invalid — unreadable never enters the set, deletes nothing, and charges nobody, while invalid means delete the pile and charge the pusher's prefix. core/node.py:237-241 is where the outcome must be distinguished from False, and core/node.py:247-248 (st.delete(k), 'retire ingress after the CAS', today unconditional) is the line that must become conditional; core/sync.py marks the range stalled rather than refetching. Note both halves are new work: there is no blame mechanism today (do_PUT returns 204 unconditionally at core/daemon.py:143-145 and turn() deletes every pile whatever its verdict), so this adds charging the invalid side AND exempting the unreadable one. Retention must be bounded or it reopens the DoS the pile design closed, an unknown tag being free to fabricate: a per-prefix byte cap and a TTL, after which the pile drops and the range re-syncs. Judgment is tuple-unpacked at its call sites in core/node.py, core/tree.py and core/mint.py, so widening the NamedTuple and fixing the unpacks is one change (see branch versioning-skeleton). Piles stay all-or-nothing on purpose, so the client stops cleanly at the version boundary rather than serving a partial truth. POC-10 called this 'incoming is volatile intake'. Keep the rebuild assert at core/node.py:594 ('own store failed its own kernel') exactly as it is — unreadable is about foreign piles, never about one's own store.
acceptance_criteria: A pile carrying an unknown (family, version) is dropped without being charged to the pusher's prefix and without being retained anywhere — POC-17's rule: bytes become durable only once the current release can decode, normalize and project them — the affected range is reported stalled rather than rediscovered on the next root change, and the same pile drains normally once the handler exists; a genuinely invalid pile still drops AND charges; the rebuild-time assert on one's own store is unchanged.

title: offers(f) as handler output: the version interlingua seam, identity everywhere, byte-identical
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §3 — the load-bearing change; the worked-out mechanism is ~/poc-17/DESIGN.md (Dotted variables, Provide). Add offers(f) to the family contract beside needs(f) — a per-version NORMALIZER in POC-17's terms, a pure function from one supported source shape to one current semantic form. The kernel admits handler.offers(f) instead of fact.offers(), so a fact's EMITTED offers can differ from the offer atoms in its body; a source offer atom is not itself a matching offer, it is input to that version's normalizer, and only the emitted row matches. Adopt three POC-17 properties verbatim: the vocabulary is a canonical dotted path (content.message.body) built through one path object shared by constructors, normalizers, validators and queries, so a source version that called it content.post.text emits the current name and no current code retains the old one; emission is ALL-OR-NOTHING, a valid fact's normalized offers copied whole with the family never returning a subset, which makes the normalizer a security boundary that must recognize an exact supported source shape and REJECT extra source offers rather than let a sender smuggle one into a valid owner (poc-16 has no such check today because the atoms simply are the offers); and normalization licenses renaming a variable, re-encoding a key or payload, splitting or combining fields, and mapping an old tag into current semantics without touching an immutable byte. Do NOT import POC-17's parking: poc-16 deleted it from the grammar, so an unmet need rejects the closed unit. Fact.offers() survives as the envelope accessor for shape and validate. Move every atom-reading call site: core/kernel.py:334-336 _admit, :246 extend_proofs offer-waiter wakeups, :278 proof_sources (which decides whether a fact needs a persistent rank, so a handler-only offerer would otherwise lose its rank across restart), core/node.py:288-290 idx offers, :350-358 _shadows memo invalidation, :333/:401-417 quarantine offer index, facts/_commands.py:44-46 publish() authorship check, facts/auth/removal.py:38 global_rows and :50 materialize. Globals ride the same seam and are published in the root (core/tree.py:167-172); removal's value is already a stable identity, so that part is plumbing. Every family's first implementation is 'return f.offers()' — the identity — so this lands byte-identical with the whole suite green. Also fix the latent poison hole this widens: _admit at core/kernel.py:372 and handler.global_rows at :374-375 sit OUTSIDE the try at :354-368.
acceptance_criteria: The offers table is filled from handler.offers(f) at every listed call site including facts/auth/removal.py:38 and :50; with identity implementations the whole existing suite is byte-identical; and a family that validates but whose atoms carry a non-scalar yields Judgment(False) rather than raising out of kernel(), covering both _admit and handler.global_rows, which sit outside the guard at core/kernel.py:354-368.

title: PROOF: cross-release replay of a golden corpus yields an identical valid set
description: docs/VERSIONING.md §9 — the centerpiece, and what makes every other bead safe to land. title: Versioning — offers as the release interlingua, replay as the upgrade
description: Port POC-10's versioning model into the atom grammar: an unversioned base store (atoms are forever, no fact rewritten or re-signed), per-version handlers that tolerate every version of their OWN type and no version of anyone else's, valid facts emitting offers normalized to the current release as a common lingua franca, one release constant held in state, and a replay of all materialized state on bump. The load-bearing consequence: a fact's EMITTED offers must differ from the offer atoms in its body — today core/kernel.py:334 _admit inserts fact.offers() verbatim and no family has an offer hook — and needs must be normalized identically, or a v1 need cannot match a v7 offer and the whole unit rejects. The reason is that a handler can tolerate all old versions of its own type but not all old versions of every type; the interlingua buys that product out. Three axes stay separate: fact version (in the tag, frozen into fid), layout version (packing/fanout/CUT), derived-state version (INDEX_VERSION/APP_VERSION). Tier 1, the valid set, may never move across releases; Tier 2, the arrangement (canonical provider choice, leaf closure, pile oids), may move and republishes. Also closes a live bug: an unknown tag rejects the whole unit (core/kernel.py:355-371, verified) so a behind-version peer re-pulls the same leaf on every walk forever, and nothing in the seven verbs, the grant, or the root carries a version to notice by. Plan of record: docs/VERSIONING.md. Centerpiece: replay a golden corpus under release N and release N+1 and get an identical valid set.
design: See docs/VERSIONING.md. Normalization must be a relabeling of a stable meaning space applied to offers and needs alike, so matching is invariant under it — offer addresses append-only, a shipped version's needs frozen in meaning, a genuine change of meaning minting a new address that each old handler decides whether it can honestly offer. Activation is authoring policy computed from the read model, never a validity input: POC-10's release-manifest-plus-trusted-time ceiling is exactly the ambient mutable state that would make verdicts time-dependent, the same argument that keeps globals out of persistent handlers. Version lives in the TAG, never as a new fact field, because validation is reconstruction equality against the family's own SHAPE constructor in every family. Composes with poc-16-808 (the offers seam sits on the one kernel judge loop; a bump replays through the cursored pump) and poc-16-jbg (a stateless mint must carry the same handler set as the drain that published the root).

Skeletons landed (2026-07-25): branch versioning-skeleton, commit 4117c7e — facts/__init__.py offers()/VERSIONS/handler_for_version/current_version, core/release.py (RELEASE + both stamps + arrangement-bump declaration + the wipe list), core/vocabulary.py (append-only address registry), kernel.UNREADABLE documented beside Judgment, and tests/test_versioning.py with 26 skip-marked acceptance tests for .1-.8. One deliberate divergence recorded: POC-17 parks an unmatched Require; poc-16 deleted parking, so an unmet need rejects the closed unit.

It covers general compat code elsewhere: read-compat shims, dual decoders, tolerant parsers, state migrations. So the legacy_* modules stay (they ARE per-version family handlers), .1 renames rather than removes them, and .8 ships a further version deliberately. Also recorded: poc-16 has no parking because every pile is CLOSED — the closer either shipped the providers or authored a broken unit, so there is nothing a wait could resolve; that is why POC-17's normalization is adopted but its Require-parks-on-no-match is not.

title: Keep purge transition delivery closed-pile and non-parking
description: Integrate recipient transition claims, reservations, and completion evidence with the poc-16 invariant that every fetchable unit is an already closed, dependency-first pile. A batch reservation explicitly refs predecessor, reader authority, the provider-authorized P/S/T/batch claim, and every included purge operation; serialization carries their complete closure in the same pile down to the workspace anchor. A receiver never parks a reservation or waits for an operation, claim, or authority fact to arrive later: any missing ref or need rejects and retires the whole ingress unit without graph, projection, queue, or hardware side effects. Retry resends the same prepared reservation fact and now-only timestamp/fid in a new complete closed pile. An included operation may be delivered independently later only as a duplicate because the accepted reservation pile already carried it. An operation not referenced by the immutable batch stays excluded even if its standalone pile arrived first and is handed downstream for poc-16-x1o.19. Recipient reservations remain non-wrap-eligible throughout.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests partition and duplicate the same accepted transition graph into valid closed piles, deliver those piles in every order, and prove identical accepted facts, batch assignment, and successor eligibility. Adversarial fixtures truncate each required predecessor, authority, schedule, batch, or operation dependency from a reservation pile; the kernel rejects the whole unit immediately, the engine deletes it rather than parking it, no pending or wake state appears, and no fence, migration, destruction, projection, or wrap eligibility begins. Retrying the byte-identical prepared reservation in a complete dependency-first pile succeeds without a new clock value or latest-state lookup. A standalone included operation delivered before or after is only a deduplicated copy; an excluded operation delivered before the reservation remains outside and survives in the stable handoff for poc-16-x1o.19. Crash and restart after rejected ingress and after accepted closed ingress preserve those results. Tests assert refs and closure, never timestamp comparison or delivery order, establish membership.
notes: Discovered during final review of revocation batching: earlier wording implied a reservation could wait for a referenced operation, contradicting poc-16 closed-pile and no-parking invariants. This bead plans the fix; no revocation implementation is included in the current branch.

title: Derive canonical mint authority from the tree in stateless runtimes
description: The landed peer mint passes its root-stamped idx canonical offer/proof view into kernel.evaluate, preventing a stale request closure from omitting an incompatible committed authority winner. Root metadata carries only view/anchor/globals, so a Worker or Lambda that evaluates from root metadata plus the submitted pile alone would reintroduce poc-16-zgj.13. Build or fetch an equivalent canonical authority projection from the root/tree on the stateless path; app.db remains absent.
design: Reuse the canonical resolver/proof rules in core/kernel.py. The derived representation is an implementation cache, never protocol state; root/tree facts are authoritative. Prefer a bounded/root-stamped authority projection that the FaaS runtime can reuse, but correctness must not rely on warmth.

title: Bind purge batches causally instead of by arrival order
description: Replace arrival-based accepted-before-freeze membership with an immutable causal retirement-batch commitment. Before a transition can close predecessor P, the device provider unique P/S/T schedule claim binds a canonical commitment to the exact purge-operation fids, and the transition reservation explicitly refs those operations so they are in its dependency closure. Inclusion is decided only by those committed refs, never by whether a replica observed, delivered, admitted, or queued an operation before a local fence. Reservations coalesce only when P/S/T and the batch commitment are identical. Different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch reservations are mismatched and never become wrap-eligible. Purge operations carried only by a mismatched or excluded reservation remain independently validated facts and are emitted as a stable queued handoff retaining their own causal refs and the P transition claim; poc-16-x1o.19 later binds that handoff to finalized S and a later claim. The strong tier uses a rollback-resistant provider one-time claim or equivalent CAS to authorize at most one batch commitment for P; the software tier documents its clone and restored-snapshot limitation. Completion refs the unique claim and exact batch. Neither timestamps, fid ranking, local negative knowledge, nor a latest-row lookup chooses batch membership or a winning claim. This bead defines batch identity, dependency closure, and the queued handoff; poc-16-x1o.21 owns closed-pile serialization and missing-ref rejection, while recipient finalization, rebasing, and later rotation remain downstream.
acceptance_criteria: Property and multi-replica tests construct the same accepted causal graph through different operation discovery and claim-construction orders; every replica derives the same operation-to-batch assignment from the immutable claim refs. Every included operation is an exact referenced dependency exposed to the closed-pile serializer. An independently valid operation excluded from the commitment remains outside even if observed earlier and is persisted exactly once in a stable handoff that retains the refs needed by poc-16-x1o.19. This bead does not require downstream rebase or rotation, and poc-16-x1o.21 separately proves that no receiver waits for a missing dependency. Cloned claims with identical P/S/T but different batch commitments cannot both authorize destruction; identical P/S/T/batch retries coalesce byte-for-byte. title: Bind the recursive recipient key schedule and transition handle peak
description: Turn the one-step successor commitment into a recursively fork-safe key schedule. Before any predecessor destruction, the transition reservation or provider claim binds both the fixed successor public key S and the next public-key commitment that S will publish for T. The provider ADR chooses how every replica with valid state obtains the same pair and how the next transition obtains the same T/U pair: a rollback-resistant hardware one-time schedule claim bound to the device provider, a deterministic forward schedule guarded by non-rollbackable monotonic state, or a software fallback with explicitly weaker snapshot guarantees. A same-S/different-T reservation is a conflict and is never equivalent. The predecessor private key alone cannot derive S or T. For independently generated non-exportable handles, budget steady state as active plus staged-next and transition peak as predecessor P plus successor S plus S staged-next T; all three exist before P is destroyed. If another mechanism claims a two-handle peak, it must prove how T remains uniquely fixed, durable, and non-derivable without a post-destruction allocation.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-provider contract tests perform at least three consecutive rotations and create cloned or concurrent reservations with same P/S but different T and with same P/S/T. Different-T attempts are permanently ineligible; identical schedule claims coalesce without changing any generation public key. Restored-state tests prove the advertised normal-disk, hardware-backed, and rollback-resistant guarantees and show that no retired schedule state can authorize a second valid pair in the strongest tier. The non-exportable implementation and fault provider expose and survive the documented three-handle transition peak, then return to two steady handles. A provider capped at two handles rejects rotation before predecessor destruction; capacity for three handles completes the transition and returns to two. Any claimed lower peak has an executable test proving its alternative mechanism. No timestamp, fid ranking, late lookup, or unbounded precomputed key list defines the schedule.

title: Rebase purge operations excluded from the committed transition batch
description: Consume the immutable causal retirement-batch claim from poc-16-x1o.20. A P-to-S completion names exactly the purge-operation refs committed in its unique P/S/T/batch claim. An independently valid operation not named by that commitment never joins the completed P transition retroactively, regardless of when it was authored, observed, delivered, or admitted and regardless of whether it was carried by a mismatched reservation. Preserve that operation as queued work, bind its retry to the finalized S by explicit refs, and include it in a later provider-authorized batch; when its retirement set is recovery-eligible under S, it triggers the S-to-T rotation. Only identical P/S/T/batch retries coalesce. A different-S, same-S/different-T, or same-P/S/T/different-batch reservation stays permanently ineligible, while independently valid operation facts reachable from it are revalidated and retained on their own merits. This is causal operation accounting, not timestamp ordering, arrival ordering, or a current-row lookup.

title: Fence recipient-generation writes before purge migration
description: Add a generation-scoped write gate shared by every path that creates or replaces local FrontierRoot or HistoryNode envelopes and every local healing or wrap operation targeting this recipient. Operations crossing the fence remain explicit queued work or return a retryable result against the prepared basis; they do not manufacture a new timestamp, causal edge, recipient, or retry identity from a latest-row lookup. title: Reserve and finalize recipient successors without fork races
description: Define and implement a two-phase recipient-successor graph protocol before irreversible purge. A public transition reservation names predecessor P, the recursive schedule pair consisting of staged successor public key S and S next commitment T, the current full-reader proof, and the immutable retirement-batch commitment plus exact purge-operation refs defined by poc-16-x1o.20, but is explicitly not a recipient and cannot satisfy any key_wrap, request, proactive-share, or healing need. Resolve sibling reservations before P destruction with a stable equivalence rule: different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch reservations fail the claim and are ineligible; only identical P/S/T/batch retries coalesce. Independently valid operation facts carried by a mismatched or excluded reservation remain queued and are handed to poc-16-x1o.19 for explicit rebasing onto S. The recursive schedule implementation in poc-16-x1o.18 ensures the next transition advances S/(T,U) without deferring a fork. A strong snapshot tier additionally requires rollback-resistant promotion and monotonic schedule state; software providers state weaker snapshot guarantees. Only a final S fact matching the fixed P/S/T/batch claim and referencing its exact causal operation closure plus durable purge evidence after P private-key destruction becomes wrap-eligible. Mismatched, unresolved, incomplete, excluded-operation, or abandoned reservations never receive wraps.

title: Declare and build tinyp2p_bao: unbreak facts import on a fresh checkout
description:
core/bao.py does a module-scope `import tinyp2p_bao`, and both content families
import it (facts/content/file.py:12, facts/content/chunk.py:8). On any checkout
without a local build, `import facts` raises

    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tinyp2p_bao'

That is the whole facts package failing to import, not just attachments.

It resolves today only because a maturin build happens to sit at
~/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/tinyp2p_bao/. The crate is vendored at
native/bao_py/ (bao =0.13.1, pyo3 =0.28.3, abi3-py38), but nothing in the repo
builds it: no root pyproject.toml, no setup.py, no requirements file, and no
document describes a build step.

Precedent worth following rather than copying: PyNaCl is already an undeclared
dependency, named only in prose at docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md:4. The difference in kind is
that PyNaCl is one `pip install` from PyPI, while tinyp2p_bao needs a Rust
toolchain plus a maturin build of a vendored crate. A contributor can recover from
the first by reading the error; they cannot recover from the second.

Options, cheapest first:
  (a) Document the build in a root setup section and keep the dependency ambient,
      matching how pynacl is handled today.
  (b) Add a root pyproject.toml declaring pynacl and a maturin build of
      native/bao_py.
  (c) Make core/bao.py degrade: import lazily and raise a directed error naming
      the exact build command, so non-attachment use of facts keeps
      working.

(c) is worth doing regardless of (a) or (b), because it converts a package-wide
import failure into a feature-scoped one — today a missing Rust build breaks
messages, auth, and sync too, none of which touch bao.

Found while assessing whether the attachments branch could land on main; it blocks
landing on ANY branch, not just main, so it is actionable now rather than after
poc-16-t53.
acceptance_criteria: On a checkout with tinyp2p_bao NOT installed, either 'import facts' succeeds (bao imported lazily, non-attachment paths unaffected) or it fails with a directed error naming the exact build command. The build of native/bao_py is documented or automated in-repo rather than assumed present in site-packages. Verified by importing facts with tinyp2p_bao blocked via a sys.meta_path finder.
notes: Added lazy core/bao.py seam, vendored native/bao_py Cargo+maturin package and lockfile, exact build command in README/docs, and a fresh-process sys.meta_path blocker regression. python3 -m pip wheel produced cp38-abi3 wheel; isolated install round-tripped 524544 bytes/3 slices. cargo fmt and clippy --locked -D warnings pass. Full pytest: 182 passed, 1 expected skip. Own-agent review APPROVED after adversarial rejection checks (tamper/trailing/wrong root/wrong length). Claude Fable final review triggered 2026-07-25, no output before bounded 120s timeout (exit 124), unavailable; continued per user instruction.

Exercise post-purge compromise, stale snapshot, malicious re-delivery, peer lag, and interrupted rotation. File separate beads for revocation/suppression issues discovered; do not fold unrelated revocation fixes into this implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A storage-surface inventory links each secret to an owner and purge hook. Automated adversarial tests retain ciphertext plus old root and HistoryNode wraps, include a valid pre-purge wrap withheld on another peer, complete an initial F purge and at least one later eligible-cover purge, then deliver the withheld wrap and attempt every supported recovery path. All fail for the claimed tier while survivor content still opens. Memory and cache hooks verify eviction and best-effort zeroization. Backup, export, and log fixtures contain no plaintext or local private material. An auth-only infra fixture never receives reader-authorized key material. Any untestable platform guarantee is explicitly scoped and documented rather than asserted.

title: Rotate recipient eph generations on recovery-eligible key purge
description: Integrate purge-triggered recipient rotation as a resumable local state machine driven by the explicit retirement set and poc-16-x1o.16 through poc-16-x1o.21. A purge advances the recipient generation exactly once when it retires any secret recoverable through the current generation: F, a wrap-eligible HistoryNode, a generation-sealed equivalent, or material derivable through a retained generation root. Recovery eligibility is monotonic and causal from immutable secret kind plus source, sealing, recipient, and provider-policy refs; it never comes from visible-wrap inventory. Under the standard bounded provider, root and HistoryNode secrets are eligible and purge rotates even with no observed wrap; the first-F-only rule exists only for an explicit non-wrappable, non-generation-bound, non-root-derivable provider tier. From caller-supplied saved state, claim predecessor P and the immutable retirement-batch commitment, load the recursive schedule pair S/T and now-only fact timestamp, and publish a non-wrap-eligible reservation that explicitly refs every batch operation and carries its complete closed-pile dependency set. Resolve full P/S/T/batch equivalence before irreversible work; never add an operation merely because it arrived before a local boundary, and reject rather than park any incomplete reservation. Install the P generation write fence, drain or abort in-flight P-bound writers, validate the exact claimed operation closure, enumerate and migrate every survivor to S, and durably validate S/T. Only after every capacity-dependent claim, allocation, closure, migration, and T preparation succeeds may the transition retire old-generation wraps and destroy P private material. It then performs allocation-free promotion, publishes finalized S with commitment T, and completes exactly the committed operations. Every independently valid operation outside the batch—including one carried by a mismatched reservation—remains queued and rebases by explicit refs onto S; if recovery-eligible under S it enters a later unique batch and triggers the S-to-T rotation. Persist monotonic phases because database, manifest publication, fencing, schedule promotion, and hardware deletion are not one transaction. Retries reuse saved prepared state; timestamps never choose or order claims, operations, batches, or generations.
acceptance_criteria: Crash injection before and after predecessor plus batch claim, S/T load, complete reservation ingestion, full claim resolution, operation-closure validation, writer fence and drain, survivor migration, T validation, old-wrap purge, P destruction, allocation-free promotion, S finalization, excluded-operation rebase, and completion converges without exposing a reservation as a wrap target, losing survivors, changing batch membership by arrival, parking an incomplete claim, or claiming completion while old material works. Delayed P wraps cannot open after destruction. Standard healing rotates for every eligible cover purge; a first-F-only fixture is allowed only with the explicit weaker provider proof. The poc-16-x1o.16 barriers prove no P-bound authoring, seal, request, or healing commit lands after the fence or escapes the survivor scan. The poc-16-x1o.17, poc-16-x1o.18, poc-16-x1o.20, and poc-16-x1o.21 matrices prove different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are permanently invalid, only identical whole claims coalesce, closed-pile delivery order cannot change operation assignment, truncated claims reject with no pending state, three or more generations remain fork-free, a two-handle cap fails before P destruction, and a three-handle-capable non-exportable provider completes and returns to two. The poc-16-x1o.19 matrix proves every excluded valid operation rebases onto S and, when eligible, causes a second rotation; a remote peer wraps the target to S before that second purge and withholds the wrap, then destroyed S cannot open it. Neither concurrency nor retry uses timestamp arbitration, fid ranking, arrival ranking, or latest-row lookup. Locked hardware or capacity failure at every claim, fence, allocation, closure, migration, or T-preparation boundary fails closed without finalizing S, completing purge, or destroying P; crash or lock after destruction resumes allocation-free promotion from saved S/T. Auth-only infra cannot supply reader proof. Strong-tier rollback tests reject restored snapshots.
