title: Implement bounded local secret provider and encrypted cover store
description: Implement the key-provider boundary selected by the hardware ADR: generate, use, and destroy active recipient ephemeral private handles; maintain the recursively unique schedule state that fixes transition pair P/(S,T); atomically authorize a caller-supplied immutable retirement-batch commitment as part of the one-time transition claim; envelope-seal F and retained-cover nodes to the active generation; enumerate and migrate live ciphertext records without exporting a hardware private key; expose generation-scoped writer leases, close-and-drain fencing, commit compare-and-set, and the selected schedule-and-batch claim capability; and report capabilities and recovery-eligibility metadata. For independently generated non-exportable keys, steady state holds active P plus staged S. Before P destruction, transition preparation verifies S and generates and durably protects S staged-next T, so the peak is three handles and no quota-dependent allocation remains after the irreversible boundary. Final promotion destroys P and changes durable generation state to the already existing S/T pair; the next transition advances the schedule to T/U under the same rule. Standard generation sealing makes every sealed cover node recovery-eligible, so the provider reports that causal property even if shared HistoryNode wraps are disabled. It does not choose operation membership, author recipient reservations or successors, or perform purge-triggered rotation; poc-16-x1o.16 through poc-16-x1o.20 and poc-16-x1o.10 consume the primitives and own those workflows. Keep stable identity and attestation operations separate from content unwrapping. An optional first-F-only provider mode may exist only if it stores cover under independently deletable, non-generation-bound keys and proves no active recipient key or retained root can unwrap archived node ciphertext. The software test provider models deletion, rollback, cloned state, and missing monotonic claims honestly rather than claiming Secure Enclave guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests run against an in-memory fault provider and every available real or software provider. They cover three or more P/S/T/U schedule advances; two-handle steady and three-handle transition-peak counts for the non-exportable hierarchy; full P/S/T/batch claim matching; rejection of a replay with the same P/S/T but a different batch; proof that P private material cannot derive S or T; pre-destruction preparation of T; allocation-free idempotent promotion to S/T; handle deletion; wrong generation and AAD; writer-lease acquisition and drain; post-fence commit rejection; partial migration primitives; locked hardware; restart; cloned and restored state; backup restore; transient-buffer zeroization where possible; and capability reporting. Quota exhaustion at a two-handle limit fails every non-exportable rotation before P destruction, while capacity for the documented third transition handle succeeds and returns to two after promotion. Any claimed lower-peak provider has a contract test for its alternative. Key creation, claim, fence, migration, or next-key preparation errors never report unusable state as durable, never destroy P, and destroy or track orphan allocations. After P destruction, promotion and finalization consume only validated durable S/T state; a lock or crash may delay completion but cannot require a new allocation or lose S. Provider retries use caller-supplied prepared state; causal operation selection, graph resolution, evidence rebasing, and end-to-end rotation remain downstream. Stress tests keep handles bounded by the documented per-recipient steady and transition constants, independent of content count. A generation-sealed HistoryNode is reported recovery-eligible; this bead does not rotate it. No stable root API can request or derive a retired generation.

title: Encrypt messages and files with KDF leaf keys
description: Replace plaintext message and file fact payloads with versioned AEAD ciphertext using the KDF leaf selected by the explicit content coordinate and frontier ref. Authenticate all clear routing/authorization/dependency fields as AAD. Define whether file descriptors and chunks use distinct derived subkeys/nonces, and preserve sealed-but-not-yet-openable projection so ciphertext may sync before the recipient has cover material. Keep plaintext out of durable fact bytes, treap piles, manifests, delivery logs, blob filenames/metadata, and ordinary projection rows.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic multi-peer tests author, sync, open, restart, and late-deliver messages plus small/large files; ciphertext-before-wrap later opens through dependency/key healing. Tampering with ciphertext, nonce, coordinate, frontier, channel, parent, signer, chunk index, or size fails closed. Raw scans of fact/blob/index/app databases, WAL/journal files, manifests, logs, and sync payloads find no test plaintext. Same prepared authoring input retries without consulting latest state.

title: Implement exact/range puncture and durable secret erasure
description: Port poc-10 exact leaf retirement and time-prefix or range chop. Given an explicit validated victim coordinate or range and content frontier, materialize survivor siblings, atomically replace the old cover with the canonical new cover, exact-delete the leaf, descend path, and F when applicable, purge canonical secret bytes and transient caches, and retain only non-secret tombstone and retirement evidence needed to prevent resurrection. Emit an explicit retirement set for every removed F, HistoryNode, and leaf secret. For each item, carry a recovery-eligibility class derived from immutable secret kind and explicit source, recipient-generation, sealing, and wrap-policy refs. A FrontierRoot or HistoryNode that protocol policy allows any peer to wrap is conservatively eligible even when no wrap is present in the local pile; local absence is never evidence of no delayed or archived wrap. Leaf-only material may be ineligible only when the protocol causally forbids it as a wrap or generation-seal source. Rotation consumes this explicit set; neither retry state nor recovery eligibility is inferred from timestamps, latest-row lookup, or observed wrap inventory.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests puncture random leaves and ranges in varying orders and compare decryptability with an oracle. The victim cannot be derived from any retained node while every live coordinate remains openable. Duplicate or reordered purge work is idempotent from explicit operation id and basis refs. Fault tests cover the local database transaction and canonical-byte and WAL cleanup. Root and HistoryNode retirement reports recovery eligibility when a valid wrap was created remotely and withheld, and when no shared wrap is allowed but the node is sealed to the current generation. Tests distinguish a causally non-wrappable and non-generation-bound transient secret, which may skip rotation, from the same secret with a wrap, generation-seal, or retained-root recovery ref, which rotates. No implementation proves ineligibility from an empty local wrap query.

title: Implement canonical retained-cover and lazy leaf derivation
description: Represent the decryptable remainder after punctures as the canonical prefix-free sibling cover from poc-10. Derive fresh leaves from F or the deepest retained covering sibling, materialize only what authoring/opening or a puncture needs, and reject a coordinate with no retained ancestor. Persist secret-bearing cover nodes only through the selected encrypted local-secret provider; public graph/pile state may carry coordinates and tombstones but never node secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Model/property tests compare randomized author/puncture/open sequences with a simple set-of-live-leaves oracle, prove the cover is prefix-free/non-overlapping and cannot cover a punctured coordinate, and show all surviving coordinates still derive the expected leaf. Restart tests reconstruct the same cover. Measurements demonstrate no one-key-per-content durable state: fresh operation stays near one root plus lazily used leaves, and p punctures grow with the tree cover bound rather than total content count.

title: Add content frontiers, reader-bound recipient successors, and key_wrap facts
description: Port poc-10 removal_frontier and local_key_secret, workspace-scoped local_recipient_key and recipient_key, and key_wrap design using poc-16 facts and closure. Initial and replacement content-frontier facts use explicit predecessor and authority refs and bind the scope chosen by poc-16-t9f.4; random F is local secret material and never shared plaintext. The local recipient private half and key-schedule state are protected through the selected provider. The shared recipient fact is self-signed by stable device identity, causally refs an eligible full-reader authority proof for the same scope, and carries the next-recipient public-key commitment fixed by the recursive schedule claim; sync-only or infra authority cannot satisfy that need. For transition P to S, the non-wrap reservation and finalization bind S, the next commitment T that S publishes, an immutable retirement-batch commitment, and explicit refs to every included purge operation. Each fetchable transition unit carries the full dependency-first closure; missing refs reject the unit and never park. A wrap-eligible S explicitly refs P, matches the full P/S/T/batch claim, publishes the matching T commitment, carries a still-eligible reader proof and finalized transition evidence, and retires P without latest-timestamp selection. Different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are structurally ineligible; multiple valid facts for the identical whole claim denote one transition rather than competing keys or batches. Provide the codec and need distinction for the non-wrap-eligible transition reservation completed by poc-16-x1o.17, poc-16-x1o.20, and poc-16-x1o.21: a reservation or staged public-key commitment is not a recipient and cannot satisfy request, proactive-share, healing, or key_wrap validation. Proactive sharing, key requests, and healing all need the same reader proof and a finalized recipient. A key_wrap binds scope, frontier, recipient generation and fact id, reader-authority ref, algorithm and version, WrappedSecretKind of FrontierRoot or HistoryNode, exact node coordinate, source and tombstone context, recovery-eligibility policy ref, authorized sender, and ciphertext as AEAD associated data. Root and HistoryNode sources permitted by healing are recovery-eligible whether or not a recipient has yet observed their wrap.
acceptance_criteria: Real X25519 plus AEAD tests cover initial F distribution, root and retained HistoryNode wraps, two full-reader peers, an auth-only infra peer, multiple frontiers per recipient, wrong scope, frontier, reader proof, secret kind, node coordinate, recipient or AAD, replay, tamper, predecessor from another device, successor before predecessor, duplicate delivery, retry, and concurrent successor attempts. Schema and closure tests across at least P/S/T/U reject a direct successor whose public key, published next commitment, or retirement-batch commitment differs from the provider claim; coalesce only identical P/S/T/batch retries; prove every included operation travels in the reservation pile by dependency-first closure; reject a truncated reservation without pending state; and prove a bare, losing, unresolved, incomplete, or abandoned reservation cannot be used as a recipient or key_wrap target. Only matching finalization evidence can enable S. The infra peer may sync and validate ciphertext but cannot publish an eligible content recipient, satisfy a request, or receive proactive or healing wraps. After finalized successor closure new wraps never target P, and delayed P wraps cannot be opened after private-key purge. A retired root or leaf cannot be mislabeled as a live HistoryNode. Shared facts contain only public or ciphertext material; local F, private keys, and schedule state never enter synced trees, piles, manifests, delivery logs, app projections, or sync. Schedule, batch, closed-delivery, and destructive-race tests belong to poc-16-x1o.18, poc-16-x1o.20, poc-16-x1o.21, and poc-16-x1o.17.

title: Specify explicit content coordinates and causal encryption refs
description: Define the shared and local fact shapes after poc-16-t9f.4 records workspace-frontier versus channel-frontier scope. A shared content fact carries an explicit fresh 256-bit content coordinate or equivalent collision-resistant prepared nonce, its scoped content-frontier ref, authorization refs, and ciphertext. Timestamp is captured as now on first authoring and may select the time-tree bucket only. Retry reuses saved prepared inputs and never queries the latest timestamp, key, or frontier to manufacture determinism. Derived local KDF and retirement artifacts carry no timestamp or copy the basis fact timestamp as inert metadata. Content-frontier and recipient-key successor facts explicitly name predecessors. Every recipient key also names a causal content-reader authority proof for the selected scope; auth-only membership is not such a proof. Key requests, proactive sharing, and key_wrap creation need that proof in closure. Each wrap names recipient, frontier, wrapped-secret kind, exact root or HistoryNode coordinate, and an explicit recovery-eligibility source or policy ref. Suppression and deletion name victim or death key so closure, not temporal comparison, relates facts.
acceptance_criteria: A schema and closure diagram plus codecs pin every ref, need, signed field, coordinate, recovery-eligibility bit or policy ref, reader-authority proof, and AEAD associated-data field. Tests prove two facts from one author with the same timestamp get distinct leaves; retrying a saved prepared command is byte-identical without a database read or clock call; out-of-order arrival converges by dependency closure; changing timestamp alone cannot grant authority, prove content-reader eligibility, select an active recipient, supersede a key, or satisfy a causal need; and a sync-only or infra participant cannot construct a recipient pile that satisfies wrap or healing eligibility.

title: Decide secure-hardware key hierarchy and purge guarantee tiers
description: Choose how poc-16 protects a potentially large retained KDF cover without one Secure Enclave or KeyStore handle per content key. Separate stable device signing and attestation identity from rotating content-unwrapping and key-schedule state. Compare independently generated non-exportable recipient ephemeral handles, a deterministic forward schedule guarded by rollback-resistant monotonic state, a permanent enclave root that can serve only the live schedule position, and any independently deletable non-generation-bound node-key option proposed for the first-F-only special case. Select a recursively anti-fork transition-claim primitive: for transition P to S, the predecessor state or rollback-resistant one-time claim fixes S, the next public key T that S will commit, and the immutable causal retirement-batch commitment; at the next transition the advanced state fixes T, U, and its next exact batch. Different-S, same-S/different-T, or same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are structurally invalid, while identical whole claims denote one transition. Account for the non-exportable hierarchy as two steady handles (active plus staged-next) and a three-handle transition peak (P, S, and S staged-next T before P destruction), unless an alternative proves a lower bound without post-destruction allocation, unbounded precomputation, or making P derive S or T. Reject a stable dev_box or root that can derive an old generation, reopen an archived wrap, unwrap an archived cover blob, reuse retired schedule state, or authorize two valid schedule or batch claims for one strong-tier predecessor. Define cover envelope encryption, survivor migration, writer fencing, schedule and batch claim, handle destruction and garbage collection, backup behavior, and guarantees possible on Apple, Android, TPM, and software-only providers.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR selects the primary hierarchy and portable fallback, with steady and transition-peak handle counts, backup and restore behavior, enclave API assumptions, crash windows, generation write-fence primitives, recursive unique-schedule plus causal-batch claim, and explicit normal-disk, hardware-backed, and rollback-resistant tiers. Tests perform three or more generations and prove each accepted transition claim P/(S,T,batch), then S/(T,U,batch2), is uniquely fixed; a successor public key, next commitment, or batch commitment that differs from the claim is invalid; and P private material alone cannot derive or open S or T. The independently generated non-exportable design budgets and exercises a three-handle peak before P destruction and returns to two; an alternative lower peak needs executable proof. A restored old sealed-state snapshot cannot recover retired keys or authorize a second claim in any tier claiming rollback resistance; software schedule designs state weaker snapshot and clone guarantees. The ADR includes rotate, migrate, destroy, claim, reservation, promotion, and finalization protocols and rejects deterministic old-key derivation from a retained root unless hardware monotonic state makes retired positions permanently inaccessible. If it permits a first-F-only mode, it proves retained cover nodes are neither shared-wrappable nor sealed or derivable through the active recipient generation or retained root; otherwise that mode is rejected.
close_reason: Selected the bounded independent-generation hierarchy and guarantee tiers; documented the runtime-facing contract and realistic executable fault model. Final review findings are intentionally deferred to poc-16-x1o.23 through poc-16-x1o.27 under the requested tracking-only policy.

title: Port the two-axis KDF core with cross-implementation vectors
description: Implement a small pure/executable core for F → power-of-two time-range splits → within-bucket 256-bit content-coordinate trie, preserving poc-10's domain separation (`topo time split v1`, `topo trie split v1`) unless the source-contract bead versions a change. Time is only an address into the first axis; the fresh content coordinate supplies uniqueness on the second. Make child derivation, coverage checks, coordinate encoding, and AEAD leaf-key derivation explicit and usable by running encryption/puncture code.
acceptance_criteria: Known-answer tests consume the frozen poc-10/poc-16 fixtures and cover root boundaries, left/right splits, minute/bucket edges, 256 trie bits, invalid geometry, domain separation, and distinct same-timestamp content coordinates. Property tests show a child is deterministic from explicit inputs and no API reads a clock or database. Runtime content encryption calls this verified/tested core rather than a parallel model.

title: Freeze poc-10 encryption lineage, threat model, and test vectors
description: Turn the relevant poc-10 lineage into the port source contract: 7f60936f and ad380cb4 for two-axis per-content puncturing; 536b13c3, 9b40f352, and bdaa60f6 for derive, wipe, and retained-sibling recovery; 178f198b through 341b8c37 to ed04d84f and 122cc471 for wrap-bound root-loss recipient rotation and purge; and later key healing that wraps retained HistoryNode secrets after F is gone. Resolve the historical wording in favor of key-purge-triggered rotation, then close the distributed composition gap: local absence of a wrap never proves a secret unrecoverable because another peer may delay a valid wrap, and forbidding shared wraps still does not prove safety when retained cover is envelope-sealed to the live recipient generation. Any root or retained node that can be a wrap source or is generation-bound is recovery-eligible from causal source, sealing, and policy refs; its purge advances the recipient generation even if this peer never observed a wrap. The original first-F-only result applies only when retained nodes are explicitly non-wrappable and non-generation-bound with no retained-root recovery path. Record as intentional poc-16 additions the generation write fence before survivor migration, immutable causally referenced retirement-batch claim with excluded-operation rebasing, closed-pile non-parking transition delivery, non-wrap reservation, recursive P/S/T then S/T/U schedule claim, and steady versus transition-peak handle budget. Record post-purge disk and snapshot attackers, availability tradeoffs, cloned-state boundary, content-reader eligibility, and the narrower contribution from poc-13 connection ephemeral-secret purge behavior. Identify every intentional deviation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in design record maps each poc-10 source type and transition to its poc-16 counterpart, cites source commits, and contains state and secret ownership tables plus an adversary matrix. Versioned fixtures cover F generation, both KDF domains, splits and leaf derivation, root and HistoryNode wrap/open, first-F and later-cover purges, a remote wrap delivered after purge, generation-sealed cover, a predecessor-bound writer racing survivor scan, identical and mismatched P/S/T/batch reservations across S/T/U, a complete reservation carrying an included operation in closure with a later standalone duplicate, a truncated reservation rejected without parking, and an excluded operation observed before the accepted reservation. The record states key purge—not deletion timestamp or observed wrap—is the trigger; recovery eligibility includes shared, sealed, and retained-root paths; reservations cannot receive wraps; only the exact causally committed batch completes with P and excluded valid operations rebase to S; same-S/different-T and same-P/S/T/different-batch are conflicts; independently generated non-exportable rotation peaks at three handles; incomplete piles reject rather than wait; and timestamps are now-only metadata or addresses, never causality, authority, eligibility, supersession, assignment, winner selection, or retry ordering.
close_reason: Frozen poc-10/poc-13 source lineage, causal purge and recipient-transition contract, versioned cryptographic/lifecycle vectors, full test coverage, and accepted independent review.

title: Puncturable content encryption + KDF history tree (poc-10 port)
description: Port poc-10 content encryption into poc-16: a random secret F per content frontier; a domain-separated two-axis KDF with time bucket as an address only and then a 256-bit content-coordinate trie; lazy leaf derivation; a canonical retained-sibling cover; exact/range puncture; encrypted content facts; and wrap-based recovery. Recipient rotation is driven by key purge, not by a wrap lookup. On each peer, a purge that retires any secret causally eligible for recovery through the current recipient generation—F or a HistoryNode that peers may wrap, or a generation-sealed local equivalent—triggers one eager recipient ephemeral-key rotation for that purge transition even when no wrap is visible locally. Recovery eligibility comes from immutable secret kind plus explicit source, sealing, and recipient policy refs and is monotonic; an unseen, delayed, archived, or locally sealed recovery path is always assumed possible. Under the standard bounded-provider design, both FrontierRoot and HistoryNode are wrap-eligible or envelope-sealed to the active generation, so each purge that retires one rotates. The poc-10 first-F-only result is an optional special case only if an explicit causal provider policy makes retained nodes both impossible shared-wrap sources and impossible to recover through the recipient generation or any retained root, for example through independently deletable non-generation-bound node keys with an honestly weaker snapshot tier. A transient leaf-only purge may skip only under the same no-recovery proof. For transition P to S, a non-wrap-eligible reservation carries a recursively unique P/S/T schedule claim and a provider-authorized immutable retirement-batch commitment. The reservation explicitly refs every included purge operation, and its serialized ingress unit carries the complete dependency-first closure; only identical P/S/T/batch retries coalesce. Different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are invalid. An incomplete reservation rejects immediately and never parks waiting for a missing operation. The transition fences and drains P-bound writers before scanning survivors, migrates all survivors, prepares the full S/T state, destroys P, and only then makes S wrap-eligible. Independently valid operation evidence outside the committed batch never joins retroactively, regardless of arrival: it rebases by explicit refs onto S and causes S-to-T rotation when recovery-eligible. If a provider cannot prove the unique schedule and batch claim, it retains P and fails closed. Keep content-frontier rotation for membership removal distinct from purge-triggered recipient rotation. A long-lived device identity may survive, but no stable dev_box, root operation, archived or delayed wrap, generation-sealed blob, post-fence write, sibling claim, partial pile, or rollbackable snapshot may reconstruct retired material in a tier claiming that protection. Retained covers are encrypted as data rather than one enclave handle per item. An independently generated non-exportable recipient hierarchy uses two handles at steady state and a three-handle P/S/T transition peak; a permanent hardware root or lower-handle design is allowed only with non-rollbackable schedule retirement and an explicit guarantee. Timestamps are authored as now and have zero causal, authorization, supersession, eligibility, operation-assignment, winner-selection, or retry-ordering weight; refs, needs, transition-batch claims, and pile closure establish relationships. Derived local artifacts carry no timestamp or copy a basis timestamp only as inert metadata. Compose confidentiality retirement with global suppression without putting suppression into stable validity.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed. Cross-implementation vectors pin the poc-10 KDF geometry and intentional poc-16 coordinate, fencing, recursive-schedule, causal-batch, closed-pile, evidence-rebase, and rotation deviations. Realistic multi-peer tests prove survivors remain decryptable while a suppressed or retired leaf, F, cover, old wrap, sealed blob, superseded private key, plaintext cache or WAL copy, and—on the strong tier—a restored sealed-state snapshot cannot recover deleted plaintext after completion. Delayed-wrap tests cover P and a later wrap to S followed by S-to-T purge. Barrier and multi-replica tests prove no P-bound writer commits after the fence, every pre-fence survivor migrates, reservations cannot receive wraps, different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are invalid across at least P/S/T/U, and excluded operation evidence rebases and completes in a later rotation. Identical accepted graphs yield identical operation-to-generation assignments under every closed-pile delivery order: a causally included operation rides the reservation closure and any later standalone copy deduplicates, while an excluded operation observed early remains queued for S. Truncated reservation piles reject without pending state or destructive side effects, then the same prepared fact succeeds when resent with its complete closure. The non-exportable provider proves two steady handles, succeeds through a three-handle transition peak, returns to two, and fails closed before P destruction when capped at two. Fault injection proves retries resume from saved state, never create timestamp or causal data from lookup, rotate once for each committed transition batch with recovery-eligible work, and skip only under explicit no-recovery policy. Auth-only infra lacks reader proof for recipients, requests, proactive shares, or healing wraps. Scale results show secret state grows with canonical cover and handles with active recipient generations rather than content count, and measure fence, rebase, fanout, healing, conservative rotation, and rewrap costs. Documentation distinguishes storage deletion, hardware deletion, rollback-resistant erasure, and weaker clone or snapshot tiers.

title: Suppression closure edge in the kernel (resolve_supp), validity-independent

Mirrors resolve_deps. Concurrency needs NO write-time match: T_supp is a CvRDT, concurrent deletion+target writes converge (two-root merge = set union); the only cost is latency-to-visibility (self-healing staleness), not a data race.

Cost O(S·log N) at ingest, monotone, paid once.

description: Reusable method exercised during F1 final validation: when a behavior test over random keys fails, inspect and report the fixture-shape precondition separately from the behavior assertion, then repeat the exact isolated case across fresh seeds. The full suite produced disjoint held_pages/pages in test_warm_sync_fetches_no_closure_siblings, while five immediate isolated runs passed, mapping the failure to existing poc-16-npz rather than the ObjectStore changes.

title: Bound non-interactive Cloudflare build and test subprocesses
description: Deployment mutations now have deadlines, but non-interactive build/test paths still call Pywrangler or pytest with timeout=None. A stuck package resolver, custom-build hook, or dry-run can hang CI and release automation indefinitely. The interactive dev server is intentionally long-running and is outside this bound.
acceptance_criteria: build and each finite test subprocess have explicit separately named deadlines; injected TimeoutExpired probes require no sleeping and preserve the command phase in the error; workerd child cleanup still terminates/kills reliably; dev remains interactive. Documentation distinguishes finite release commands from the long-running dev command.
notes: Reusable probe: capture every subprocess edge in non-interactive management commands and fail when timeout is None, with an explicit allowlist only for supervised interactive processes.

title: Centralize the provider-neutral logical-key byte budget
description: Host preflight currently duplicates the longest emitted core key as pile/<16>/<64> so it can prove workspace base prefixes fit S3's 1024-byte physical-key ceiling before any mutation. core.object_store.validate_key defines characters/segments but no total byte ceiling or emitted-key shape budget. A future longer core namespace can silently make host preflight unsound again; FsStore can also defer an oversized logical key to platform path-limit errors.
acceptance_criteria: Define one provider-neutral maximum logical-key byte budget or a central emitted-key-shape contract consumed by validate_key and host prefix validation. Tests enumerate every core-produced key namespace, prove each fits, ratchet the longest shape, reject one-byte-over logical and physical keys before I/O across FsStore/S3/R2, and fail when a new producer bypasses the declared budget.
notes: Reusable drift-finder from the independent poc-16-x1p.6 review: compare every literal/formatted store key producer against preflight's assumed maximum, then add a negative control one byte beyond the provider's physical limit. Current code is safe because pile/<16>/<64> is the longest emitted key; this is a future-proofing ratchet, not an x1p.6 blocker.

title: Batch idempotent immutable-object pushes without coupling them to fact piles
description: The correctness repair for directed peers sends each locally available Bao object through an individually bounded, hash-verified PUT before the fact-only pile. This preserves retry safety and keeps piles small, but a 10 GiB file can require tens of thousands of HTTP requests. Design a bounded batch or resumable missing-object negotiation that retains objects-first publication, per-object integrity, idempotent conditional create, provider limits, and fact/blob separation.
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark and request-count test cover large multi-slice files; the selected protocol has explicit request/response byte ceilings, splits adaptively, retries without duplicate semantic effects, never delivers the fact pile after an available-object upload failure, and remains compatible with read-only peers.

title: Make ordinary object-store queue mutations explicitly idempotent
description: Authoritative root/obj semantics are precise, but pile, invite, and failed queue operations still use ordinary mutable put/delete outcomes. Reduce ambiguity where keys are content addressed: use conditional create for piles and immutable quarantine payloads, define idempotent delete/retirement outcomes, and retain overwrite only where a real node-local mutable record needs it. Unknown outcomes must be reconciled by key/value read rather than guessed.
acceptance_criteria: The store contract identifies every mutable namespace and its idempotency rule; content-keyed piles/quarantine payloads cannot clobber different bytes; replayed puts/deletes are harmless; ambiguity tests show recovery without deleting authoritative objects or another member’s work.

title: rebuild's foreign-envelope branch CASes from a base that Publisher.base() never validated
description:
core/node.py:456-464. When the current root will not decode, rebuild calls
Publisher.same_snapshot_envelope (publication.py:66-78), which compares the
foreign JSON against meta['root-bytes'] -- the last root THIS index stamped --
and if five fields match, calls self.commit(ws, reuse=False, _base=base).

Passing _base skips Publisher.base() (publication.py:39-52) entirely, so there
is no check that the index is currently stamped for anything at all. It can be
mid-dirty: a prior publisher.dirty(base) deletes meta['root'] (publication.py:64).
The node then compiles a root purely from local SQLite and CASes it over the
foreign one.

On a shared bucket, two co-tenants running different LAYOUT stamps
(manifest.py:25) would each keep rewriting the other's root, with _sync_index
giving up after 8 attempts (node.py:245). Because the content stays
semantically identical this is livelock and mutual clobbering rather than
corruption -- but it is a write loop with no backoff and no detection.

tests/test_shared_bucket_node.py:400 covers only the negative case: a DIFFERENT
snapshot is correctly refused, single-threaded. The positive case -- a matching
envelope, concurrently, from a possibly-dirty index -- is untested.

Related: the same function is the reason poc-16-nuk exists, since this branch is
one of the two places rebuild re-reads root to adopt a newer base.

title: Orphaned objects grow with publication attempts, not commits, and nothing bounds them
description:
Every lost CAS leaves behind a complete set of path-copied tree pages, leaf
piles and closure siblings: publication.py:126-129 emits them all before the CAS
at publication.py:184. Nothing ever removes them. FsStore.delete refuses obj/
outright (store.py:138-141), RemoteStore has no write surface at all, and
DESIGN.md states physical GC is unbuilt.

tests/test_shared_bucket_model.py:88 asserts that pre-CAS orphans are HARMLESS,
which is true and is the right safety property. Nothing asserts they are
BOUNDED, which is the availability property. With N contending writers, stored
bytes grow with attempts rather than with commits, and the retry-cost defect
(poc-16-1uc) makes attempts superlinear in N because each loser recompiles the
whole corpus before trying again.

So this is not merely "GC is future work" -- it is a concurrency amplifier
specific to the shared-bucket deployment, and it deserves a measurement before
it deserves a collector. Extend the F2 fuzzer to report bytes-written per
committed root as writer count rises; if the ratio grows with N, that number is
the argument for prioritizing GC.

title: Node.rebuild re-reads root to adopt a newer base, contradicting the stated law
description:
DESIGN.md, under Store and publication: "Catalog settlement returns a
publication plan pinned to the exact root bytes and ETag that settlement read.
Object and tree compilation never rereads `root` to adopt a newer base."

core/node.py rebuild() rereads root and adopts a newer base at two points:

  node.py:462-464   foreign-envelope branch, after commit(..., _base=base)
  node.py:481-483   semantic-upgrade branch, after commit(..., reuse=False)

Both do the same three lines: raw = st.get("root"); base = (raw, h(raw));
root = manifest.decode_root(raw). Between our own CAS and that re-read another
writer can land its own CAS, so the adopted base can be a root we never wrote.

Effect appears benign rather than unsafe: the adopted root is a real committed
root, resident() then reads that root's manifest, settlement derives from it,
and publish CASes against its ETag -- so the pinning is internally consistent
and a concurrent change still loses at the CAS. What is wrong is the stated
law, which is currently false for the one code path most likely to run during
contention and recovery.

Resolve one way or the other: either re-read into a fresh pinned pair and say
so in DESIGN.md (the law becomes "compilation never MIXES bases"), or hoist the
re-read so rebuild restarts cleanly from a single pin. The second is easier to
reason about and matches how Publisher.base() already behaves.

Related evidence gathered during review: racing writers DO converge on this
path. Three nodes with independent SQLite, racing deletions (which force the
non-incremental publish branch), 4 lost CASes retried -- 5 commits, every one
agreeing with a from-scratch rebuild of its own manifest, all nodes converged,
bucket history linearizable. So this is a documentation/clarity defect, not a
known correctness break.

title: No fault injection anywhere on the sync/HTTP path
description:
The sync dial is the only place two nodes actually touch, and none of its
failure modes are exercised by a real fault.

core/node.py record_sync_failure is called directly by tests; no test ever
triggers it with a peer that hangs, half-responds, returns a 5xx mid-pull,
closes the connection between the root read and the page reads, or returns a
short body. tests/test_blackbox.py test_alice_bob_carol is the only real
subprocess/socket daemon test in the repo and it is a single scripted happy
path.

This matters more than it looks, because core/sync.py sync() is not
transactional. One dial performs, in order: an action pull, an action push, a
push of local-only keys, a pull of remote ranges, a turn, a blob fetch, and
then a cache update (sync.py:143-204). A failure at any of those points leaves
the sync_cache in a state the next dial inherits -- note the deliberate
retag = None after a push (sync.py:189) and the cache.pop("blobs") on
incomplete blob fetch (sync.py:204). Those are the right instincts, and they
are untested.

Add: a peer harness that can fail at each seam, plus assertions that the next
dial recovers, that no partial state is stamped, and that a failed dial never
advances the local root.

title: Simplify: unify the two kernel contexts behind one declared protocol
description:
core/kernel.py carries two context implementations selected by duck typing:

  offer_src   branches on hasattr(db, "resolve_offer")   (kernel.py:138)
  proof_rank  branches on hasattr(db, "rank")            (kernel.py:200)

MemoryContext (kernel.py:64-121) is the database-free one used by
drain()/kernel() -- the Worker authorization path and the ingress door.
Context (kernel.py:30-61) is the SQLite one used by Catalog._accept. Their
interfaces are not the same shape: Context has no has_fact(), so _judge() would
raise AttributeError on it. The two are held in agreement only by convention.

This is the one place in an otherwise strikingly one-directional design where
the same question has two implementations and no declared contract between
them. Everything else in core/ has exactly one: one pile codec, one treap
codec, one fact codec, one registry, one CAS.

Replace the hasattr dispatch with an explicit protocol both classes implement,
so the differential fuzzer in poc-16-kgp.6 enforces a stated contract rather
than an accident, and so a future third context (a store-only publisher, see
poc-16-bw3) has something to conform to.

Smaller related cleanups found while reading:
  - core/manifest.py is named "manifest" but its docstring and DESIGN.md both
    call the thing it implements RangeTree. Pick one name.
  - btreap.Built.pages means "logical pages" from build() and "writes
    performed" from update() (btreap.py:107-130 vs 291,369). Two meanings, one
    field.

title: need_key(requires=...) is readable by the Worker but never written by either build path
description:
core/indexes.py need_key takes a `requires` component and folds it into the
canonical authority address (indexes.py:74-80). Both build paths write only
the empty form: the incremental path calls need_key(*address) with a 3-tuple
(indexes.py:253) and the full path does the same (indexes.py:312).

core/worker.py WorkerView.authority_provider accepts `requires` and passes it
through to need_key (worker.py:88-90). Any caller that passes a non-empty
requires therefore looks up an address that is never written, gets None, and
DENIES -- silently, and only on the Worker path, while the SQLite path
(kernel.offer_src, kernel.py:153-159) handles requires correctly.

Nothing triggers it today: the only live requires= is
facts/auth/device_invite.py:77, which flows through offer_src, and
facts/auth/request.py:63 calls authority_provider with no requires. So this is
a loaded trap for the next family author rather than a live bug -- the client
would accept and the Worker would refuse, which is the worst shape of
divergence this architecture can have.

Note _committed_needs_match already works around it by looking up the base
address and then checking co-offers against the provider's FactRecord
(worker.py:118-137). That is the correct design. Given that, the fix is
probably to DELETE the requires parameter from need_key and
authority_provider, so the tree has one address shape and the co-offer check
has one implementation.

title: A peer that echoes our action_etag silently disables the action-sync leg in both directions
description:
core/manifest.py decode_root validates action_etag only as valid_fid
(manifest.py:293) -- it is a free 64-hex field, bound to nothing. core/sync.py
then trusts it for a skip decision:

    same_actions = remote_root and local_before
        and remote_snapshot.action_etag
        == manifest.decode_root(local_before).action_etag     (sync.py:130-132)

When it matches, remote_actions is populated from our OWN local SQLite
(sync.py:134-140). That value is then used BOTH ways: pull_actions receives it
as `rows` and pulls nothing, and push_actions receives it as `remote_rows` and
computes an empty push set (sync.py:143-145, 300-318).

So a peer that simply copies our action_etag out of our root makes the entire
authenticated action leg a no-op in both directions.

Severity is bounded rather than critical: removal facts still travel as
ordinary facts through the RangeTree diff, and merge() re-archives and
re-settles them (core/node.py:383-384), so the removal is recovered. What is
lost is the evidence leg and its independent validation.

The reason to fix it anyway is that DESIGN.md states the opposite -- "Workers
never trust it, and action evidence remains authoritative only through the
authenticated trees" -- and that is true of Workers and false of sync. Either
bind action_etag to the SuppTree root it claims to summarize, or drop the
shortcut and let the oid comparison do the pruning it already does everywhere
else.

Fuzz assertion to add regardless: a peer lying about action_etag must not
change the converged state of either side.

title: F7: widen the abstract shared-bucket model to N writers and the real snapshot shape
description:
tests/shared_bucket_model.py is the best piece of concurrency evidence in the
repo: a breadth-first explorer over an explicit small-state machine that
returns a MINIMAL counterexample schedule, with mutation switches proving the
laws are non-vacuous. Two limits keep it from covering what it is cited for.

1. It is hardcoded to two writers and one reader (initial_state() at
   shared_bucket_model.py:162-171). Three writers is where retry-of-a-retry
   scenarios begin. Parameterize the writer count and keep the state budget
   honest -- the explorer already has a max_states guard.

2. Its snapshot is a 2-branch toy (manifest + index over shared leaves,
   shared_bucket_model.py:41-48). The real root binds a manifest plus THREE
   trees plus an action_etag, and the trees are path-copied rather than
   rebuilt. "Split root generation" in the model is a single equality between
   two branches; in production the equivalent failure is one tree advanced
   and another not. Extend the model snapshot to the real arity so the
   split-root law actually covers the shape that exists.

Also worth encoding as a model law: a reader that pins a root must be unable
to observe an ACTIVE suppression slot whose action fact is absent from that
root's manifest. That is a cross-structure law the current 2-branch model
cannot express.
notes: The current explorer is 1,000 states by default and 18,456 with crashes, leaving room for a third writer and real root arity. Extend the snapshot to manifest + all three authenticated trees + action_etag and add the cross-structure law that ACTIVE suppression evidence is manifest-reachable. ABA is excluded today by monotone toy token sets. First find whether full production roots can go A->B->A under deactivate/reactivate or action winner changes. Model provider tokens as opaque and possibly reusable. Assert each CAS can be linearized against the then-current token; do not reject duplicate expected strings globally. If byte-identical A is an extensional state, show why stale computation from A remains safe. Otherwise add an explicit generation to root bytes and test it.

title: Bound file queries to one descriptor's chunks
description: A file resolve/save/bytes call currently scans every file_bao and chunk_bao fact and performs hashing/Bao verification for every resident slice while holding the Node lock. The canonical catalog is intentionally simple, but one file query should not cost O(all workspace chunks).
design: Keep facts(fid, blob) as the sole canonical body store and do not reintroduce app.db, family tables, or materialized views. Extend the generic family-declared index only as needed so a file descriptor selects its own chunk facts (for example, an indexed parent/reference key). Assemble the result in the file family. Pin the required local state under the Node lock, then decode/hash/Bao-verify outside the lock where concurrency semantics permit.
acceptance_criteria: A single file resolve/save/bytes operation decodes and verifies only that file's descriptor and chunks; unrelated workspace files are not visited. Canonical blobs remain the source of truth, there is no projection database or file-family table, concurrent root/query behavior remains safe, and a realistic multi-file test instruments decoding or Bao verification to prove unrelated chunks are untouched. The resulting code is at least as readable and does not increase total production LOC without explicit justification.
close_reason: Implemented generic explicit-reference routes, bounded file queries, coherent unlocked verification, migration crash safety, and realistic regressions.

title: Simplify the client projection boundary if it reduces total code
description: WHY: Client nodes currently keep a separate app.db plus log, cursor, replay, and reproject recovery around the workspace catalog. This is understandable but may duplicate the root-stamp recovery transaction already present in the workspace index. CF Workers must remain database-free; clients may use SQLite. WHAT: Prototype one workspace-local transactional projection boundary, measure total branches/LOC and crash semantics, and keep it only if it is materially simpler rather than a file move.
design: Candidate: place family projection tables in the workspace index transaction, use root-stamp mismatch as the sole crash recovery rule, and remove app cursor/log only if exact replay and blob-received semantics remain clear. Never introduce SQLite into WorkerView or mint.
acceptance_criteria: Either land a design with fewer total production lines and fewer recovery states while preserving projection crash/restart, blob arrival, suppression, rebuild, and multi-workspace tests, or document the measured reason the existing separate pump is simpler and discard the prototype.
close_reason: Replaced app.db, projection pump/log/cursor, and family materialization tables with one canonical fact-blob catalog plus generic type/offer indexes and query-time family assembly. Production LOC and recovery states decreased; WorkerView remains SQLite-free. Added migration, restart, corruption-reindex, blob, suppression, and crash tests.

title: Make suppression-state publication incremental without another tree
description: WHY: Ordinary authenticated-index updates still enumerate the full effective action table, even when no suppression state changed. WHAT: Feed exact changed suppression ids from Catalog settlement into Publisher/indexes and path-copy only those FactTree corroboration and SuppTree slots. Keep the composite root and one B-treap codec; do not add a second action/removal index.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict-free ordinary append performs no full SELECT over effective suppression actions; action add/clear and duplicate-winner changes still produce byte-identical roots to a full rebuild; realistic trace and equivalence tests ratchet both properties.
notes: Implemented exact changed-SID propagation through Eligibility and PublicationPlan. Conflict-free appends reuse the pinned action_etag, perform only indexed action point reads, and path-copy only new reservations; activation and winner deltas update only their FactTree/SuppTree slots. Action facts are resolved through catalog callbacks rather than actions.j. Added SQL trace/query bound, path-copy delta, randomized incremental-vs-full, clear, and evidence-only plan coverage. Validation: 254 pytest tests pass; latency benchmark 1000/5000/10000 passes; compileall and diff check clean; production Python LOC 6810 -> 6849 (+39).
close_reason: Exact incremental suppression publication and equivalence/query-count ratchets implemented and validated.

title: Thin Node with a stable family-neutral admission catalog
description: core/node.py still combines turn orchestration with local account configuration, application projection, canonical-proof quarantine, suppression projection, and family-registry interpretation. The current delete-to-quarantine-JSON/reinsert cycle duplicates fact storage and SQL mutation paths, while principal reservation rules leak concrete offer kinds into core indexing.
design: Keep Node as the serial workspace coordinator. Replace physical fact deletion/reinsertion and the quarantine offer cache with one immutable admitted-fact catalog plus a derived eligible/proof set. Have family policy declare principal and liveness suppression reservations so indexes and suppression_state iterate data rather than naming member/device offer kinds. Move application projection and local account concerns behind their existing keychain/pump boundaries only where doing so removes duplicate coordination paths; do not perform file-only extraction.
acceptance_criteria: core/node.py retains orchestration but no quarantine JSON restore/delete machinery, application schema construction, or concrete fact/offer kind tests; opposite-arrival, shadow/restore, rebuild, suppression, daemon, and property suites remain green; production Python LOC decreases overall rather than merely moving the same methods to new files.
close_reason: Landed the stable admission catalog, family-owned named authority policy, DB-free Worker judge, composite authenticated indexes, thin workspace runtime/publication boundaries, and realistic convergence/crash/deletion tests; 219 tests pass and production LOC decreases.

title: Rename suppression state and document authenticated index invariants
description: The stateful core/actions.py name is ambiguous, and core/indexes.py does not clearly explain its three security-critical authenticated views. Rename the module to suppression_state.py and document the lookup questions, CLEAR/ACTIVE semantics, duplicated action witness invariant, and incremental-versus-bulk equivalence.
design: Keep core/suppression.py as the pure clear-envelope selector/target vocabulary. Move admitted action state, liveness scopes, screening, and local reverse projection to core/suppression_state.py. Document the three tree schemas and atomic/deterministic publication invariants beside core/indexes.py.
acceptance_criteria: No core/actions.py or imports remain; behavior tests use core.suppression_state; a reader of core/indexes.py can determine what each tree maps, why FactTree and SuppTree both bind an active action, what CLEAR and ACTIVE certify, and which determinism/rebuild invariants incremental updates preserve.
close_reason: Renamed the stateful module to suppression_state.py, documented all three authenticated index roles and CLEAR/ACTIVE/atomic/determinism invariants, updated behavioral imports, and verified the full 208-test suite.

title: Eliminate the full canonical-key scan on commit
description: Authenticated trees and changed manifest ranges update incrementally, but each commit still scans every indexed fact key to derive the canonical range partition. This is the remaining corpus-sized cost in hot posting.
design: Use the published authenticated RangeTree itself as the persistent range map. For each new canonical key, perform a bounded predecessor/successor lookup, verify the selected old pile, union its members with the additions, and path-copy replacements. Content-derived cuts never disappear, so only those old leaves can split. Keep the full catalog-backed build solely for client repair, format cutover, deactivation, and authority changes.
acceptance_criteria: A one-fact hot commit does not call Node.keys or execute a corpus-wide ordered key scan; incremental and from-scratch builds produce byte-identical roots under randomized insertion orders; realistic latency tests show sublinear touched objects and no regression in sync diffing.
notes: 2026-07-29 correction: the original close reason's SQLite neighborhood was removed to preserve client/CF read isomorphism. Incremental publication now uses bounded authenticated RangeTree neighbor reads; fact_keys and fact_boundaries SQLite indexes no longer exist. Randomized updates remain byte-identical to full builds.
close_reason: Incremental publication finds affected leaves with bounded authenticated RangeTree predecessor/successor reads, verifies and extends those piles, and path-copies canonical rows. No SQLite range directory, fact_keys/fact_boundaries index, Node.keys call, or corpus scan remains; randomized roots equal full builds and sync still prunes by OID.

title: Make index generation stamping exception-safe
description: An exception partway through _stamp() can leave an implicit SQLite transaction open with a visible uncommitted root row. _sync_index then mistakes it for alignment and the next merge fails BEGIN with a nested-transaction error. Roll back partial stamp writes and make same-process recovery converge.
acceptance_criteria: A fault between root and version stamp writes leaves no open transaction; the retained pile retries in the same process and index/app stamps converge to the published root.
close_reason: Index generation stamping now rolls back partial writes; trigger-backed atomicity and mid-stamp same-process retry regressions pass.

title: Keep changed-fid projection filtering linear
description: Device reconciliation tests membership in merge's changed-fid list for every closure-expanded valid, making bulk ingest O(U*V). Normalize changed IDs to a set once at the projection boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Changed-fid filtering uses set-like membership and a realistic bulk regression demonstrates it does not perform list membership per valid.
close_reason: Projection boundary normalizes changed ids to a frozenset once; bulk closure-replay regression rejects linear list membership.

title: Avoid replay-driven full device roster projection
description: Reviewed closure piles replay already-known device facts on every device-authored write. device.reconcile sees those replayed device_key offers and deletes/reinserts the full workspace device roster even though no canonical winner changed, making ordinary writes O(total devices).
acceptance_criteria: Materialize/reconcile only newly admitted facts unless canonical pruning/restoration requires a full reprojection; add a realistic device-authored ordinary-write regression proving the roster is not rebuilt; preserve winner-switch reprojection and pass the full suite.
close_reason: Device reconciliation now considers only newly admitted facts during ordinary turns and uses the full active set only for canonical reprojection; device-authored writes no longer rebuild the roster and winner-switch tests remain green.

title: Keep direct device grants deterministic across proof-winner changes
description: A direct grant that inherits its current canonical device provider's timestamp changes fid if an equal-valid provider later becomes canonical. A retry then misses the exact fact and fails as already enrolled, violating deterministic lost-response and reconcile retries.
acceptance_criteria: Derive the mandatory Fact timestamp from immutable workspace/logical-cell input without scanning for an existing logical grant; preserve the rule that timestamps carry no causal weight; add a restart retry and a canonical-provider-switch retry regression.
close_reason: Direct grants derive their required timestamp from the immutable workspace anchor, never a mutable proof winner or logical-cell scan; restart and provider-switch retry regressions pass.

title: Invalidate generation for direct index commit callers
description: Supported direct/bulk index builders can mutate and commit facts before Node.commit(). Because only merge() normally invalidates the root stamp, a pre-CAS Node.commit failure can leave their ahead index stamped as the old authoritative root across restart. Provide a shared mutation boundary or otherwise invalidate in the same direct mutation transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic direct/bulk builder mutation followed by a pre-CAS failure and restart rebuilds from the old manifest rather than retaining unpublished facts; ordinary bulk seed/benchmark paths remain green.
close_reason: Live merge and supported bulk builders now share commit_index(), which transactionally removes the root stamp; pre-CAS restart regression and all 5k benchmark guards pass.
